name: put behind
meanings: [{"name":"to stop worrying about or being upset by (something that happened in the past); If you put a bad experience or your own bad behavior behind you, you do not let it affect your life now","examples":["It was a disappointing loss, but we need to put it behind us and focus on winning the next game.","I should put jealousy behind me.","It's over. You need to put it behind you now, and make plans for the future.","I'm going to put all this behind me and think about the future."],"media":[]},{"name":" to place something in back of someone or something","examples":["I put the box behind Mary, and she didn't even know it was there.","Please put the present behind the couch where Janet will not see it."],"media":[]}]

name: put back
meanings: [{"name":"to return (something) to the place where it belongs","examples":["Remember to put the vacuum cleaner back in the closet after you've used it.","The books had been put back neatly on the shelf.","Will you put the books back when you've finished with them?","Put back the book when you finish."],"media":[]}]

name: put down as
meanings: [{"name":"to write down the name of someone or a group as something","examples":["I will put you down as cook for the benefit luncheon.","I put down John as a likely prospect."],"media":[]},{"name":"to think of (someone) as (a specified kind of person or thing); to judge that someone is bad or undesirable in some way","examples":["If you act silly all the time, people will put you down as a fool.","He was so rude that I put him down as someone to be avoided.","Most people put him down as a fanatic."],"media":[]}]

name: put down for
meanings: [{"name":"to write the name of (someone) on a list of people who will do or give (something); to put someone's name on a list of people who volunteer to do something or give an amount of money","examples":["Can I put you down for a donation?","Can I put you down for ten dollars? ","We're having a picnic, and you're invited. Everyone is bringing something. Can I put you down for potato salad?","Put me down for potato fry."],"media":[]}]

name: put a spin on something
meanings: [{"name":"to twist a report or story to one's advantage; to interpret an event to make it seem favorable or beneficial to oneself or one's cause","examples":["The mayor tried to put a positive spin on the damaging polls.","If you find out something that's really bad, just try to put a positive spin on it.","The pundit's spin on the new legislation was highly critical."],"media":[]}]

name: put in
meanings: [{"name":"to spend (time) especially at some occupation or job","examples":["I put in six hours at the office.","You put how much time in?","I put in four months on that project.","She's put in a lot of effort on this proposal."],"media":[]},{"name":"to apply for something; to make a request for something","examples":["I put in for a transfer, but I bet I don't get it.","She put in for a new file cabinet, but she never got one.","They've put in a bid to buy the company.","I've put in an application to the college."],"media":[]},{"name":"to include something, esp. in a piece of writing or a broadcast","examples":["We put an ad in the paper to sell our car.","Kids like this computer program because they can put in images that they create."],"media":[]},{"name":"to fix a machine, piece of equipment, or system in a place and make it ready to use","examples":["Choose the bathroom you want, and we will put it in for you within three days.","They're putting Paul's new stove in next week."],"media":[]},{"name":"to place or insert something inside someone or something","examples":["The surgeon put a tube inside Chuck and left it there to drain fluid.","While you have the closet door open, will you put this in?"],"media":[]}]

name: put in a good word
meanings: [{"name":"say something good about someone","examples":["Would you mind putting in a good word for me?","I hope you get the job. I'll put in a good word for you.","Yes, I want the job. If you see the boss, please put in a good word.","Jane: What are you doing here? Kate: I told you, I came to put in a good word for Mary.\nJane: She didn't need a good word."],"media":[]}]

name: put off by someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"distressed or repelled by someone or something","examples":["I was really put off by your behavior.","We were all put off by the unfairness of the rules."],"media":[]}]

name: put off someone
meanings: [{"name":"to delay dealing with someone until a later time","examples":["I hate to keep putting you off, but we are not ready to deal with you yet.","I had to put off the plumber again. He really wants his money."],"media":[]},{"name":"to repel someone; to distress someone; to make someone dislike something or someone, or to discourage someone from doing something","examples":["You really put people off with your scowling face. ","You put off people with your arrogance.","You have to work long hours and that puts off a lot of people.","The smell of pasta always puts me off."],"media":[]},{"name":"to avoid or evade someone","examples":["I don't wish to see Mr. Brown now. Please put him off.","I won't talk to reporters. Tell them something that will put them off. ","Put off those annoying people!"],"media":[]},{"name":"to remove someone from a form of transportation, such as a train, ship, or airplane, owing to illness or misbehavior","examples":["The captain ordered that the unruly passengers be put off the ship at the next port.","We put the thief off at the dock."],"media":[]}]

name: put off something
meanings: [{"name":"postpone something; schedule something for a later time; delay or postpone an action or event to a later time, often due to reluctance or an obstacle","examples":["I have to put off our meeting until a later time.","I put off a visit to the dentist as long as I could."],"media":[]},{"name":"discourage or make someone lose interest; cause dislike or disgust","examples":["The bad smell put me off eating there. (= The smell made me lose my appetite.)","The high price put me off buying it. (= The high price discouraged me from buying it.)"],"media":[]},{"name":"distract someone","examples":["Don't put me off while I'm speaking. (= Don't distract me.)","Please stop talking; you are putting me off my work."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase comes from the literal meanings of put (\"place\") and off (\"away from\" or \"at a distance\").","In Middle English and Early Modern English, put off often meant to move something away from oneself or remove it.","From the idea of moving something away came the figurative sense of pushing an event into the future → postpone.","Similarly, if something \"puts you off,\" it metaphorically pushes you away from an idea, activity, or object, leading to the meanings discourage or repel."]],["Easy trick to remember the phrase",["You can think of the core idea as: put off = push away","Push an event away in time → delay","Push a person away from an activity → discourage","Push food away → lose appetite","Push attention away → distract"]]]

name: put on
meanings: [{"name":"to pretend; to act as if something were true","examples":["Ann wasn't really angry. She was just putting on. ","I can't believe she was just putting on. She really looked mad.","I can't tell whether he's really upset or if he's just putting it on.","She's not really angry - it's just a put-on."],"media":[]},{"name":"to dress oneself in; don; to cover part of the body with clothes, shoes, make-up, or something similar; to clothe someone or an animal in something","examples":["Put your shoes on - we're going out.","He put on his jacket.","She puts face cream on every night."," The mother put a little jacket on her child. ","June put the lid on the pickle jar and put it in the fridge.","She put sand on Tom as he lay napping on the beach.","Please put the paper on the coffee table.","Sir, step out of the vehicle and put your hands on the car, please."],"media":[]},{"name":"to tease or deceive someone innocently and in fun; to joke with someone","examples":["Come on! You're just putting me on!","John: I hear Joe's quit his job. Mike: You're putting me on!"],"media":[]},{"name":"to add or increase an amount or action","examples":["I put on weight when I went away to college.","The school puts a lot of emphasis on music and art.","He's put on ten pounds in the last month."],"media":[]},{"name":"to make a device operate, or to cause a device to play something, such as a CD or DVD, by pressing a switch; apply","examples":["Could you put the light on?","Do you mind if I put the television/some music on?","Don't forget to put the brake on.","I put the radio on while I prepared the meal.","I put on the brakes too fast, and the car skidded."],"media":[]},{"name":"to do an activity, esp. one that others can watch; perform","examples":["The second graders want to put a play on.","The experience of putting on a campaign was exciting.","Let's just put on the best show we can."],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"to try to appear brave or calm","examples":["She tried to put on/up a brave face/front despite the pain of the injury.","She seems all right but I think she's just putting on a brave face."],"media":[]}]

name: put on an act
meanings: [{"name":"to behave or speak in a false or artificial way; to pretend that one is something other than what one is","examples":["Be yourself, Ann. name: put someone in his/her place
meanings: [{"name":"to rebuke someone; to remind one of one's (lower) rank or station; to say or do something to show someone that he or she is not better than other people and should not be acting in such a confident and proud way","examples":["He told her to stop talking, but she quickly put him in his place.","The boss put me in my place for criticizing her.","Then her boss put her in her place for being rude."],"media":[]}]

name: put one out of (one's) misery
meanings: [{"name":"Euph. Fig. to kill someone as an act of mercy.","examples":["Why doesn't the doctor simply put her out of her misery? ","He took pills to put himself out of his misery. name: put one's feet up
meanings: [{"name":"to sit and relax; to not work or be active; to sit down, lean back, and rest; to lie down","examples":["I'm going to go home and put my feet up.","He was really exhausted and had to go put his feet up.","Time to put up my feet and get some rest."],"media":[]}]

name: put one's hand up
meanings: [{"name":"to raise one's hand to get attention from whomever is in charge","examples":["The student put his hand up to ask a question of the teacher.","She put up her hand to ask a question.","Anyone who talked to the press, please raise your hand. Put your hand up, Jane."],"media":[]}]

name: put one's heart (and soul) into something
meanings: [{"name":"to do (something) in a wholehearted way; to put all of one's sincere efforts into something","examples":["She puts her heart into everything she does.","She put her heart and soul into the singing of the national anthem.","Come on, choir. You can sing better than that. Put your heart into it!"],"media":[]}]

name: put/get/set one's house in order
meanings: [{"name":"to put one's business or personal affairs into good order; to improve or correct the way one does things","examples":["We should put/get/set our (own) house in order before we criticize others for their mistakes.","The company needs to put its financial house in order.","There was some trouble in the department office and the manager was told to put his house in order.","Every now and then, I have to put my house in order. name: put/set one's mind to something
meanings: [{"name":"to give one's attention to (something) and try very hard to do it; to concentrate on doing something; to give the doing of something one's full attention","examples":["We can solve this problem if we put our minds to it.","I know I can do it if I put my mind to it.","I will set my mind to it and finish by noon.","I'm sure if you put your mind to it, you can come up with an even better lemon meringue pie than mine.\n"],"media":[]}]

name: put one's neck on the line
meanings: [{"name":"to put oneself at great risk; to do something that you know might fail and spoil other people's opinion of you or cause you to lose money","examples":["I put my neck on the line and recommended you for the job, and now look what you've done! I'm ruined!","I really put my neck on the line for this book, Jane. No one likes the idea. No one."],"media":[]}]

name: put one's thinking cap on
meanings: [{"name":"to start thinking in a serious manner; to start trying to think of what should be done","examples":["It's time to put our thinking caps on, children.","All right now, let's put on our thinking caps and do some arithmetic.","John: I'll think of it. name: put someone/something through his/her/its paces
meanings: [{"name":"to test what someone or something can do; to test the ability or skill of a person or thing","examples":["We brought home three different computers and put them through their paces.","I bet she really put you through your paces.","I like to put a new car through its paces.","All the candidates were put through their paces during the television debate."],"media":[]}]

name: put oneself in someone else's place/shoes/position
meanings: [{"name":"to allow oneself to see or experience something from someone else's point of view","examples":["Put yourself in someone else's place, and see how it feels.","I put myself in Tom's shoes and realized that I would have made exactly the same choice.","Put yourself in my place - what else could I have done?"],"media":[]}]

name: put out

name: drive out

name: drive through

name: start off

name: I'll bite
meanings:
[{"name":"Okay, I will answer your question.; Okay, I will listen to your joke or play your little guessing game;  used to indicate that someone is willing to engage with a topic, question, or story that has been introduced, often after a moment of hesitation or skepticism","examples":["Bob: Guess what is in this box. The phrase often suggests a degree of reluctance, as the speaker may believe they are being set up for a joke, are skeptical of the claim, or anticipate regret after hearing more.

You do the math.","It's as big a car as we can afford. You do the math!"],"media":[]}]

name: you don't know where it's been
meanings: [{"name":"It may be dirty, so do not touch it or put it in your mouth, because you do not know where it has been and what kind of dirt it has picked up.","examples":["Mother: Don't put that money in your mouth. You don't know where it's been. Bill: Okay.","Father: Take that stick out of your mouth. You don't know where it's been. Bob: It's been on the ground."],"media":[]}]
origin: Most often said to children.

name: you don't say
meanings: [{"name":"used to express surprise; often used ironically to show little surprise at something; used either to express surprise or lack of surprise in a humorous and slightly unkind way","examples":["Sally: The Jones boys are keeping a pet turtle. Alice: You don't say.","\"They lost again.\" \"You don't say. What's that, eight in a row?\"","Bob: He ran off with $10,000 of the company's money. Bill: You don't say!"],"media":[]}]

name: you wouldn't dare
meanings: [{"name":"an exclamation that shows disbelief about something that the speaker has threatened to do","examples":["Bill: I'm going to leave school. Tom: You wouldn't dare leave!","Bill: Be quiet or I'll slap you. Jane: You wouldn't dare!","Wife: I'm taking my baby and I'm getting on a plane to NewYork. Husband: You wouldn't dare!"],"media":[]}]

name: get the hang of
meanings: [{"name":"to learn the skills that are needed to do (something)","examples":["He was finally getting the hang of his job.","She's getting the hang of driving.","Mary: It's harder than I thought to glue these things together. Tom: You'll get the hang of it.","Bill: I can't seem to swing this club the way you showed me. Sally: You'll get the hang of it. Don't worry. Golf is easy."],"media":[]}]

name: secret is safe with me
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that someone will not tell anyone else a secret","examples":["Don't worry. I won't tell. Your secret's safe with me.","Your secret is safe with me. I will carry it to my grave.","Don't worry. Our secret is safe with her."],"media":[]}]

name: you're/he's/she's on
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one accepts a bet or challenge; Your/his/her bet, challenge, or invitation is accepted.","examples":["\"I bet I can run faster than you can.\" \"OK, you're on.\"","Q: What about 10 pizzas at the restaurant? A: You're on! ","Q: I think we can do it. Want to try? A: You're on!"],"media":[]}]

name: you're kidding (me)
meanings: [{"name":"used when someone says something surprising or that seems as if it could not be serious or true","examples":["\"He said he lost all the papers you gave him. \" \"You're kidding me.\""],"media":[]}]

name: out of one's mind
meanings: [{"name":"crazy or behaving in a crazy way; extremely stupid or mentally ill/unsound; unable to behave or deal with things normally because something has made you very worried, unhappy, or angry","examples":["You can't climb up there! Are you out of your mind?","I feel like I'm going out of my mind.","That noise is driving me out of my mind! [=that noise is bothering me very much]","I was out of my mind with worry. = I was going out of my mind with worry [=I was extremely worried]","I'd go out of my mind if I had to do her job all day!","You must be out of your mind paying £500 for one night in a hotel!","You have to be out of your mind to go swimming when it's below freezing outside."],"media":[]}]
origin: Said to someone who has said or done something silly or stupid.

name: you're telling me
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one already knows and completely agrees with something that was just said; I know all too well the truth of what you are saying","examples":["\"This hot weather is brutal.\" \"You're telling me.\"","Tom: Man, it's hot today! Bob: You're telling me! "," Jane: This food is really terrible. Sally: Wow! You're telling me!","\"Anita's in such a bad mood today.\" \"You're telling me!\""],"media":[]}]

name: too much
meanings: [{"name":"terrible, awful","examples":["Andrew: You're too much! I'm going to report you to the head office! Bob: Go ahead. See if I care.","Bob: Get out! Just go home! You're too much! Andrew: What did I do? Bob: You're a pest!"],"media":[]},{"name":"wonderful; exciting; funny; entertaining","examples":["That rock concert was too much!","Alice: Oh, Fred, that was really funny. You're too much! Fred: I do my best. ","Sally: What a clever thing to say! You're too much! Andrew: Actually, I didn't make it up myself."],"media":[]},{"name":"more than someone can deal with","examples":["I can't take care of six children at my age - it's too much.","You can't expect him to study in the evenings after a full day of work - it's too much.","One person can't manage all this work - it's too much.","If it's too much, just say so and we'll get someone in to help out."],"media":[]}]

name: not under any circumstances / under no circumstances
meanings: [{"name":"no matter what happens; never","examples":["Do not, under any circumstances, open that door.","Andrew: Under no circumstances will I ever go back there again! Rachel: Why? What happened?","Sue: Can I talk you into serving as a referee again? Mary: Heavens, no! Not under any circumstances!"],"media":[]}]

name: use one's head
meanings: [{"name":"to think carefully; used to tell someone in a slightly angry way to think more carefully about what they are doing","examples":["Maybe if we use our heads, we can figure this out.","Why didn't you use your head and cover the furniture before you started painting?","Tom: I just don't know what to do. Mary: Use your head! You'll figure out something.","Andrew: Come on, John, you can figure it out. A kindergartner could do it. Use your head! John: I'm doing my best."],"media":[]}]

name: I bet
meanings: [{"name":"I agree; said to indicate the listener's total agreement with a statement (Often sarcastic.)","examples":["\"She was so beautiful in her new dress.\" \"I bet she was.\"","\"I was so relieved I didn't have to clean up after the party.\" \"I bet you were.\"","Tom: They're probably going to raise taxes again next year. Henry: I bet.","Fred: If we do that again, we'll really be in trouble. Andrew: I'll bet."],"media":[]},{"name":"I'm pretty sure that something is so or that something will happen","examples":["Bob: You're late. I bet you miss your plane. Rachel: No, I won't.","Sue: I'll bet it rains today. Alice: No way! There's not a cloud in the sky. "],"media":[]}]

name: raised in a barn
meanings: [{"name":"brought up to behave like a barnyard animal; behaving crudely. (Folksy.)","examples":["Close the door behind you! Were you raised in a barn?","Don't wipe your nose on your sleeve. Were you raised in a barn?"],"media":[]}]

name: reach out to (someone)
meanings: [{"name":"to try to get the attention and interest of (someone); to make an effort to communicate with people","examples":["He's reaching out to young voters.","I reached out to my cousin, hoping to restore our former friendship.","Don: I reached out to Fred, since he is so shy. Hanna: I hope he felt comfortable with your proposition."],"media":[]},{"name":"to communicate with someone, especially by using a phone, sending them an email, etc.","examples":["The Washington Post reached out to Turner for comment.","Feel free to reach out if you have any questions about study abroad.","The Democrats have to reach out to these people to win this election."],"media":[]},{"name":"to offer help or support to (someone)","examples":["She set up her charity to reach out to the thousands of homeless on the streets.","It's been amazing to see how the community has reached out and helped.","Our community reaching out to the displaced families."],"media":[]}]

name: loud and clear
meanings: [{"name":"very clearly; in a way that is easily understood","examples":["\"Can you hear me now?\" \"Loud and clear.\"","The message from management came through loud and clear: things would have to change.","Tom: If I've told you once, I've told you a thousand times: Stop it! Do you hear me? Bill: Yes, loud and clear.","I hear you loud and clear."],"media":[]}]

name: remember/mind your manners
meanings: [{"name":"to behave in a polite and proper way; a comment intended to remind someone of proper behavior, such as saying Thank you or Excuse me. ","examples":["As long as you are staying here with me, you will behave properly. You will mind your manners, you will do your chores.","Bob: Here, Jane. Have one of these. Jane (taking one): Wow! Bob: Okay. Have another. Mother: What do you say? Remember your manners. Jane: Thanks a lot!","After Mary gave a cookie to little Bobby, Bobby's mother said to him, “Remember your manners.”"],"media":[]},{"name":" a parting instruction, usually to a child, encouraging proper behavior.","examples":["As Jimmy was going out the door, his mother said, “Have a good time and remember your manners.” ","John: It's time for me to go to the party, Mom. Mother: Yes, it is. Remember your manners. Good-bye."],"media":[]}]

name: right away / right now
meanings: [{"name":"immediately","examples":["John: Take this over to Sue. Bill: Right away. ","John: How soon can you do this? Sue: Right now.","I need someone to help me right away.","I'll get to it right away."],"media":[]}]

name: run it by someone
meanings: [{"name":"to tell something to someone; to present to someone(as for evaluation)","examples":["Alice: Do you understand? Sue: No. I really didn't understand what you said. Run it by me again, if you don't mind. ","John: Put this piece into the longer slot and the remaining piece into the slot on the bottom. Sue: Run it by again. I got lost just after put.","Mary: Keep to the right, past the fork in the road, then turn right at the crossroads. Do you follow? Jane: No. Run it by me again.","Any diamond ring we find, we'll run it by you.","They ran some ideas by her."],"media":[]}]

name: as hell
meanings: [{"name":"used to make a statement more forceful","examples":["\"Can you finish on schedule?\" \"We'll sure as hell try.\"","They were mad as hell.","We've been working as hard as hell to finish on schedule.","It's better for father, it's better for mother and it's sure as hell better for that baby.","Yeah, I'm proud as hell.","I'm sure as hell not going to say \"No.\""],"media":[]}]

name: sure thing
meanings: [{"name":"Yes.; Of course.; used to show agreement","examples":["Jane: Can I talk to you? Masha: Sure thing, Jane.","\"Could you give me a ride home tonight?\" \"Sure thing!\"","Jane: If you don't mind, will you make sure Sally and Celia do their chores? Masha: Sure thing."],"media":[]},{"name":"something that is certain to happen; something certain to win or succeed","examples":["The president's re-election is now far from a sure thing.","Your promotion is a sure thing – you're the best person for the job."],"media":[]}]

name: same here
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one thinks, feels, or wants the same thing as someone else; Me, too.; I hold the same opinion.; I choose the same thing.","examples":["\"I'm tired.\" \"Same here.\"","\"I'll have a coffee.\" \"Same here, please.\"","A: I'll have a slice of pie and coffee. B: Same here.","\"I never really liked him.\" \"Same here.\""],"media":[]}]

name: Save it!
meanings: [{"name":"Stop talking!; Shut up!","examples":["I've heard enough. Save it!","Save it! You talk too much!"],"media":[]}]

name: say no (to)
meanings: [{"name":"to say that one will not accept or agree to something","examples":["We requested more time, but she said no.","She said no to our request.","I never say no to dessert."],"media":[]}]

name: say no more
meanings: [{"name":"used to tell someone that it is not necessary to explain something further because one understands what that person is trying to say; I agree.; I will do it.; I concede, no need to continue talking.","examples":["\"A word of advice: don't mention the war.\" \"Say no more—I'll stay off the subject!\"","Kid: That apple pie just made my mouth water. Mother: Well, say no more. One slice coming right up.","Jane: Of course, we don't have to add salt to the wound. Masha: Say no more. I'll get out of your hair.","John: Someone ought to take this stuff outside. Bill: Say no more. Consider it done.","Mary: Shouldn't we turn here if we plan to visit Jane? Alice: Say no more. Here we go."],"media":[]}]

name: out of one's hair
meanings: [{"name":"out of one's way; not in one's hair; stop annoying someone","examples":["Please keep the children out of his hair for a while.","Oh, gosh. I can't get this out of my hair.","Well, I'll just finish up with the sink and be out of your hair.","Why not just let me take my trust fund, and I'll get out of your hair forever?","Will you get out of my hair! You are a real pain!"],"media":[]}]

name: in someone's hair / in one's hair
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. tangled in someone's hair","examples":["My bubble gum got in my hair and I had to cut it out."],"media":[]},{"name":"annoying someone; to annoy someone, usually by being present all the time","examples":["The children have been getting in my hair all afternoon.","I don't want to be in your hair.","You can watch what I am doing, but don't get in my hair. ","I wish you wouldn't get in my hair when I'm trying to do something."],"media":[]}]

name: say what?
meanings: [{"name":"used to express surprise at what someone has just said; What did you say?; Please repeat what you said.","examples":["\"I'm moving out.\" \"Say what?\"","Sally: Would you like some more salad? Fred: Say what? Sally: Salad? Would you like some more salad?","John: Put this one over there. Sue: Say what? John: Never mind, I'll do it."],"media":[]}]

name: set/put someone straight
meanings: [{"name":"to correct someone who is mistaken by providing accurate information; to tell someone the true facts about a situation that the person had not understood (Often said in anger or domination.)","examples":["He set/put her straight about/on what happened.","I had to set him straight about what really happened.","The article about the trial really set the record straight.","I set her straight about who she had to ask for permission to leave early."],"media":[]}]

name: set/put something straight
meanings: [{"name":"to put everything in its proper place in (something) : to organize (something)","examples":["After supper, the kids helped set/put the kitchen straight."],"media":[]}]

name: set/put the record straight
meanings: [{"name":"to correct a false story; to provide the facts about something that people have a false understanding or idea about","examples":["Let me set the record straight about what really happened last week.","To put the record straight, I do not support that idea and never have.","The media initially reported that the escaped animal was a tiger, but zoo officials set the record straight, announcing that it was a harmless kangaroo.","The manager thought Jean was to blame, but she soon set the record straight.","Jane's mother heard that Tom is a married man, but he set the record straight. He's divorced."],"media":[]}]

name: Shake it (up)!
meanings: [{"name":"Hurry up!; Move faster!; Run faster!","examples":["Fred: Move it, Tom! Shake it up! Tom: I can't go any faster!","Jane: Move, you guys. Shake it! Bill: Hey, I'm doing the best I can!"],"media":[]}]

name: shame on someone
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that someone should feel sorry for doing something wrong","examples":["Shame on you for being so rude.","John: I think I broke one of your figurines. Mary: Shame on you! John: I'll replace it, of course. Mary: Thanks, I sort of liked it.","“Shame on you!” said Mary. “You should have known better!”"],"media":[]}]

name: since when
meanings: [{"name":"used to show that one is surprised and often angry, annoyed, or doubtful about what someone has said or done","examples":["\"I'm a vegetarian.\" \"Since when?\"","\"You told me to do it.\" \"Since when did you start listening to me?\"","Since when is it okay to cheat?"],"media":[]}]

name: skip it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one does not want to do something, talk about something, etc.; Never mind!; Forget it!","examples":["I meant to … oh, skip it. It's not important anyway.","John: I need some help on this project. Mary: You've got to be kidding! John: Oh, skip it! ","Jane: Will you be able to do this, or should I get someone with more experience? Bob: What did you say? Jane: Oh, skip it!"],"media":[]}]

name: slow going
meanings: [{"name":"a situation in which progress is slow; the rate of speed when one is making little progress","examples":["It's been slow going so far, but the project should speed up soon.","It was slow going at first, but I was able to finish the project by the weekend.","Getting the heavy rocks out of the field is slow going."],"media":[]}]

name: so be it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one is resigned to the fact that one can do nothing to change something; it is necessary to accept the situation as it exists; That is the way it shall be.; It shall be as just described","examples":["If they insist on going, so be it.","If she spends all her money on clothes, so be it!","If that means we can't be friends at work, so be it.","I want a new stove, Bob, and if I need to get a job to pay for it, so be it.","I want to better myself through higher education. If it makes Andy angry, so be it. "],"media":[]}]

name: so do I
meanings: [{"name":"used to express that one feels the same way; I do too","examples":["Mary: I want some more cake. Sally: So do I.","Bob: I have to go home now. Tom: So do I. Bob: Bye.","\"I wish I had a coffee right now.\" \"So do I.\""],"media":[]}]

name: so much for something
meanings: [{"name":"We will not be dealing with that anymore; used to say that everything that can be said about or done with something or someone has been said or done","examples":["Well, so much for that idea. We'll have to look for a better solution."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that something has ended; that is the end of","examples":["Well, it's raining. So much for our perfect weather.","\"It's raining.\" \"So much for our day at the beach.\"","Mother: Here, try some carrots. Child (brushing the spoon aside): No! No! Mother: Well, so much for that.","John tossed the stub of a pencil into the trash. “So much for that,” he muttered, fishing through his drawer for another."],"media":[]}]

name: so much the better / all the better
meanings: [{"name":"That is even better (than expected or desired); used to say that something makes a situation, experience, etc., even better than it was","examples":["My daughter loves taking care of children. If she can earn money by doing it, so much the better!","And if the recipe produces a gorgeous, show-stopping dessert, all the better.","Tom, if you decide to leave now and pick up Jean at the airport, so much the better.","A: She finally agreed to use the old ones rather than replace them. B: So much the better. The new ones are really cheaply made.","If you can go there this afternoon, so much the better."],"media":[]}]

name: so soon
meanings: [{"name":"early; before the regular time; ahead of schedule","examples":["I got there early because my bus arrived so soon. ","Because the meeting ended so soon, I had some extra time.","Why are you back so soon?","Stay here. Don't go so soon to London. Just one more day."],"media":[]}]

name: so to speak
meanings: [{"name":"this is one way to say it; used to indicate that one is using words in an unusual or figurative way rather than a literal way; as one might say; said a certain way, even though the words are not exactly accurate","examples":["In that house it's very much Jane who wears the trousers, so to speak (= Jane makes all the important decisions).\n","We need to be all on the same wavelength, so to speak."," I am a writer, so to speak.","John helps me with my taxes. He's my accountant, so to speak.","I just love my little poodle. She's my baby, so to speak."],"media":[]}]

name: in a manner of speaking
meanings: [{"name":"if you think about it in a particular way; true in some but not all ways; in some ways, though not exactly","examples":["His retirement was, in a manner of speaking, the beginning of his real career.","After the storm destroyed their house, they were, in a manner of speaking, lost at sea.","His old self died, in a manner of speaking, and he was born again as a devout Hindu."],"media":[]}]

name: (So )what else is new?
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one is not surprised by something one has been told; This isn't new. It has happened before.","examples":["\"They lost again.\" \"So what else is new?\"","Mary: Taxes are going up again. Bob: So what else is new?","John: Gee, my pants are getting tight. Maybe I'm putting on a little weight. Sally: What else is new?"],"media":[]}]

name: with you in a second/minute/moment
meanings: [{"name":"Please be patient, someone will help you very soon.","examples":["Sue: Oh, Miss? Clerk: Someone will be with you in a minute.","Bill: Please wait here. I'll be with you in a minute. Bob: Please hurry.","Have a seat. I'll be with you in a second.","Kid: Mommy, I can't find my ball. Mom: Charlie, I'll be with you in a second, okay?"],"media":[]}]

name: hold/hang on a moment
meanings: [{"name":"used to tell someone to wait or to stop for a brief time","examples":["\"Aren't you finished yet?\" \"Hold on a moment. I'm almost done.\"","Hang on a moment—I don't understand.","Hang on a moment—I didn't hear you. Could you repeat what you said?"],"media":[]}]

name: hold/hang on a minute
meanings: [{"name":"used to tell someone to wait or to stop for a brief time","examples":["\"Aren't you finished yet?\" \"Hold on a minute. I'm almost done.\"","Hang on a minute—I didn't hear you. Could you repeat what you said?","Uh, hold on a minute. I need to hop on another call.\n"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to express surprise or disbelief","examples":["Hold on a minute! That's not what you said yesterday!"],"media":[]}]

name: something has got to give / something has to give
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that someone or something has to stop trying to resist or oppose something; Emotions or tempers are strained, and there is going to be an outburst","examples":["Alice: There are serious problems with Mary and Tom. They fight and fight. Sue: Yes, something's got to give. It can't go on like this.","Bill: Things are getting difficult at the office. Something's got to give. Mary: Just stay clear of all the bickering.","For the strike to be settled, something has (got) to give!"],"media":[]}]

name: sooner than you think
meanings: [{"name":"sooner rather than later","examples":["Sally: I'm going to have to stop pretty soon for a rest. Mary: Sooner than you think, I'd say. I think one of our tires is low.","Tom: The stock market is bound to run out of steam pretty soon. Bob: Sooner than you think from the look of today's news.","When he is tired of being alone, he will meet somebody. Maybe sooner than you think."],"media":[]}]

name: no sooner than
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that something happens immediately after something else; a second thing happens immediately after the first","examples":["No sooner had I spoken than he appeared.","No sooner did I walk through the door than the phone rang.","No sooner had I started mowing the lawn than it started raining."],"media":[]}]

name: Sorry I asked
meanings: [{"name":"Now that I have heard the answer, I regret asking the question.","examples":["Alice: Can we get a new car soon? The old one is a wreck. John: Are you kidding? There's no way that we could ever afford a new car! Alice: Sorry I asked.","After he heard the long list of all the reasons he wouldn't be allowed to go to the concert, Fred just shrugged and said, “Sorry that I asked.”"],"media":[]}]

name: afraid/sorry to say
meanings: [{"name":"used as a way of expressing one's disappointment, regret, or sorrow; used to show that something that must be said causes sadness or disappointment","examples":["Most of us worked very hard, but she, I'm afraid to say, did no work at all.","I'm sorry to say that the project's funding has been cancelled.","Well, I'm sorry to say that you're mistaken.","I'm sorry to say there's been an incident."],"media":[]}]

name: speak up / speak out
meanings: [{"name":"to speak loudly and distinctly; Please speak more loudly.; Do not be shy—speak more loudly.","examples":["“Speak up. I can hardly hear you,” said Uncle Henry, cupping his hand to his ear.","Sorry, you're gonna have to speak up a little bit louder. I'm hard of hearing.","Could you speak up? We can't hear at the back.","You'll have to speak up a bit if you want everyone to hear you.","Stop muttering and speak up!"],"media":[]},{"name":"to express an opinion freely","examples":["speak up for truth and justice.","If you disagree, please speak up.","He spoke out against the school's admissions policy.","It was nice to hear a politician speak out about the problems facing farmers today."],"media":[]}]

name: quality time
meanings: [{"name":"time spent giving all of one's attention to someone who is close (such as one's child)","examples":["Dad and I spent some quality time together.","You can spend more quality time|with your real friends."],"media":[]}]

name: stand up for
meanings: [{"name":"to defend against attack or criticism; to defend or support someone or something; to defend or support a particular idea or a person who is being criticized or attacked","examples":["Don't be bullied, learn to stand up for yourself and what you believe in.","You have to stand up for your rights - you can't let them walk all over you.","He's a big boy - I'm sure he can stand up for himself.","Well, stand up for yourself. Don't let him get away with that."],"media":[]}]

name: stay with me
meanings: [{"name":"Follow along with what I am explaining.; Pay attention.","examples":["This explanation is going to be quite complicated, so stay with me, and ask lots of questions.","I know it's late, and you're all tired, but stay with me until I cover this last graph."],"media":[]}]

name: stay with someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to remain in the company of someone or something","examples":["Please stay with me for a little while. ","How long did you stay with the company?"],"media":[]}]

name: stick by
meanings: [{"name":"to continue to support or be loyal to (someone or something)","examples":["The troops stuck by their general to the end.","I promised to support you and I'll stick by my promise.","She's the only person in this neighborhood who's stuck by you.","You stuck by him during the health problems."],"media":[]}]

name: the usual suspects
meanings: [{"name":"the usual people or things that are suspected or thought of in a particular situation (often used humorously)","examples":["The breakfast menu had all the usual suspects—eggs, pancakes, waffles, and French toast.","His heart attack was caused by the usual suspects: poor diet, stress, and smoking."],"media":[]}]

name: stick with
meanings: [{"name":"to continue using or doing (something)","examples":["You need to find a job and stick with it.","I'll stick with my usual brand."],"media":[]},{"name":"to not change (a decision, belief, etc.)","examples":["The company is sticking with its decision to close the store."],"media":[]},{"name":"to force (someone) to deal with (something or someone unpleasant) - often used as (be/get) stuck with","examples":["Whenever we go out to eat, they always stick me with the bill.","The teacher always sticks me with Tom.","I was stuck with washing dishes.","I got stuck with Tom again."],"media":[]},{"name":"to stay close to (someone) in a race or competition","examples":["The challenger stuck with the champion until the very last round."],"media":[]},{"name":"to stay near (someone) in order to gain knowledge, protection, etc.","examples":["Stick with me, kid, and you'll learn something!","Stick with me, and we'll do lots of interesting things."],"media":[]},{"name":"to be remembered by someone for a very long time","examples":["The lessons she learned from that experience stuck with her."],"media":[]}]

name: take it or leave it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one will not make a better offer than the offer one has made; There is no choice.; Take this one or none.","examples":["I'll give you $500 for the camera, but that's my final offer. Take it or leave it.","Bill: That's my final offer. Take it or leave it. Bob: Aw, come on! Take off a few bucks.","Bill: Aw, I want eggs for breakfast, Mom. Mother: There's only Sweet Wheets left. Take it or leave it."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that one does not care about or is not excited about something","examples":["\"Do you like lobster?\" \"I can take it or leave it.\""],"media":[]}]

name: at face value
meanings: [{"name":"for the price that is printed on something","examples":["We bought the tickets at face value.","We paid $100 for tickets that had a face value of $50."],"media":[]},{"name":"as true or genuine without being questioned or doubted; to accept someone or something based on outward appearance","examples":["After all his lying, nothing he says now should be taken/accepted at face value.","Don't just take her offer at face value. Think of the implications.","Jane tends to take people at face value, and so she is always getting hurt."],"media":[]}]

name: take it personally
meanings: [{"name":"to be offended or upset by what someone said","examples":["He says unkind things to everyone. Try not to take it personally.","Don't take this personally","She takes criticism very personally."],"media":[]}]

name: Tell me this isn't happening
meanings: [{"name":"I can't believe that this is happening.; Assure me that what seems to be happening isn't really happening.","examples":["Ye gods! That man just stole my purse! This isn't happening!","My arm is bleeding, and I think my wrist is broken. I think I'm going to pass out. Tell me this isn't happening!"],"media":[]}]

name: thank God / thank goodness / thank heaven
meanings: [{"name":"used to express happiness or relief that something did or did not happen","examples":["Thank goodness it turned out to be a false alarm.","John: Well, we finally got here. Sorry we're so late. Mother: Thank goodness! We were all so worried."," Jane: There was a fire on Maple Street, but no one was hurt. Bill: Thank God!"],"media":[]}]

name: that/it (all) depends
meanings: [{"name":"used in speech to say that the answer to a question will be different in different situations","examples":["\"Do you think you'll go back to college?\" \"It all depends. I will if I can afford it.\"","\"Which team do you think will win?\" \"That depends. If all of our players are healthy, I think we'll win.\"","\"How long does it take to get to the airport?\" \"Depends. If you're going during rush hour it'll take at least an hour.\"","Tom: Will you be able to come to the meeting on Thursday night? Mary: That all depends.","Bob: Can I see you again? Sally: That depends."],"media":[]}]

name: that does it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one has finished doing something; That completes it!; It is now done just right! ","examples":["I just need to sign one more letter. There, that does it.","When Jane got the last piece put into the puzzle, she said, “That does it!”"],"media":[]},{"name":"used in angry speech to say that one will not accept or allow something anymore; That's the last straw!; Enough is enough!","examples":["\"They say we'll have to wait another hour.\" \"That does it! We're leaving right now!\"","Bill: We're still not totally pleased with your work. Bob: That does it! I quit! "],"media":[]}]

name: that's all / that is all
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that something is finished, completed, or enough","examples":["\"Do you need anything else?\" \"No, thanks, that's all.\"","They're (just) different, that's all.","That is all for today. Fall out.","We fell asleep. That is all."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that something is all that is needed or wanted","examples":["I went there to visit friends and that's all.","Bob: Okay, ladies, I have 15 minutes, and they are all yours.\nKate: That is all we need."],"media":[]}]

name: that's the spirit
meanings: [{"name":"used to approve or encourage someone's positive attitude (= way of thinking) or action","examples":["\"I know I can do it if I keep trying.\" \"Yeah, that's the spirit!\"","\"Come on, we can win this game.\" \"That's the spirit.\"","\"Bad weather won't put me off.\" \"That's the spirit!\"","\"Obstacles are there to be overcome.\" \"That's the spirit.\"","We haven't come this far to give up now!\" \"That's the spirit!\""],"media":[]}]

name: that's not to say
meanings: [{"name":"that does not mean","examples":["It's odd, but that's not to say that it's bad.","However, that's not to say other growers haven't been catching up as well.","Actually, the color of your passport follows no strict system of country categorization — though that's not to say the color each country chooses is totally random, either.","Of course, that's not to say all riddles for kids are a serious learning experience—some are just plain goofy and fun."],"media":[]}]

name: that's more like it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that something is better or more pleasing; more accurate or true; That is a better response than the previous one.","examples":["\"I've done twice as much today as yesterday!\" \"Well, that's more like it! Congratulations!\"","It was a long and tiring day, but as the waiter brought me my dinner, I thought to myself, \"Well, this is more like it.\"","Waiter: Here is your order, sir. Roast chicken as you requested. Sorry about the mix-up. John: That's more like it.","Kid: I've finished my vegetables, Father. I shall now excuse myself to go tidy the kitchen.\nFather: Well. That's more like it."],"media":[]}]

name: neither here nor there
meanings: [{"name":"irrelevant; not important, or not connected with the subject being discussed","examples":["Her age is neither here nor there – the real question is, can she do the job?","Comfort is neither here nor there to a real sailor.","Waiter: But it's raining, and everyone will come in with umbrellas and wet coats. Chef: That's neither here nor there. If we don't have the food prepared on time, we'll be fired whether the customers are wet or dry.","A: Fred can bring games for the children, and Mary can bring party hats. B: That's neither here nor there—since the party has been cancelled."],"media":[]}]

name: that's that
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that a decision or situation cannot be changed; an expression that shows that something has ended; That is the end of that! Nothing more can be done; That is final and nothing more needs to be said or done","examples":["I won't sell it for less than 50 dollars and that is that.","I'm not going and that's that.","I won't agree to it and that's that (= I won't discuss it any longer).","I refuse to go with you and that's that!"],"media":[]}]

name: that's the stuff
meanings: [{"name":"That is the right attitude or action","examples":["Bob: I'm sure I can do it! Fred: That's the stuff!","“That's the stuff!” cried the coach as Mary crossed the finish line."],"media":[]}]

name: that's the ticket / just the ticket / the ticket
meanings: [{"name":"the correct or most desirable thing; just the perfect thing; the thing that is needed or wanted; That is what is required!","examples":["Compromise, now that's the ticket.","Perhaps a pilgrimage to one of your heritage places is the ticket?","Keeping a filling, nutritious snack on you can be the ticket to preventing a meltdown.","Mary: I'll just get ready and drive the letter directly to the airport! Sue: That's the ticket. Take it right to the airport post office.","This soup is just the ticket for a quick lunch.","A good, hot cup of coffee will be just the ticket."],"media":[]}]

name: that's the way it goes / that's the way life goes
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that it is a fact that bad or disappointing things will happen sometimes; That is fate.","examples":["We lost the game, but that's the way it/life goes.","Mary: All my roses died in the cold weather. Sue: That's the way it goes.","Sally: Someone stole all the candy we left out in the front office. Jane: That's the way it goes."],"media":[]}]

name: (that's the) way to go
meanings: [{"name":"used to tell someone that he or she has done something well; a phrase encouraging someone to continue the good work","examples":["Nice job, guys! Way to go!","As John ran over the finish line, everyone cried, “That's the way to go!”","“Way to go!” said Mary when Bob finally got the car started.","I just think it's the way to go."],"media":[]}]

name: that's why!
meanings: [{"name":"a tag on the end of a statement that is an answer to a question beginning with why. (Shows a little impatience.)","examples":["Mary: Why do you eat that awful peppermint candy? Tom: Because I like it, that's why!","I'm not impressed. Because you're freaking me out, that's why!"],"media":[]}]

name: every hour on the hour
meanings: [{"name":"at the beginning of each hour (at 12:00, 1:00, 2:00, etc.)","examples":["Trains leave the station every hour on the hour.","Water shows are scheduled for every hour on the hour.","Visitors to Athens can watch the changing of the guard in front of the Parliament building at Syntagma Square every hour on the hour."],"media":[]}]

name: there aren't enough hours in the day
meanings: [{"name":"There are too many things to do and not enough time","examples":["I am behind in all my work. There aren't enough hours in the day! ","We can't handle all the problems that come our way. There aren't enough hours in the day."],"media":[]}]

name: there is no such thing as a free lunch
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that it is not possible to get something that is desired or valuable without having to pay for it in some way; Nothing is really free because there is always some obligation","examples":["I ended up paying even more when they added on tax and carrying charges. There's no such thing as a free lunch.","Why won't my insurance pay for my cousin's operation also? A: No such thing as a free lunch."],"media":[]}]

name: there's no time like the present
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that the best time to do something is right now; Do it now.; Don't put it off.","examples":["\"Should we do it now?\" \"Sure. There's no time like the present.\"","A: I think I will try to find a lawyer in a few weeks to help me with my will. B: Do it now. There's no time like the present.","Don't wait another moment. You need a new bicycle while you're still young. There's no time like the present."],"media":[]}]

name: (there's) nothing to it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that something is very easy to do; It's easy!","examples":["There's really nothing to it once you know how.","Learning the game is easy - there's nothing to it.","John: Is it hard to learn to fly a small plane? Sue: There's nothing to it!","Bill: Me? I can't dive off a board that high! I can hardly dive off the side of the pool! Bob: Aw, come on! Nothing to it!"],"media":[]}]

name: nothing to
meanings: [{"name":"no truth to (something)","examples":["There's nothing to the story/claim."],"media":[]},{"name":"of no interest, value, or importance to (someone)","examples":["Money is nothing to them.","He's nothing to me now."],"media":[]}]

name: this is it
meanings: [{"name":"This is the time, place, or thing that we have been looking or waiting for.; I have discovered the right thing!; This is the one! ","examples":["This is it. This is the chance you've been waiting for! ","This is it. This is my stop. I have to get off the bus.","“This is it!” shouted the scientist, holding a test tube in the air.","Sue: This is it! This is the book that has all the shrimp recipes. Mary: I never saw anybody get so happy about shrimp!"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that a very important thing is about to be done, a very important event is about to happen, etc.","examples":["This is it, men. Let's take home the championship!","As the car skidded out of control, I thought, \"This is it. I'm going to die.\""],"media":[]}]

name: more like
meanings: [{"name":"close to; about, approximately","examples":["I thought it would only take two or three minutes, but it ended up taking more like half an hour.","You look more like your mother every day."],"media":[]}]

name: those were the days
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that a period of time in the past was pleasant and often better than the present time; The days we have been referring to were the greatest of times","examples":["A: Ah, yes. The eighties. B: Those were the days!","Those were the days. Back when people knew right from wrong.","When I was a kid, we spent our summers at the beach. Those were the days!"],"media":[]}]

name: through no fault of someone's own
meanings: [{"name":"not because of someone's fault","examples":["We ended up missing the entire ceremony through no fault of our own.","Through no fault of his own, he failed third grade. His eyes were bad, and nobody caught it. "],"media":[]},{"name":"not because of someone's skill, luck, or planning; in spite of all the bad things that happened. (Irony. Here fault = skill, effort, planning.)","examples":["We got to the ceremony right on time—through no fault of our own.","Through no fault of our own, we managed to amass a small fortune by the time we were each forty years old."],"media":[]}]

name: times have changed
meanings: [{"name":"the situation is different now from the way it was in the past","examples":["Times have changed and many more women now have executive jobs than in the past."],"media":[]}]

name: to hell with someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"used to say in a forceful and angry way that one does not care about someone or something","examples":["They want me to stop, but to hell with them! I'll do what I want to do!","I was ready to say to hell with it and leave."],"media":[]}]

name: too good to be true
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that something cannot be as good as it seems to be; so good in a way that is difficult to believe; almost unbelievable","examples":["The price of the car is too good to be true. There must be something wrong with it.","Her new job sounds too good to be true.","I'm not surprised the offer wasn't genuine, it sounded too good to be true.","The news was too good to be true.","When I finally got a big raise, it was too good to be true."],"media":[]}]

name: too little, too late
meanings: [{"name":"not enough and not soon enough to make a difference; not enough of something that should have been provided earlier:","examples":["Her efforts to improve her grade were too little, too late.","A spokeswoman described the aid for the refugees as too little, too late.","Andy: Your help with the picnic was appreciated, but it was too little, too late. By the time we got there, it was raining. Helen: Sorry. ","It was a great speech, but the damage had already been done. It was just too little, too late."],"media":[]}]

name: over there / way over there
meanings: [{"name":"in a place some distance away","examples":["I see a house way over there in the field.","My hat is over there on the table.","I'm not schlepping way over there.","The coast is all the way over there."],"media":[]}]

name: What a shame/pity!
meanings: [{"name":"an expression of consolation meaning That's too bad. (Can also be used sarcastically.) ","examples":["Bill: I'm sorry to tell you that the cat died today. Mary: What a pity!","Mary: The cake is ruined! Sally: What a shame!"],"media":[]}]

name: so what?
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that something should not be considered objectionable; used to mean \"it's not important\" and \"I don't care\"","examples":["So what if he wears a necktie with a plaid shirt?\n","\"Andrew won't like it, you know.\" \"So what? - I don't care what Andrew thinks!\"","\"We are not supposed to be here.\" \"So what?\""],"media":[]}]

name: what about it?
meanings: [{"name":"So what?; Do you want to argue about it? (Contentious.); used to rudely say that you do not think something is important","examples":["\"Excuse me, I think your car is blocking my driveway?\" \"What about it?\"","Bill: I heard you were the one accused of breaking the window. Tom: Yeah? So, what about it?","Mary: Your piece of cake is bigger than mine. Sue: What about it?"],"media":[]}]

name: what about
meanings: [{"name":"does that include (someone); how about (someone)","examples":["\"We're all going to the beach.\" \"What about Kate?\""],"media":[]},{"name":"how does that affect (someone or something); what should be done about (someone or something)","examples":["\"I need to leave—something has come up.\" \"What about the meeting?\" \"We'll have to reschedule it.\"","What about the people who can't afford health insurance?"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to make a suggestion about what could be done","examples":["We'll need to talk about this again. What about (meeting) next week?","There's still time. What about playing another game?"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to ask someone to tell one something in response to the thing that one has just said","examples":["I like skiing and hiking. What about you? What sports do you like?","Everyone else is coming. What about you?"],"media":[]}]

name: What brings you here?
meanings: [{"name":"What is your reason for being here?","examples":["Tom: Hello, Mary. What brings you here? Mary: I was invited, just like you.","Doctor: Well, John, what brings you here? John: I've had this cough for nearly a month, and I think it needs looking into."],"media":[]}]

name: what are you trying to prove
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask why someone is behaving in a way that seems unreasonable","examples":["What are you trying to prove by behaving so recklessly?\n"],"media":[]}]

name: What can I say?
meanings: [{"name":"I have no explanation or excuse. What do you expect me to say?","examples":["Bill: Why on earth did you lose that big order? Sally: What can I say? I'm sorry! ","Bob: You're going to have to act more aggressively if you want to make sales. You're just too timid. Tom: What can I say? I am what I am."],"media":[]}]

name: what did I tell you
meanings: [{"name":"used to say to someone that he or she should have listened and followed one's advice","examples":["\"The car turned out to be a lemon!\" \"What did I tell you?\"","What did I tell you about asking too many questions?","What did I tell you about being rude to customers?  Stick a smile on your face.","What did I tell you about puttin' away those clothes? I'm serious."],"media":[]}]

name: what does it matter
meanings: [{"name":"used to state that something does not matter","examples":["What does it matter if she arrives a bit late?","What does it matter what I'm wearing?","This is so silly. what does it matter who says it first?"],"media":[]}]

name: What do you think?
meanings: [{"name":"What is your opinion?","examples":["Mary: This is our new company stationery. What do you think? Bill: Stunning. Simply stunning.","Mary: We're considering moving out into the country. What do you think? Sue: Sounds good to me."],"media":[]}]

name: What do you think you are doing here?
meanings: [{"name":"Why are you in this place? (Stern and threatening.) ","examples":["John: Mary! Mary: John! John: What do you think you're doing here?","“What do you think you're doing here?” said Fred to a frightened rabbit trapped in the garage."],"media":[]}]

name: What do you want me to say?
meanings: [{"name":"I have no response.; I have no answer. Do you have one for me to say? (Almost the same as What can I say?; What can I tell you?) ","examples":["Tom: You've really made a mess of all of this! Bill: Sorry. What do you want me to say?","Bob: All of these problems should have been settled some time ago. Why are they still plaguing us? Tom: What do you want me to say?"],"media":[]}]

name: what for
meanings: [{"name":"why; for what purpose or reason; usually used with the other words of a question between what and for","examples":["A: I want you to clean your room. B: What for? It's clean enough.","A: You need to leave now. B: What for? Did I do something wrong?","Jane: What do you need the money for?\nKate: It's for Betty.","Kate: What are you apologizing for?\nBob: You didn't punish me.","What exactly are you here for?","Well, what are we waiting for? Call him."],"media":[]}]
origin:
What for? - is the standard, informal phrase used to ask for the purpose, reason, or motivation behind an action, functioning as a direct synonym for "Why?"
For what? - In casual speech, it can sometimes carry a confrontational tone, implying disagreement or questioning the validity of a request. Sometimes, it can be used in more dramatic tone.

name: what gives?
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask the reason for something; What happened?; What went wrong?; What's the problem?","examples":["You've been acting weird all week. What gives?","So what'd you dig up on Mr. Dave? It's been two days. What gives?","Jane: The Police says you were spotted coming out of the storage room right before the fire started. What gives?\nJohn: I don't know what they're talking about. I have an alibi.","Bill: Hi, you guys. What gives? Bob: Nothing, just a little misunderstanding. Tom's a little angry."],"media":[]}]

name: what goes around comes around
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that if someone treats other people badly he or she will eventually be treated badly by someone else","examples":["You should not mistreat them. What goes around comes around.","Always stay humble and what goes around comes around.","Now he is the victim of his own policies. Whatever goes around comes around.","I believe that what goes around comes around and that one day he will pay for the misery he has caused.","In movies as in life, what goes around comes around."],"media":[]}]

name: what good / what good does it do / what good would that do / what good would that be
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one does not think that something is helpful, useful, or worth doing; a way of asking what the purpose of (doing) something ","examples":["What good is a college education when you can't get a job after you graduate?","What good does it do to bring an umbrella along if you are only going to leave it in the car?","I could try talking to him, but what good would that do/be? He has already made up his mind.","What good is sitting alone in your room?","What good is money that doesn't spend?"],"media":[]}]

name: What (have) you been up to?
meanings: [{"name":"a greeting inquiry. (A detailed answer may be expected.) ","examples":["Mary: Hello, Jane. What have you been up to? Jane: Been up to no good. What about you? Mary: Yeah. Me, too.","John: Bill, baby! What you been up to? Bill: Nothing really. What about you? John: The same, I guess."],"media":[]}]

name: what someone's having
meanings: [{"name":"I would like to have the same as someone ordered. (A response to a waiter) ","examples":["Bob: I think I'd like a cup of coffee with cream. Waiter: And you, sir? Tom: What he's having. ","Q: Can I get you something to drink? A: A lemonade would be nice. No. I changed my mind. What he's having.","Bob: I'll just have what she's having. Waiter: I'm sorry, sir. That was our last piece."],"media":[]}]

name: what if I do?
meanings: [{"name":"Does it matter to you if I do it?; What difference does it make if I do it? (colloquial.)","examples":["Tom: Are you really going to sell your leather coat? Bob: What if I do?","Jane: You're not going to go out dressed like that, are you? Sue: So, what if I do?"],"media":[]}]

name: What is it?
meanings: [{"name":"What do you want from me?; Why do you want to get my attention? (There is also a literal meaning.)","examples":["Tom: John, can I talk to you for a minute? John: What is it? ","Sue: Jane? Jane: What is it? Sue: Close the door, please."],"media":[]}]

name: what makes someone tick
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. something that motivates someone; something that makes someone behave in a certain way; If you know what makes someone tick, you understand why that person behaves the way he or she does","examples":["I've never been able to understand what makes him tick.","I've always wondered what makes people like that tick.","William is sort of strange. I don't know what makes him tick.","When you get to know people, you find out what makes them tick."],"media":[]}]

name: What makes you think so?
meanings: [{"name":"Why do you think that?; What is your evidence for that conclusion?","examples":["Tom: This bread may be a little old. Alice: What makes you think so? Tom: The green spots on the edges. ","Bob: Congress is in session again. Tom: What makes you think so? Bob: My wallet's empty."],"media":[]},{"name":"Is that not totally obvious? (Sarcastic.)","examples":["John: I think I'm putting on a little weight. Mary: Oh, yeah? What makes you think so?","Mary (shivering): Gee, I think it's going to be winter soon. Alice (also shivering): Yeah? What makes you think so?"],"media":[]}]

name: What more can I do?
meanings: [{"name":"I am at a loss to know what else to do.; Is there anything else I can do? (An expression of desperation, not an inquiry.)","examples":["Bob: Did you hear about the death in the Wilson family. Bill: Yes. I feel so helpless. I sent flowers. What more can I do? ","Bill: Is your child still sick? Mary: Yes. I'm giving her the medicine the doctor sent over. What more can I do?"],"media":[]}]

name: What would you say if I did something?
meanings: [{"name":"How would you feel or think about my doing something? (Also in other persons.) ","examples":["Bill: What would you say if I ate the last piece of cake? Bob: Go ahead. I don't care. ","Mary: What would you say if we left a little early? Sally: It's okay with me."],"media":[]}]

name: what you see is what you get
meanings: [{"name":"said to show that there is nothing hidden; Nothing additional is concealed or available.; What is in front of you is all you get.","examples":["Q: Are there any red or green ones available? A: Sorry. What you see is what you get.","Director: Could we get a little more excitement in your face when you say the lines? Actor: Not today. I'm too upset. What you see is what you get."],"media":[]}]

name: Whatever
meanings: [{"name":"Anything—it doesn't matter.; Either one.","examples":["Bob: Which do you want, red or green? Tom: Whatever.","Mary: Do you want to go with me to the seashore or stay here? Jane: Whatever."],"media":[]}]

name: What's cooking?
meanings: [{"name":"What is happening?; How are you? (Colloquial or slang.)","examples":["Bob: Hi, Fred! What's cooking? Fred: How are you doing, Bob?","Bob: Hi, Bill! What's cooking? Bill: Nothing. Anything happening with you?"],"media":[]}]

name: What's eating someone?
meanings: [{"name":"What is bothering someone? (Slang.)","examples":["Tom: Go away! Bob: Gee, Tom, what's eating you?","Bill: Tom's so grouchy lately. What's eating him? Bob: Beats me!"],"media":[]}]

name: What's going on (around here)?
meanings: [{"name":"What is happening in this place?; What is the explanation for the strange things that are happening here? ","examples":["Bill: There was an accident in the factory this morning. Bob: That's the second one this week. What's going on around here?","Mary: What's all the noise? What's going on? Sue: We're just having a little party."],"media":[]}]

name: What's in it for someone?
meanings: [{"name":"What is the benefit for someone in this scheme?","examples":["Bob: Now, that plan is just what is needed. Bill: What's in it for me? What do I get out of it?","Sue: We signed the Wilson contract yesterday. Mary: That's great! What's in it for me?"],"media":[]}]

name: what's it to someone?
meanings: [{"name":"why does someone want to know; It's none of someone's  business. used to respond in a somewhat angry or annoyed way to a question that one does not want to answer","examples":["\"He wants to know how much they pay you?\" \"Why? What's it to him?\"","Tom: Where are you going? Jane: What's it to you?","Mary: Bill's pants don't match his shirt. Jane: Does it matter? What's it to you?"],"media":[]}]

name: what's the big idea
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask why someone is doing or saying something; used to ask someone why they have done something annoying; What have you done?; Why did you do that? (Usually expressing a little anger.)","examples":["Hey! What's the big idea!?","What's the big idea? I was watching that program!","You knocked the book out of my hand. What's the big idea?","What's the idea? You just about knocked me down! Watch where you're going!"],"media":[]}]

name: what's the big deal?
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask why something is so important?","examples":["So I'm late. What's the big deal?"],"media":[]}]

name: What's the deal? / What's the scam?
meanings: [{"name":"What is going on around here? (Often implies that something seems to be wrong.)","examples":["There's a big rumpus down the hall. What's the scam? ","I gave you a twenty, and you give me five back? What's the deal? Where's my other five?","Hey, What's the deal? You've been parked on our street for two hours.","John, what's the deal? You're cutting school, you dropped out of activities that used to matter to you.","Mary: What's the deal? Sue: Oh, hi, Mary. We're just cleaning out the closet.","Bill: Hi, you guys. What's the deal? Bob: Nothing, just a little misunderstanding between Fred and Jane."],"media":[]}]

name: What's the catch?
meanings: [{"name":"What is the drawback?; It sounds good, but are there any hidden problems? What are the negative factors? (Colloquial.)","examples":["Bill: How would you like to have these seven books for your very own? Sally: What's the catch? Bill: There's no catch. You have to pay for them, but there's no catch.","Bob: Here, take this dollar bill. Sue: So, what's the catch? Bob: No catch. It's counterfeit.","Sounds too good to be true. What's the catch? ","This looks like a good deal. What's the catch?"],"media":[]}]

name: what's the difference?
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask how one thing is different from another","examples":["\"I like this one a lot more than that one.\" \"Why? What's the difference (between them)?\""],"media":[]},{"name":"what difference does it/that make?; used to ask why something is important or to suggest that something is not important","examples":["What's the difference whether I go or not?","What difference does it make if I go with you?"],"media":[]}]

name: What's the matter (with you)?
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. Is there something wrong with you?; Are you ill?; used for asking someone if there is a problem","examples":["Bill: What's the matter with you? Fred: I have this funny feeling in my chest. Bill: Sounds serious.","Bob: I have to stay home again today. Bill: What's the matter with you? Have you seen a doctor?","Mary: Oh, I'm so miserable! Sue: What's the matter? Mary: I lost my contact lenses and my glasses.","John: Ouch! Alice: What's the matter? John: I bit my tongue.","You look worried – what's the matter?"],"media":[]},{"name":"How very stupid of you! How can you be so stupid? (Usually said in anger.)","examples":["As Fred stumbled over the step and dumped the birthday cake on the floor, Jane screamed, “What's the matter with you? The party is in fifteen minutes and we have no cake!”","Mary: I think I just lost the Wilson account. Sue: What! What's the matter with you? That account pays your salary!"],"media":[]}]

name: What's there to know? / What's to know?
meanings: [{"name":"This doesn't require any special knowledge—so what are you talking about?","examples":["Bill: Do you know how to wind a watch? Bob: Wind a watch? What's there to know?","Sue: We must find someone who knows how to repair a broken lawn mower. Tom: What's to know? Just a little tightening here and there. That's all it needs."],"media":[]}]

name: What's with someone or something?
meanings: [{"name":"what is wrong with someone or something;  Why is someone or something in that condition?; What's going on with someone or something?","examples":["What's with him? Is he upset?","“What's with this stupid coffeepot? It won't get hot!” groused Alice.","So what's with all the boxes? Are you moving in, or is she moving out?"],"media":[]}]

name: what's the good of something?

When these individuals broke their pledge and started hitting the bottle again, they were said to have ‘fallen off the wagon'."]]]
