meanings: [{"name":"to affect or involve (someone or something) as the result of an event or action; to affect (someone or something) in a bad or harmful way","examples":["What is going to happen to me?","An odd thing happened to me on my way to the office last week.","I promise nothing will happen to you.\n","What happened to the car? There's a big scratch on the fender."],"media":[]},{"name":"to do or be by chance","examples":["I just happened to hear (= heard by chance) that you have an extra ticket?","They happened to look (= looked by chance) in the right place almost immediately.","We're just two friends who happen to be roommates."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that something is true, although other people may not agree or may find it surprising","examples":["She happens to like cleaning (= she likes cleaning, although that is surprising).","Well, do you happen to be in the Hamptons right now?","We happen to be going away this weekend.","I also happen to be from your hometown.","This happens to be the best restaurant in town."],"media":[]}]

name: rivet on
meanings: [{"name":"to attach something to something with rivets","examples":["The pockets of these jeans are riveted onto the body of the pants.","You should rivet on this part of the frame to the wall."],"media":[]},{"name":"to attract and hold (something, such as a person's attention) completely","examples":["Everyone riveted their eyes on the trick that the magician was performing on stage.","Their eyes riveted on the paintings."],"media":[]}]

name: think about
meanings: [{"name":"to contemplate; to give serious and careful thought to; to remember or imagine someone or something","examples":["Whenever I think about him, I get goose bumps.","I don't want to think about it.","He was thinking about the time he spent in the army."],"media":[]}]

name: not think straight / not see straight
meanings: [{"name":"to be unable to use your mind in an effective way; unable to think clearly; cannot function (often because of strong emotion)","examples":["I was so tired, I couldn't think straight.","I'm very stressed. And with you and Kate down my throat, I can hardly think straight.","I really can't think straight when I'm hungry.","Jane: I am so upset I can barely think straight.\nBob: Jane, I understand that you're upset. But, this is your fault, too, you know.","She left me so frustrated that I couldn't see straight.","I was so bored I couldn't see straight.","Jane: Come on, I need help here, all right?\nKate: Look, I got to sleep, okay? I can't think straight."],"media":[]}]

name: stroll around
meanings: [{"name":"to walk around casually","examples":["I think I will stroll around a bit this evening.","Would you like to stroll around a little and see the sights?"],"media":[]}]

name: stroll through
meanings: [{"name":"to walk casually through something or some place","examples":["Would you like to stroll through the park with me?","We were strolling through the park and no one was around.","Let's stroll through a few shops and see what the prices are like here."],"media":[]}]

name: taken with someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"highly attracted to someone or something; delighted with","examples":["The princess would be so taken with my style and elegance.","The audience was taken with the stage setting.","I'm just taken with her."],"media":[]}]

name: don't get me started
meanings: [{"name":"Don't encourage me to start talking about something; (implication: because it could take a long time and it wouldn't be complimentary)","examples":["Oh, those politicians always walking over the small businessman. Don't get me started about the government.","“How was the food?” “Don't get me started on the food” (excited or upset about the culinary experience).","Don't get me started on the fauna!","Don't even get me started on yours."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782379864/phrases/iinbu5izxgq5qytuuxbv.mp4","publicId":"phrases/iinbu5izxgq5qytuuxbv","type":"video"},{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782379875/phrases/bcwbmioxrj138q2kf3n4.mp4","publicId":"phrases/bcwbmioxrj138q2kf3n4","type":"video"}]}]
extraDetails: [["Literal meaning",["Don't cause me to begin talking about this subject.","But in actual usage, it usually implies: If I start talking about it, I won't stop easily."]]]

name: on one's own
meanings: [{"name":"alone","examples":["I don't mind going to the movies on my own.","I'm gonna make it on my own, and I certainly can't think straight with all this noise.","He made the decision on his own."],"media":[]},{"name":"left to rely entirely on one's own resources","examples":["If you mess up, you're on your own."],"media":[]}]

name: in peace
meanings: [{"name":"peacefully; in a state of quiet and calm","examples":["They have lived in peace for many years.","Let her dine in peace.","The point is you got to leave so I can live my life in peace.","Can I get a little privacy so I can use my machine in peace."],"media":[]}]

name: better late than never
meanings: [{"name":"Doing something late is better than not doing it; it is better for someone to arrive or do something late than not to arrive or do it at all","examples":["\"Dan finally paid me the money he owed me.\" \"Well, better late than never.\"","I'm sorry I'm late to the party. Better late than never, right?","Jill: Lisa's birthday was two weeks ago. Should I send her a card now? Jane: Better late than never."],"media":[]}]

name: lay eyes on / set eyes on
meanings: [{"name":"to see someone or something for the first time","examples":["I knew when I set eyes on that car that it was the car for me.","Have you ever laid eyes on such a beautiful flower?","I never laid eyes on her before today."],"media":[]}]

name: rest up
meanings: [{"name":"to relax in order to have strength for something","examples":["Why don't you take a nap to rest up for the party?","Excuse me, but I have to go rest up for the concert tonight.","I really need to rest up a while."],"media":[]},{"name":"to recover or recuperate from something tiring","examples":["I need about a week to rest up from my long travels. ","I'll need a few days to rest up."],"media":[]}]

name: days on end
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. many days; several or many days in a row; many hours, days, etc. without stopping","examples":["Sometimes they didn't speak to each other for days on end.","We kept on traveling for days on end.","Her work took her away from her family, sometimes for months on end.","Doctor, I've had this pain for days on end.","We shouldn't have to stare at your cans for days on end."],"media":[]}]

name: muddy up
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to make water muddy; to stir up the mud in water, as at the bottom of a pond or river","examples":[" Don't muddy the water up. It will clog our filters. ","Don't muddy up the water"],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to make something unclear; to make a situation more confusing or difficult","examples":["You have really muddied this issue up. I thought I understood it.","You sure muddied up this issue."],"media":[]}]

name: have to do with
meanings: [{"name":"to be associated with or related to something; to deal with; to be about something","examples":["The story has to do with real people.","My question has to do with last week's assignment.","Sally's unhappiness has to do with the way you insulted her.","What does that have to do with Kate?"],"media":[]}]

name: thud into someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to bump into someone or something, making a dull noise on impact","examples":["The door blew open and thudded into Marie, giving her a bump on the knee.","The ball thudded into the side of the house.","Apples thudded into baskets."],"media":[]}]

name: up to something
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. [of someone] plotting something","examples":["I think they are up to something.","I am sure that Lily and Max are up to something evil. "],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. [of someone] well enough or rested enough to do something","examples":["I'm not quite up to the party. ","Are you up to a game of volleyball?","Are you SURE you're up to baking the muffins?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to be as good as something; to be good enough for something","examples":["This work's not up to the standard of the class.","Your last essay was not up to your best."],"media":[]}]

name: in the blink of an eye /  in the wink of an eye / in the twinkling of an eye
meanings: [{"name":"in an instant; extremely quickly","examples":["I can bake anything from fritters to pies in the blink of an eye.","In the blink of an eye, he was gone.","He was back in the twinkle/twinkling of an eye.","It was all over in the wink of an eye.","Just call us on this number if you have any problems, and we'll be back in the wink of an eye."],"media":[]}]

name: come between
meanings: [{"name":"to cause disagreement between (people or groups); to cause problems between two people or interrupt two people","examples":["We shouldn't let these problems come between us.","Don't let one little quarrel come between you."],"media":[]},{"name":"to stop someone from doing something that they like doing","examples":["Nothing comes between Jim and his food."],"media":[]}]

name: suffice to say / suffice it to say
meanings: [{"name":"it is enough to say;  it is sufficient to say; used to say that one could give more information about something but that the statement that follows is enough","examples":["Suffice to say, she has a lot on her hands with four children.","Suffice (it) to say, Mike won't be going to Tina's birthday party after what he said about her to her boss.","Suffice it to say, I'm not a huge fan of this hospital project."],"media":[]}]

name: heat up
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. get warmer or hot","examples":["The morning started out cold but it heated up quickly.","It really heats up in the afternoon around here.","How soon will dinner be heated up? "],"media":[]},{"name":"cause (something) to become warm or hot); raise the temperature of something to a certain level","examples":["Could you heat up the vegetables, please?","Let's see what happens when I heat it up.","Please heat this room up to about seventy degrees.","Can you heat up the room a little more?"],"media":[]},{"name":"become more active, intense, or angry; make someone angry","examples":["Their conversation started to heat up.","Competition between the two companies is heating up.","The debate began to heat up near the end.","Their argument was heating up, and I was afraid there would be fighting.","This kind of nonsense really heats me up.","Mean talk heats up the kids."],"media":[]}]

name: fall off the radar
meanings: [{"name":"to stop being noticed or talked about","examples":["With so many other pressing problems that need attention, things can just fall off the radar.","An actor who has fallen off the radar.","But if that's the case, why has Bob fallen right off our radar?"],"media":[]}]

name: dish up
meanings: [{"name":"to put (food) into a dish or dishes for serving or eating","examples":["Please dish up some soup.","The crew dished up fish sandwiches to the hungry workers."],"media":[]},{"name":"present; show; to produce something","examples":["The movie dishes up a wild mix of comedy and violence.","The offer is better than anything the other airlines can dish up."],"media":[]}]

name: keep one's eye on the ball
meanings: [{"name":"to stay focused; to continue thinking about or giving attention to something important; to remain alert to the events occurring around oneself","examples":["She really needs to keep her eye on the ball if she wants to win the election.","You have to keep your eye on the ball in business.","If you want to get along in this office, you're going to have to keep your eye on the ball.","Bill would do better in his classes if he would just keep his eye on the ball."],"media":[]},{"name":"to watch or follow the ball carefully, especially when one is playing a ball game; to follow the details of a ball game very carefully","examples":["John, if you can't keep your eye on the ball, I'll have to take you out of the game.","“Keep your eye on the ball!” the coach roared at the players."],"media":[]}]

name: keep an eye on / have an eye on
meanings: [{"name":"to watch someone or something; to monitor someone or something closely","examples":["I have my eye on the apple tree. When the apples ripen, I'll harvest them.","The security services always have eyes on known foreign intelligence operatives, he said.","Please keep an eye on the baby.","Will you please keep your eye on my house while I'm on vacation?","Traveling alone, you always have to have eyes on your luggage."],"media":[]}]

name: have one's eye on
meanings: [{"name":"to be looking at or watching someone or something; to watch constantly and attentively","examples":["Two officers had eyes on the suspect shortly before he disappeared.","He radioed that he had eyes on the building.","Travellng alone, you always have to have eyes on your luggage.","I had my eye on her. I don't think she noticed."],"media":[]},{"name":"to be thinking about getting or intend to get something or someone","examples":["He suspected other farmers of having eyes on his land.","She now has eyes on the championship title.","The electronics group made a takeover bid for the company, having had eyes on it for some time.","She has her eye on a little cottage in the country."],"media":[]}]

name: let down
meanings: [{"name":"If you let down a piece of clothing, you make it longer; to allow to descend gradually","examples":["My trousers shrank in the wash so I let them down."],"media":[]},{"name":"to relax one's efforts or vigilance","examples":["Now is no time to let down. Keep on your guard.","After the contest was over, Jane let down a bit so she could relax."],"media":[]},{"name":"disappoint; to fail to support; to cause someone to be disappointed, often because you have failed to do what you promised","examples":["You'll be there tomorrow – you won't let me down, will you?","She felt her parents had let her down.","With my poor performance I really felt that I had let my teammates down.","Please don't let me down. I am depending on you.","I'm sorry I let you down. Something came up, and I couldn't meet you.","I don't want to let you down, but I can't support you in the election."],"media":[]}]

name: head out (for something)
meanings: [{"name":"leave or depart for something or some place; begin a journey to something or some place","examples":["We headed out for Denver very early in the morning.","What time do we head out tomorrow morning?","Hey, Kate, I'm gonna head out and get some food. I'll be back in a bit."],"media":[]}]

name: sweep one off one's feet / knock one off one's feet
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to knock someone down","examples":["The wind swept me off my feet.","Bill punched Bob playfully, and knocked him off his feet."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to overwhelm someone (figuratively); to gain immediate and unquestioning support, approval, or acceptance by a person","examples":["The news was so exciting that it knocked me off my feet."],"media":[]}]

name: make the rounds
meanings: [{"name":"(of a rumor, a piece of news, etc.) to be passed from one person to another person and become widely known","examples":["Rumors about his resignation were making the rounds.","The story that Kate told made the rounds."],"media":[]},{"name":"to talk to a lot of people","examples":["I've made/done the rounds of all the agents, but nobody has any tickets left.","Kate is making the rounds.","On Monday, Kate will make the rounds across New York City."],"media":[]}]

name: roll in
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to come in large numbers or amounts, easily, as if rolling. (Alludes to the arrival of many wheeled conveyances.); to appear or arrive in large numbers or amounts","examples":["The money has been rolling in.","We didn't expect many people at the party, but they just kept rolling in.","Money is simply rolling in for our charity."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to have lots of something, such as money— enough to roll in","examples":["She is just rolling in cash.","Mary is rolling in money because she won the lottery."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to rotate about in something","examples":["What is that dog rolling in?","We had fun rolling in the leaves."],"media":[]},{"name":"to arrive at a place especially later than usual or expected","examples":["He finally rolled in at 3:30 in the morning.","The two cars rolled into the parking lot at about the same time."," What time did they roll in?"],"media":[]}]

name: on a roll
meanings: [{"name":"experiencing a period of success or good luck; in the midst of a series of successes","examples":["Don't stop me now. I'm on a roll.","Things are going great for Larry. He's on a roll now.","They've won nine games in a row, so they're obviously on a roll."],"media":[]}]

name: brace yourself
meanings: [{"name":"said to warn someone to be prepared for something; to prepare yourself physically or mentally for something unpleasant","examples":["Brace yourself. I have some bad news.","The passengers were told to brace themselves (= to press their bodies hard against something or hold them very stiff) for a crash landing.","She told me she had some bad news for me and I braced myself for a shock.","We're bracing ourselves for the first snow of winter."],"media":[]}]

name: order in
meanings: [{"name":"to have something, usually food, brought into one's house or place of business.","examples":["Do you want to order pizza in?","Shall I order in pizza?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to command someone to get into something","examples":["She didn't want to go, but the cop ordered her in.","The officer ordered Ann into the wagon."],"media":[]}]

name: go by (someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"to pass by someone or something","examples":["We went by Alice without even noticing her.","We went by because we were in a hurry."],"media":[]},{"name":"to move past, in space or time","examples":["You can watch the trains going by from this window.","You can't let an opportunity like that go by - it's too good to miss.","Hardly a day goes by when I don't think about her.","As time goes by, it becomes easier to forgive and forget."],"media":[]},{"name":"to follow or use information provided by something or someone","examples":["Don't go by what she says – she's always wrong.","I'm sorry, madam, but we have to go by the rules."],"media":[]}]

name: work one's magic
meanings: [{"name":"to do something very well","examples":["The kitchen where a great cook works her magic."],"media":[]},{"name":"to have a desired good effect","examples":["It may take a few hours for the medication to work its magic."],"media":[]}]

name: easy pickings
meanings: [{"name":"[of things] easy to get or steal; [of people] easy to get or persuade; a large range of good things to choose from","examples":["The pickpockets found lots of easy pickings at the state fair.","The checks are easy pickings for thieves, defense lawyers have told the Daily News.","Investors have found easy/rich pickings in the property market in recent years."],"media":[]}]

name: serve a purpose
meanings: [{"name":"to be useful or helpful in some way; to be useful in accomplishing some purpose","examples":["Public information advertisements serve a valuable public purpose.","This large book should serve a useful purpose. We can use it for a doorstop.","School uniforms also serve a useful purpose by identifying who belongs on campus.","Do these ridiculous rules serve any purpose at all?"],"media":[]}]

name: serve no purpose
meanings: [{"name":"to not be useful or helpful in any way","examples":["Arguing with him serves no purpose.","Conflicts will serve no purpose, but preparation will."],"media":[]}]

name: serve someone's purpose / answer someone's purpose
meanings: [{"name":"to fit or suit someone's aim or goal","examples":["This piece of wood will answer my purpose quite nicely. ","The new car serves our purpose perfectly."],"media":[]}]

name: stand by
meanings: [{"name":"to remain loyal or faithful to; defend","examples":["He stood by her through the difficult times.","You have to stand by your friends through thick and through thin.","Don't worry. I'll stand by you no matter what."],"media":[]},{"name":"to be prepared for something; to wait and remain ready. (Generally heard in communication, such as broadcasting, telephones, etc.)","examples":["Cabin crew, please stand by for take-off.","Is everyone ready for the telecast? Only ten seconds—stand by.","The general ordered his troops to stand by for a possible attack.","The Central Bank was standing by, ready to intervene to prevent a further slide against the dollar."],"media":[]},{"name":"to stand next to someone or something","examples":["Jeff, please stand by Judy. I want to take your picture.","Can I stand by the window and watch the birds?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to let something happen or to be unable to prevent something; to allow something unpleasant to happen without doing anything to stop it","examples":["How could anyone simply stand by while the man was robbed?","We stood by helplessly while the fire destroyed our barn.","We can't stand by while millions of people starve."],"media":[]}]

name: build on something
meanings: [{"name":" Lit. to construct something on the base of something else","examples":["The ancients built their houses on the houses of earlier people."],"media":[]},{"name":"to use a success or achievement as a base from which to achieve more success; to add to and develop something that already exists","examples":["We must build on our reputation to expand the business.","He has to build on his strong friendships with the customers.","She built her success on years of experience in the fashion industry.","A good relationship is built on trust."],"media":[]}]

name: in a word
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. in short; said simply; concisely said; said when you are going to give your opinion about something quickly and directly","examples":["In a word, she's lying.","Mrs. Smith is—in a word—haughty.","In a word, the play flopped."],"media":[]}]

name: benefit of the doubt
meanings: [{"name":"a judgment in one's favor when the evidence is neither for one nor against one; to believe something good about someone, rather than something bad, when you have the possibility of doing either","examples":["I was right between a B and an A. I got the benefit of the doubt—an A.","I thought I should have had the benefit of the doubt, but the judge made me pay a fine.","I didn't know whether his story was true or not, but I decided to give him the benefit of the doubt.","When you moved here, I tried to give you the benefit of the doubt! But you're evil. "],"media":[]}]

name: in the mood
meanings: [{"name":"feeling a desire for something or to do something; to feel like doing or having something","examples":["Kate:  Are you in the mood for pizza?\nJane: No, I'm in the mood for biryani.","I'm sorry. I'm just not in the mood to talk.","\"Would you like to see a movie?\" \"No, I'm not in the mood (to see a movie).\"","We could go out to eat, if you're in the mood.","I'm not really in the mood for shopping.","He seemed to be in the mood to fight."],"media":[]}]

name: worthy of something
meanings: [{"name":"suitable for or characteristic of something; good enough to have been written, said, done, or created by (someone, especially someone famous)","examples":["He threw a party worthy of a millionaire.","Truly, it was a feat worthy of a superhero.","I thought she showed patience worthy of a saint.","This, it was generally agreed, was a performance worthy of an Oscar nomination."],"media":[]}]

name: worthy of the name
meanings: [{"name":"deserving to be so called; good enough to enjoy a specific designation","examples":["There was not an actor worthy of the name in that play. ","Any art critic worthy of the name would know that painting to be a fake.","Everyone at N.Y.U. hates me. I have minions, of course, but they're hardly even worthy of the name."],"media":[]}]

name: get to know someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to spend time with someone or something so that you gradually learn more about them or it; becoming acquainted with someone or something","examples":["We just bought a house here last month, and we're still getting to know our neighbors.","I'll need a few weeks to get to know the system.","Are you just too interested in yourself to get to know me?","I spent my evenings walking around, getting to know the area."],"media":[]}]

name: slip up
meanings: [{"name":"to make a mistake; blunder","examples":["We were late because of a slipup in the schedule.","These figures don't make sense - have we slipped up somewhere?","I hope you don't slip up again. Try to be more careful.","I'm afraid I slipped up on that detail."],"media":[]}]

name: harm's way
meanings: [{"name":"a dangerous place or situation","examples":["She was placed in harm's way.","We got them out of harm's way.","We got everyone out of harm's way just minutes before the house was ripped apart by the tornado.","Soldiers are expected to know what to do when they are in harm's way."],"media":[]}]

name: take a shot
meanings: [{"name":"to fire a gun; to fire a shot","examples":["He took a shot and missed.","Bob took a shot at you?","The hunter took a shot at the deer. ","Who took a shot at my mailbox?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to try to hit","examples":["She took a shot at me with a snowball but missed."],"media":[]},{"name":"to make a critical or hurtful remark about someone","examples":["They took shots at each other throughout the debate."],"media":[]},{"name":"to attempt to do something successfully ","examples":["Take a shot at the math problem.","I never changed a tire before, but I'll take a shot at it."],"media":[]},{"name":"to photograph something","examples":["Be sure to take a shot of the house.","Tap it to launch the camera instantly from standby, press again to take a shot."],"media":[]}]

name: sneak around
meanings: [{"name":"to move around a place in a sneaky or stealthy fashion","examples":["Please don't sneak around the house. It makes me nervous."," Please stop sneaking around!","I'm getting tired of always sneaking around.","It's not like we have to sneak around behind her back."],"media":[]}]

name: above all
meanings: [{"name":"especially; more than everything","examples":["I'm gonna be kind and faithful and above all, honest.","I'm a woman of a certain age in a business that values youth above all else.","Show up on time, no more 3-course lunches, and above all, have ready all your presentations.","She knew red was her color. She knew diamonds went with everything. But the one thing Gaby knew above all else, she would never want children."],"media":[]}]

name: give out
meanings: [{"name":"break down; fail; to wear out and stop; If a machine or part of your body gives out, it stops working","examples":["My old bicycle finally gave out.","I think that your shoes are about ready to give out.","Apparently Bob's heart just gave out."],"media":[]},{"name":" to be depleted; to last no longer","examples":["Food supplies will give out by the end of the week.","The paper napkins gave out, and we had to use paper towels.","The eggs gave out, and we had to eat cereal for breakfast for the rest of the camping trip."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to distribute something; to pass something out; to give something to each of a number of people","examples":["The teacher gave the test papers out.","The teacher gave out the papers.","They're giving out free tickets to the circus."],"media":[]},{"name":"to make something known to the public","examples":["When will you give the announcement out?","The president gave out the news that the hostages had been released."],"media":[]}]

name: fall apart
meanings: [{"name":"to break into separate pieces; disintegrate","examples":["The pie was falling apart as I served it.","Our furniture is falling apart.","My poor old boots are falling apart."],"media":[]},{"name":"break down; to fail completely and be unable to continue in the usual way; to succumb to mental or emotional stress","examples":["The deal fell apart because of a lack of money.","When his wife died, he fell apart (= was unable to continue with life in the usual way).","She began to fall apart when her son was imprisoned."],"media":[]}]

name: cover one's tracks
meanings: [{"name":"to conceal one's trail; to conceal one's past activities; to do things that hide someone's activities from other people, so that they cannot find out what someone has been doing","examples":[" The robber failed to cover his tracks.","It's easy to cover up your tracks when the investigators botch their job.","She was able to cover her tracks up so that they couldn't pin the charges on her.","He transferred money illegally into his own account, and then tried to cover his tracks by destroying the computer records."],"media":[]}]

name: haggle about something
meanings: [{"name":"to bargain or negotiate about something","examples":["They are always willing to haggle about the price, so don't take the first price you're given.","I wish you wouldn't try to haggle about everything when we shop."],"media":[]}]

name: haggle (with someone) (over someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"to argue with someone over someone or something; to argue about the price of something in an attempt to make the seller reduce it","examples":["I don't want to haggle with you over Tom and whose team he's going to be on. ","Let's not haggle over the price.","There is no point in haggling with her.","If you're a cash buyer, haggle with the dealer to get the best price and/or free extras."],"media":[]}]

name: web of lies
meanings: [{"name":"sophisticated and complex network of falsehoods, designed to deceive and entangle others, often with devastating consequences when exposed.","examples":["A CEO's web of lies is exposed after federal investigators uncover years of embezzlement, revealing a complex network of false financial records and misleading statements.","A politician's web of lies is exposed after a thorough investigation reveals a pattern of dishonesty and deception, including fabricated stories and misleading statements.","The entire evening had been a web of lies."],"media":[]}]

name: on the table
meanings: [{"name":"up for consideration or negotiation; If a plan or suggestion has been put/laid on the table, it has been made available for people to hear, read, or discuss","examples":["There are several important issues on the table.","The chairman said we could not discuss salaries since the topic was no longer on the table.","There's a deal on the table, and it's fast-tracked to close in 24 hours.","Who says the offer's still on the table?"],"media":[]}]

name: off the table
meanings: [{"name":"not up for consideration or negotiation; no longer being considered","examples":["A dividend payment this year is definitely off the table.","That option is now off the table."],"media":[]}]

name: do justice
meanings: [{"name":" to treat fairly or adequately; to do something well; to represent or portray something accurately; to treat or show (something or someone) in a way that is as good as it should be","examples":["This postcard doesn't do justice to the wonderful scenery.","I knew I could never do  both jobs justice.","The movie does not do justice to the book","Just calling the movie “fun” doesn't do it justice (= it is better than just “fun”).","Sally did justice to our side in the contract negotiations."],"media":[]},{"name":" to eat or drink a great deal","examples":["Bill always does justice to the turkey on Thanksgiving.","The party didn't do justice to the chicken fry. There were nearly ten pounds leftover."],"media":[]}]

name: slough off
meanings: [{"name":"to get rid of something or someone unwanted; If you slough something off, you treat it as unimportant or do not take it seriously","examples":["He seemed to want to slough off all his old friends.","Politicians sloughed off the issue.","I didn't want to be one of those kind of women, you know, sloughing things off onto coworkers because of a pediatrician appointment or a dance recital."],"media":[]},{"name":"to ignore or disregard a negative remark or incident","examples":["I could see that the remark had hurt her feelings, but she just pretended to slough it off.","Liz sloughed off the remark."],"media":[]}]

name: work into

name: case in point

For a case in point, look at what happened to Bob Smith last Deepavali.","Many students struggle with time management; a case in point is Sarah, who frequently misses deadlines.","Technology can lead to social isolation; a case in point is how many teens prefer texting over face-to-face conversations."],"media":[]}]

name: jump out at
meanings: [{"name":"to suddenly come at (someone) from a hiding place","examples":["The hidden assailant jumped out at them."],"media":[]},{"name":"to immediately get the attention of (someone); If something jumps out at you, you notice it immediately","examples":["The sculpture jumps out at you when you enter the house.","I checked for errors, but nothing jumped out at me.","Please. Just check to see if something jumps out at you.","That's a very effective advertisement - it really jumps out at you."],"media":[]}]

name: keep in check /hold in check
meanings: [{"name":"to keep someone or something under control; to restrain someone or something","examples":["He's trying to hold his emotions in check.","The government has raised interest rates in an attempt to keep inflation in check.","Hang on to this rope to keep the dog in check. ","I was so angry I could hardly hold myself in check."],"media":[]}]

name: slippery slope
meanings: [{"name":"a dangerous pathway or route to follow; a route that leads to trouble; a bad situation or habit that, after it has started, is likely to get very much worse","examples":["You're on a slippery slope once you start lying about your age!","But it's too much of a slippery slope for me.","Lowering your standards is a slippery slope, Bob."],"media":[]}]

name: razor's edge
meanings: [{"name":"used in various phrases to refer to a dangerous position or a position in which two different things are carefully balanced","examples":["He's a thrill-seeker who likes living on the razor's edge.","The country's future is balanced on a razor's edge.","He walks a/the razor edge between humor and bad taste in his comedy.","I've been walking the razor's edge since Bob joined the gang."],"media":[]}]

name: face facts / face the fact(s)
meanings: [{"name":"to admit that something is true; to accept that something unpleasant is true and start to deal with the situation","examples":["Let's face facts—our plan isn't working.","Time to face facts. We have no money.","Eventually, you will have to face the facts. Times are hard.","We have to face facts here - we simply don't have enough money."],"media":[]}]

name: stay behind
meanings: [{"name":"to not leave at the present time; to not leave a place when other people leave","examples":["You can go on ahead. I'll stay behind to help clean up.","I stayed behind after class.","I will stay behind and tell the late arrivers where you have gone.","Fred always stayed behind to clean up."],"media":[]}]

name: carry one's (own) weight / pull one's (own) weight
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to do one's share of work that a group of people is doing together; to earn one's keep. (The weight is the burden that is the responsibility of someone.)","examples":["Tom, you must be more helpful around the house. We each have to carry our own weight.","Bill, I'm afraid that you can't work here anymore. You just haven't been carrying your weight.","If he doesn't start pulling his weight, he'll lose his job.","I could come with you guys. Let me pull my weight.","The others had complained that Sarah wasn't pulling her weight."],"media":[]}]

name: to the tune of
meanings: [{"name":"using the tune of (a particular song)","examples":["Amusing lyrics were sung to the tune of \"New York, New York.\""],"media":[]},{"name":"in the amount of; approximately; used to emphasize that the amount or extent of something (such as money) is considerable","examples":["They are drowning in the medical bills to the tune of 5 million.","Kate first shared a snippet of the track to her official TikTok page on Sept. 12 to the tune of 80,000 likes and 460,000 views.","We're in debt to the tune of $50,000.","She is suing the company for breach of contract to the tune of $10 million."],"media":[]}]

name: in lockstep
meanings: [{"name":"in complete agreement with someone or something","examples":["He said that he and the rest of the board were in lockstep behind their leader.","The two judges usually voted in lockstep.","It's time to work now, all of us, in lockstep."],"media":[]}]

name: live by
meanings: [{"name":"to agree with and follow (something, such as a set of beliefs)","examples":["He tried to live by his faith.","a principle I try to live by."],"media":[]},{"name":"to survive by (doing something)","examples":["They were an ancient people who lived by hunting and gathering.","She lives by her own skill and hard work.","We live by the skills that we have—and hard work, of course.","Let me share two words to live by. Plausible deniability."],"media":[]}]

name: by and large
meanings: [{"name":"generally; usually; on the whole; when everything about a situation is considered together","examples":["By and large, the people of this state are not happy with the governor's policies.","There are a few things that I don't like about my job, but by and large it's very enjoyable.","I find that, by and large, people tend to do what they are told to do.","By and large, rosebushes need lots of care."],"media":[]}]

name: none the wiser
meanings: [{"name":"not knowing or understanding anything more about something","examples":["The investigation has been going on for months, and we're still none the wiser about the true cause of the accident."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to describe someone who is not at all aware of something that has happened; not knowing any more in spite of events or exposure to facts.","examples":["I borrowed his car and returned it, and he was none the wiser.","I read the computer manual, but I'm still none the wiser.","The health department gave the restaurant a warning, but the customers were none the wiser."],"media":[]}]

name: in passing
meanings: [{"name":"incidentally; by the way; while talking or thinking about something else","examples":["I just heard your name in passing. I didn't hear more than that.","He amazed us by remembering all sorts of things we had only mentioned in passing.","She acknowledged their financial support, but only in passing.","Jane: Kate, Did you tell anyone about the hospital bill.\nKate: I may have mentioned it to my parents in passing."],"media":[]}]

name: flesh and blood
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. a living human body, especially with reference to its natural limitations; a human being; people","examples":["This cold weather is more than flesh and blood can stand.","Carrying 300 pounds is beyond mere flesh and blood."],"media":[]},{"name":"near kindred; one's own relatives; one's own kin","examples":["I want to leave my money to my own flesh and blood.","Let's receive these exiles as if they were our own flesh and blood.","She is our flesh and blood, and she's out there! I need to know how she's doing. I need to know she's okay!","Jane: He will not abandon his own flesh and blood.\nKate: You're his flesh and blood. He put you in a home.","You're my grandson. My flesh and blood."],"media":[]},{"name":"Sometimes used jokingly to remind people of their family obligations","examples":["You can't cut her out of your life. She's your flesh and blood.","Come on, Dad, let me borrow the car. You can't refuse your own flesh and blood."],"media":[]}]

name: lay low / lie low
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to keep quiet and not be noticed; to avoid being conspicuous. (Lay is a common error for lie.)","examples":["I suggest you lie low for a few days.","The robber said that he would lay low for a short time after the robbery."],"media":[]}]

name: all eyes and ears
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. listening and watching eagerly and carefully","examples":["Be careful what you say. The children are all eyes and ears.","Tell us quick. We are all eyes and ears!"],"media":[]}]

name: back down
meanings: [{"name":"to go down something backwards, such as a ladder or inclined driveway","examples":["Harry backed down the ladder safely.","Looking behind him, he backed down slowly."],"media":[]},{"name":"to yield to a person or a thing; to fail to carry through on a threat","examples":["Jane backed down from her position on the budget.","It's probably better to back down from this situation; looks like you are at a disadvantage."],"media":[]},{"name":"to lessen or drop an earlier rigid position on something; to yield something in an argument","examples":["She backed down on her demands","In the end, she backed down."],"media":[]}]

name: play it safe
meanings: [{"name":"to be careful and avoid risk or danger","examples":["I decided to play it safe and leave early so that I would be sure to arrive on time.","Let's play it safe and allow an extra ten minutes to get there.","You should play it safe and take your umbrella.","If you have a cold or the flu, play it safe and go to bed."],"media":[]}]

name: gobble up
meanings: [{"name":"to eat someone or something completely and rapidly","examples":["The wolf said that he was going to gobble the little girl up.","The wolf wanted to gobble up the little pig."],"media":[]},{"name":"to use up, buy up, or occupy all of something","examples":["The shoppers gobbled all the sale merchandise up in a few hours. ","They gobbled up everything.","The mounting legal costs quickly gobbled up their savings."],"media":[]}]

name: own up / own up to
meanings: [{"name":"to admit something; to confess to something; to tell the truth or to admit that you are responsible for something","examples":["Finally, he owned up to his mother about breaking the vase.","I know you broke the window. Come on and own up to it.","They denied having broken the window, but later owned up.","No one has owned up to stealing the money.","If no one owns up, then I shall punish the whole class."],"media":[]}]

name: snap up
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to grasp something quickly","examples":["Karen snapped her pencil up and strode out of the room.","Harry walked through the kitchen and snapped up two cookies on the way."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to purchase something quickly, because the price is low or because the item is so hard to find","examples":["We put the cheap shirts out for sale this morning and people snapped them up in only a few minutes. ","Shoppers came to the store to snap up bargains after the holidays.","They snapped up the bargains quickly.","The company is hiring. name: shore up
meanings: [{"name":"to stop a wall or a building from falling down by supporting it with building materials such as wood or metal","examples":["They shored up the roof/wall.","After the earthquake we had to shore up ceilings and walls.","Boundary walls have had to be shored up.","The fence fell over, so we shored it up with more posts. "],"media":[]},{"name":"to support or help (something); to make something stronger by supporting it","examples":["The tax cuts are supposed to shore up the economy.","Everyone co-operated to shore up John when his mother died.","The plan will enable his company to shore up its financial position.","India's central bank has spent an estimated $1-2 billion to shore the rupee up since April."],"media":[]}]

name: blow in
meanings: [{"name":"to arrive casually or unexpectedly; a person, usually from a city, who goes to live in a smaller town or village","examples":["It was late when we blew in from Detroit. ","What time did you blow in?","A lot of us were blow-ins from the big city."],"media":[]}]

name: smooth sailing / clear sailing
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. a situation where progress is made without any difficulty; easy progress without impediment or difficulty","examples":["Once you've passed that exam, it will be clear sailing to graduation.","Working there was not all smooth sailing. The boss had a very bad temper.","After the mix-up was rectified, it was smooth sailing again.","Katie, Look, I know things haven't been smooth sailing between us."],"media":[]}]

name: on speaking terms
meanings: [{"name":"friendly enough to talk; friendly and willing to speak to each other; on friendly terms with someone. (Often with the negative.)","examples":["They're not on speaking terms.","Are we even on speaking terms, Kate?","I'm not on speaking terms with Mary. We had a serious disagreement.","We had an argument, but we're back on speaking terms now."],"media":[]}]

name: strike down
meanings: [{"name":"[for a court] to invalidate a ruling or law; to declare (a law) illegal and unenforceable; annul; nullify","examples":["The board struck down the appointment.","The higher court struck the ruling of the lower court down.","The Supreme Court struck down the law."],"media":[]},{"name":"to knock someone or something down by striking","examples":["Max struck Lefty down with one blow.","He struck down the weeds with a scythe."],"media":[]}]

name: make amends
meanings: [{"name":"to do something to correct a mistake that one has made or a bad situation that one has caused; to make up to someone for something that someone or something did","examples":["She tried to make amends by apologizing to him.","I'd like to make amends (to you) for my behavior last night.","Don't worry. I will make amends to her for my sister, who behaved so badly.","I can make amends to Sam, I'm sure."],"media":[]}]

name: cut someone down
meanings: [{"name":"to kill someone with a weapon, such as a sword, or with gunfire, etc.","examples":["The bandits cut the bystanders down and fled. ","The gunman cut down an innocent pedestrian."],"media":[]}]

name: to the bone
meanings: [{"name":"very much","examples":["We were frozen to the bone.","I was frozen/chilled to the bone after waiting so long for the bus.","Our budget is bled to the bone. We simply don't have the money.","He's working himself to the bone."],"media":[]},{"name":"as much as possible","examples":["The company has cut costs to the bone in an effort to save money."],"media":[]}]

name: chilled to the bone
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. very cold","examples":["I got chilled to the bone in that snowstorm.","The children were chilled to the bone from their swim in the ocean."],"media":[]}]

name: on the verge of
meanings: [{"name":"at the point when (something) is about to happen or is very likely to happen; at the very beginning of doing something; just about to do something","examples":["The company was on the verge of going bankrupt.","The child was on the verge of tears.","Bill was on the verge of leaving town when he found a job.","Susan was on the verge of laughter, so she left the lecture hall."],"media":[]}]

name: plain as day / plain as a pikestaff
meanings: [{"name":"very obvious; very plain and simple","examples":["The answer is (as) plain as day.","Although his face was as plain as day, his smile made him look interesting and friendly.","Fred: I have a suspicion that Marcia is upset with me. \nAlan: A suspicion? name: see to it
meanings: [{"name":"to make sure that something is done","examples":["Can you see to it that everyone gets a copy of this memo?"],"media":[]}]

name: in place
meanings: [{"name":"in an original or proper position; If something is in place, it is in its usual or correct position","examples":["The chairs are all in place.","Her hair was held in place with a scarf.","The maid came into the room and put everything into place.","It's good to see everything in place again."],"media":[]},{"name":"established, instituted, or operational; organized","examples":["The arrangements are all in place for the concert next Thursday.","The vaccination program is not yet in place.","There is a plan in place to get aid to the regions that need it.","They quickly put a range of safety measures in place."],"media":[]},{"name":"in the same spot without forward or backward movement","examples":["She looked like she was running in place as six women flew past her.","It was so difficult to run in the sand, he felt like he was running in place at times.","They warmed up by running in place.","They were jumping up and down in place."],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"to watch, observe, or check (something) for a special purpose over a period of time; to monitor someone or something; to observe someone or something","examples":["We are continuing to keep watch on developments in the region.","Keep close watch on Bill. name: slug it out
meanings: [{"name":"to fight or compete over something until one side wins; to fight something out; to argue intensely about something","examples":["The companies are slugging it out in court.","They finally went outside to slug it out.","We'll just have to sit down in the conference room and slug it out."],"media":[]}]

name: a means to an end

name: music to someone's ears
meanings: [{"name":"something that someone is very happy to hear; news that someone is pleased to hear","examples":["Her words were music to my ears.","When she said they would make a profit, it was music to Richard's ears.","Jane: Here's your paycheck for this month. Bob: Ah, that's music to my ears!"],"media":[]}]

name: a mile a minute
meanings: [{"name":"very fast; with great speed","examples":["Mike was very excited, talking a mile a minute.","She talks a mile a minute and is very hard to keep up with.","You are running around a mile a minute."],"media":[]}]

name: pray tell
meanings: [{"name":"used for emphasis to demand an answer when asking someone for a reason, explanation, etc.","examples":["Why should I trust them, pray tell?","What were you doing, pray tell?"],"media":[]}]

name: leave behind something/someone
meanings: [{"name":"to go away and not take something or someone with you","examples":["The flood victims were forced to leave behind family photos and mementos.","He left behind a wife and six-year-old twin boys (= He died but they are still living).","He was forced to leave the country, leaving behind his wife and children.","We left in a hurry and I must have left my keys behind."],"media":[]}]

name: sock away
meanings: [{"name":"to put away (money) as savings or investment; to save money by putting it in a bank or by investing it (= giving it to companies hoping to get more back); to store something in a secure place","examples":["He's socked away hundreds of dollars in a savings account.","I try to sock a little money away each month for my vacation.","I will sock away some money."],"media":[]}]

name: on the line
meanings: [{"name":"at great risk; at risk of failing or being harmed","examples":["His job is on the line.","Firefighters regularly put their lives on the line.","What? Is someone on the line?","Please stay on the line. Your call is very important to us."],"media":[]}]

name: call out
meanings: [{"name":"to speak loudly; to speak loudly to get someone's attention","examples":["Speak up – call the names out so we can all hear.","He called out, but she didn't hear him.","Mike called out to Tom that there was a telephone call for him.","I heard someone call out, but I could see no one.","Who called the warning out?","Don't just call the answers out - raise your hand.","Someone in the crowd called out his name."],"media":[]},{"name":"to ask someone to come in order to do a job, especially when it is an emergency; to request the services of someone or a group","examples":["We had to call out a doctor.","The government called the army out to deal with violent disorder on the streets."],"media":[]},{"name":"to challenge someone to a fight; to challenge to a duel","examples":["Wilbur wanted to call him out, but thought better of it","Why did you call out that guy? name: take a stand
meanings: [{"name":"to express one's opinion; to express and maintain a strong opinion of something","examples":["It's time for you to take a stand and tell them that things need to change.","I hope you take a firm stand on the need for more office security.","There's a risk of taking a stand too early. That's all I'm saying.","The treasurer was forced to take a stand against the board because of its wasteful spending"],"media":[]}]

name: come up with
meanings: [{"name":"to produce especially in dealing with a problem or challenge; to suggest or think of an idea or plan","examples":["He came up with a great idea for the ad campaign.","She came up with a solution.","Next you need to come up with a name for your product."],"media":[]},{"name":"to manage to find or produce something that is needed, usually money","examples":["They gave him 30 days to come up with the money he owed.","Where am I supposed to come up with a million dollars?","Investigators have come up with what may be crucial evidence.","Half a million is a lot to come up with.","My mom is always able to come up with some yummy snack for me in the afternoon."],"media":[]}]

name: among friends
meanings: [{"name":"surrounded by people who are one's friends and are not threatening in any way","examples":["Relax. You're among friends here and can speak freely.","Jane: All right, you're next, Kate. You sing? Kate: Only when I'm alone. Jane: We're among friends. Kate: I don't think so.\n","Jane convinced them to come celebrate among friends."],"media":[]}]

name: pay homage to
meanings: [{"name":"to honor; to openly honor or worship someone or something","examples":["Her paintings pay homage to women artists of the past.","On this occasion we pay homage to him for his achievements.","We pay homage to him for his achievements in medical research.","Do you expect me to pay homage to your hero?","I refuse to pay homage to your principles."],"media":[]}]

name: play along (with someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to pretend to cooperate with someone or something in a joke, scam, etc.; to agree to do or accept what other people want; to do what someone asks you to do, for a limited period of time","examples":["They wanted me to cooperate with them, but I refused to play along with their plan.","I decided that I would play along with Larry for a while and see what would happen.","I don't think I want to play along.","All right. I will play along."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to play a musical instrument with someone or a group","examples":["The violinist sat down and began to play along with the others.","Do you mind if I play along?"],"media":[]}]

name: pay a visit to
meanings: [{"name":"to visit a person or place, usually for a short time; to go somewhere to spend time with (someone, such as a friend or relative)","examples":["He paid a visit to his parents.","We thought we'd pay a visit to the museum while we were in Lisbon.","Why don't you pay us a visit next time you're in town?","I think the police may pay him a visit later today."],"media":[]}]

name: pull the plug
meanings: [{"name":"to stop something from continuing; to put an end to someone's activities or plans; to do something that prevents an activity from continuing, especially by no longer giving money to support it","examples":["The network pulled the plug on the show after three weeks.","If the viewing figures drop much more, the TV network will probably pull the plug on the whole series.","The mayor was doing a fine job until the treasurer pulled the plug on him. ","David pulled the plug on Fred, who was taking too long with the project."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to turn off someone's life-support system in a hospital","examples":["Fred signed a living will making it possible to pull the plug on him without a court order.","They had to get a court order to pull the plug on their father."],"media":[]}]

name: cut a rug
meanings: [{"name":"to dance, especially in an energetic way","examples":["He's not young anymore, but he can still cut a rug on the dance floor.","Within minutes, most of the crowd was cutting a rug.","Can you cut a rug?"],"media":[]}]

name: tale of woe
meanings: [{"name":"a sad story; a list of personal problems; an excuse for failing to do something","examples":["She listened to his tale of woe without saying anything.","All right. Come on in. Tell me your tale of woe.","This tale of woe that we have all been getting from Kelly is just too much."],"media":[]}]

name: trip the light fantastic
meanings: [{"name":"to dance","examples":["Shall we go trip the light fantastic?","You can trip the light fantastic."],"media":[]}]

name: beg the question
meanings: [{"name":"to elicit a question logically as a reaction or response; to invite the (following) question; If a statement or situation begs the question, it causes you to ask a particular question","examples":["Spending the summer travelling around India is a great idea, but it does beg the question of how we can afford it.","To discuss the company's future begs the question of whether it has a future.","His complaints beg the question: Didn't he cause all of his problems himself ?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to carry on a false argument where one assumes as proved the very point that is being argued, or more loosely, to evade the issue at hand. ","A: Why do two lines that are equidistant from one another never meet? \nB: Because they are parallel. A: You are begging the question"],"media":[]}]

name: beg to differ
meanings: [{"name":"to politely disagree with someone; to disagree with someone; to state one's disagreement with someone in a polite way. (Usually used in a statement made to the person being disagreed with.)","examples":["I beg to differ with you, but you have stated everything exactly backwards. ","You say that the candidates are essentially the same, but I beg to differ."],"media":[]}]

name: of late
meanings: [{"name":"recently; lately","examples":["She has been sick of late.","We haven't spoken of late.","Have you seen Sally of late?","We haven't had an opportunity to eat out of late."],"media":[]}]

name: pony up
meanings: [{"name":"pay; to pay (a particular amount of money) for something; to pay (money) especially in settlement of an account","examples":["Despite having good credit, the couple still had to pony up a large down payment for the house.","You could be asked to pony up hundreds of dollars for a replacement.","Everybody owes seventy-five bucks. Kate's gonna kick me out unless I can pull my weight."],"media":[]}]

name: dog and pony show
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. a display, demonstration, or exhibition of something—such as something one is selling; an event that is designed to impress people in order to make them buy something or invest money","examples":["Our average customer is a businessperson who doesn't need the dog and pony show.","Gary went into his standard dog and pony show, trying to sell us on an upgrade to our software. ","Don't you get tired of running through the same old dog and pony show at every trade show?"],"media":[]}]
origin: As in a circus act where trained dogs leap onto and off of trained ponies.

name: jump through hoops
meanings: [{"name":"to do a lot of extra things, esp. silly or difficult things, to achieve something; to do everything possible to obey or please someone","examples":["We had to jump through a lot of hoops to get a loan from the bank.","It shouldn't be necessary to jump through hoops to get a computer to work properly.","We had to jump through hoops to get my Dad admitted to the hospital.","What do you want me to do— jump through a hoop?","She expects us to jump through hoops for her."],"media":[]}]

name: not that one knows of / not that I know of
meanings: [{"name":"used in answer to a question to say that someone thinks the answer is no; used when answering a question to mean that, judging from the information you have, the answer is no","examples":["\"Do they have relatives nearby?\" \"Not that they know of.\"","\"Did he leave already?\" \"Not that I know of.\"","\"Is she especially unhappy at school?\" \"Not that I know of.\""],"media":[]}]

name: do over
meanings: [{"name":"to do something again because you did not do it well the first time; to repeat something; to do something again","examples":["The teacher told him to do the assignment over.","Art, unlike life, permits do-overs: the illusion that one can get things right with craft and persistence.","Would you do this one over, please?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to decorate a room or part of a house in a new way; to rebuild, redesign, or redecorate something","examples":["We plan to do over the kitchen next year.","We did our living room over for the holidays","We made over the family room because it was looking shabby. "],"media":[]}]

name: have it made in the shade
meanings: [{"name":"to have a very easy life or to be in a very good situation; to have succeeded; to be set for life","examples":["She had to work hard for many years to achieve success, but now she has it made in the shade.","Wow, is he lucky! name: pipe dream
meanings: [{"name":"an idea or plan that is not practical or possible; a wish or an idea that is impossible to achieve or carry out","examples":["Many people still believe that traveling to Mars is just a pipe dream.","Your hopes of winning a lot of money are just a silly pipe dream.","Her plans are not realistic - they'll never be more than a pipe dream."],"media":[]}]

name: to death
meanings: [{"name":"a lot; excessively; beyond endurance","examples":["The movie scared the kids to death.","I am sick to death of hearing your excuses."],"media":[]},{"name":"until you die","examples":["The animals burned to death in the barn.","He choked to death on a fish bone.","He was dragged out of his car and beaten to death."],"media":[]}]

name: give something a whirl / give it a whirl
meanings: [{"name":"attempt or try (something); try something for the first time","examples":["He thought he'd give acting a whirl.","I've never done cross-country skiing before, but I thought I'd give it a whirl this winter.","I've never danced salsa before but I'll give it a whirl.","This is a good idea. name: keep one's head

name: roll around

meanings: [{"name":"owing money for something; responsible for something; to owe money or be legally responsible for something","examples":["He's still on the hook for the cost of the repairs.","If the investment company fails, they are on the hook to pay the loan.","The cleanup plan called for the companies, which are on the hook for cleanup costs, to dredge contaminated sediments from the river."],"media":[]}]

name: eat up something

name: pass muster

","If you don't wear a jacket and tie, you won't pass muster at that fancy restaurant. They won't let you in."],"media":[]}]

name: pull/yank someone's chain
meanings: [{"name":"to deceive someone in a friendly or playful way; play a joke on someone; to harass someone; to give someone a hard time.","examples":["I thought he really won the lottery but he was only pulling my chain.","Stop yanking my chain!","Do you really think you can just yank my chain whenever you want?"],"media":[]}]

name: staff of life

name: play a part in something / play a role in something / have a part in something
meanings: [{"name":"be involved in something; be a factor in something; participate in something in a specific way; help to achieve something","examples":["Luck played an important part in their success.","I hope to play a part in the development of the new product.","I want to play a role in this procedure.","My thanks to everyone who has played a part in saving the hospital.","Did alcohol have a part in causing the accident?"],"media":[]},{"name":"portray a character in a performance","examples":["He played a part in The Merchant of Venice, but it was not a major role.","Larry wanted to play a role in the next play.","Can my client have a part in your movie?"],"media":[]}]

name: far and wide / far and near
meanings: [{"name":"in every direction; everywhere","examples":["We searched far and wide."],"media":[]}]

name: from far and near / from near and far / from far and wide
meanings: [{"name":"from distant places and from near places;: from many different places; from a large number of places; r from all around, both close by and farther away","examples":["People came from far and wide to see the parade.","People came from far and wide to see the house.","The inspiring curriculum draws students from far and wide.","All the young people from far and near gathered at the high school for the game.","The eagles gathered from near and far at the river where the salmon were spawning."],"media":[]}]

name: that said / having said that

name: may as well / might as well
meanings: [{"name":"used to suggest doing something, often when there is nothing better to do; a phrase indicating that it is probably better to do something than not to do it; used to say that something should be done or accepted because it cannot be avoided or because there is no good reason not to do it","examples":["You might as well tell them the truth.","We might as well walk there.","\"Should we start now?\" \"Might as well.\"","We may as well start the meeting - the others will be here soon.","Bill: Should we try to get there for the first showing of the film? \nJane: Might as well. name: fess up (to something)
meanings: [{"name":"confess; to admit that one has done something wrong; to admit that you have done something that someone else will not like","examples":["At first he denied everything, but eventually he fessed up.","He finally fessed up about his involvement.","Fess up - it was you who ate that last piece of cake, wasn't it?","I tried to get the boy to fess up to doing it, but he wouldn't do it. name: none the

name: muddy the waters

name: meet halfway
meanings: [{"name":"to compromise with; to agree to do part of what someone wants if that person will do part of what you want","examples":["The senators met halfway on an energy bill.","We can't give you everything you've requested, but we can meet you halfway.","Can you meet us halfway on this? = Can we meet halfway on this?","The buyers wanted to bring the price down from $15,000 to $10,000, so I offered to meet them halfway at $12,500."],"media":[]}]

name: doll up

"],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"near in time or place; within reach","examples":["You should use whatever ingredients are at hand.","We want to ensure that help is at hand (= easily available) for all children suffering abuse."],"media":[]},{"name":"happening or present at this time; currently receiving or deserving attention; the topic under discussion","examples":["The space shuttle crew must stay completely focused on the task at hand.","The business at hand.","We've somehow gotten off the topic. name: redeem oneself
meanings: [{"name":"to succeed or do something good after one has failed or done something bad","examples":["They can redeem themselves for yesterday's loss by winning today's game.","After his poor performance in the golf tournament two weeks before, he was determined to redeem himself by playing well."],"media":[]}]

name: anything but

meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to leave someone stunned or surprised by something extraordinary. (Fixed order.)","examples":["I was so surprised that you could have knocked me over with a feather.","Todd could have knocked me over with a feather when he told me his news."],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"to make (someone or something) sad, depressed, or worried; If a problem or responsibility weighs on you, it makes you worried or unhappy","examples":["The bad news is really weighing on me.","I can tell that something is weighing on his mind.","He's under huge pressure at work and it's really weighing on him.","She knew she had been unfair to him and it weighed heavily on her mind for a long time."],"media":[]},{"name":"to cause problems for something such as a market or share, usually causing it to fall","examples":["Worries about a weak dollar weighed heavily on Wall Street, which suffered further losses yesterday.","Signs of sluggish economic growth weighed on banks."],"media":[]}]

What's this? A new car?","Holy cow! That car almost ran into us!"],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"Wow!; used to express surprise, amazement, or bewilderment; used to show that you think something is surprising, shocking, or impressive","examples":["Holy moley! name: go on hiatus

name: on one's hands
meanings: [{"name":"in one's possession or care","examples":["I've too much time on my hands.","We have a crisis on our hands."],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"to lower the body to the ground by bending the legs; to sit down on your heels; to sit with your knees bent in front of you so that your buttocks are almost resting on your heels","examples":["The hikers hunkered down under a cliff until the storm passed.","We hunkered down near the campfire."],"media":[]},{"name":"to stay in a place for a period of time; To hunker down is also to be prepared to stay in a particular place or situation for as long as necessary, esp. for protection or to achieve something; to focus on work; to get ready to work hard, often involving a long period of time","examples":["The leaders hunkered down at a country estate for difficult peace negotiations.","Members of Congress were hunkered down for weeks of debate on the health-care issue.","If you're going to finish that report by Monday morning, you'd better hunker down over the weekend.","There's going to be a blizzard tonight. meanings: [{"name":"Lit. come or move nearer or closer to (someone or something)","examples":["The fire was closing in on their neighborhood.","The camera slowly closed in on the actor's face.","Police were closing in on the two men.","They closed in quietly and trapped the bear."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. [for threats or negative feelings] overwhelm or seem to surround someone or something","examples":["My problems are closing in on me.","I feel trapped. extraDetails: [["\"Close in on\" vs. \"Close on\"",["\"Close in on\": Focuses on the process of approaching a target, often physically or metaphorically surrounding it (e.g., \"Police closed in on the bank\").","\"Close on\": Often means to finalize a deal or to be nearly equal to something in a race or competition (e.g., \"They hope to close on the house tomorrow\" or \"The runner is closing on the leader\")."]]]

name: by the looks of it or someone / from the looks of it or someone

[{"name":"relax and avoid hard work or strain","examples":["The doctor told her she should take it easy for a while."],"media":[]},{"name":"stay or become calm and unexcited —usually used as a command","examples":["Take it easy, Jane.
