meanings: [{"name":"for public knowledge; on the record; so that (one's own version of ) the facts will be known; something that you say before you tell someone something important that you want them to remember","examples":["And, just for the record, we were never any more than good friends.","For the record, I've never been able to get any thing done around city hall without bribing someone.","For the record, I received no payment for the work.","We met in 2006, not 2004, just for the record."],"media":[]}]

name: long gone
meanings: [{"name":"having ended, died, disappeared, etc., at a distant time in the past; used up a long time ago; gone a long time ago","examples":["Those buildings are long gone now.","Any forensic evidence is long gone.","The ice cream and cake are long gone. You are simply too late for the refreshments.","I thought you'd be long gone by now."],"media":[]}]

name: iffy
meanings: [{"name":"uncertain","examples":["Our plans are iffy.","Bob starts to feel a little iffy.","Frank and Alice asked me to babysit their babies. I'm nervous. I've never done that. I'm gonna pass, because I was kind of iffy when it was puppies."],"media":[]}]

name: mend fences / mend one's fences
meanings: [{"name":"to improve or repair a relationship that has been damaged by an argument or disagreement; to restore good relations (with someone); to try to be friendly again with someone after an argument","examples":["She mended fences with her father.","She and her father are trying to mend their fences.","Sally called up her uncle to apologize and try to mend fences."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to repair fences as part of one's chores","examples":["Tom is mending fences today at the south end of the ranch."],"media":[]}]

name: have a word with someone (about something)
meanings: [{"name":"to talk with someone briefly","examples":["Can I have a word with you about your report?","Could I have a word with you?","Bob: Can I have a word with you? \nSally: Sure. I'll be with you in a minute.","Sally: Tom? Tom: Yes.\nSally: I'd like to have a word with you. Tom: Okay. What's it about?"],"media":[]}]

name: fond of
meanings: [{"name":"to like someone or something very much","examples":["I'm fond of chocolate.","Mary isn't fond of me, but I'm fond of her.","He's very fond of his little dog.","I've always been fond of flowers, so I'm delighted that the new house has a little garden."],"media":[]},{"name":"doing (something) a lot; to like doing something; to do something often","examples":["I'm fond of swimming.","She's fond of asking silly questions.","My brother is fond of pointing out my mistakes.","He was rather fond of swimming when he was younger.","I'm so fond of knitting that I attend wool festivals in Shetland."],"media":[]}]

name: follow through / carry through
meanings: [{"name":"to complete an activity, doing what was promised; to continue something until it is completed; to bring to a successful end","examples":["I wish you would follow through with the project we talked about.","You never follow through!","Don't start the job if you can't follow through.","We are determined to carry our plans through to completion."],"media":[]}]

name: force of habit
meanings: [{"name":"owing to a tendency to do something that has become a habit; If you do something out of force of habit, you do it without thinking because you have done it so many times before","examples":["I just locked the door through force of habit, not thinking that Julia wouldn't be able to get in.","I called him 'Jimmy' out of force of habit.","I bow my head before meals just from force of habit - it doesn't mean anything.","After I retired, I kept getting up and getting dressed each morning by force of habit."],"media":[]}]

name: cast the first stone
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to make the first criticism; to be the first to attack","examples":["Well, I don't want to be the one to cast the first stone, but she sang horribly.","John always casts the first stone. Does he think he's perfect?"],"media":[]}]

name: rise to the occasion / rise to the challenge
meanings: [{"name":"to make the special effort that is required to successfully deal with a difficult situation; to meet the challenge of an event; to try extra hard to do a task","examples":["No one was sure if he could handle the pressure of making a speech, but he rose to the occasion and did an excellent job.","When the company needed to increase its sales, its employees rose to the challenge."," It was a big challenge, but he rose to the occasion.","We were not able to rise to the challenge and we lost the contract."],"media":[]}]

name: in terms of something
meanings: [{"name":"in relation to; with respect to; regarding something; concerning something","examples":["He thinks of everything in terms of money.","We try to do what is best for our customers in terms of the quality of our products.","I don't know what to do in terms of John's problem.","Now, in terms of your proposal, don't you think you're asking for too much?"],"media":[]}]

name: forgive and forget
meanings: [{"name":"Prov. You should not only forgive people for hurting you, you should also forget that they ever hurt you.","examples":["We had to learn to forgive and forget.","It's time to forgive and forget.","Sadly, not everyone is willing to forgive and forget.","It seems that voters are in no mood to forgive and forget."],"media":[]}]

name: back and forth
meanings: [{"name":"backward and forward; in one direction and then the other repeatedly; from one place to another repeatedly","examples":["The chair rocked back and forth.","The children were shuttled back and forth between school and home.","We tossed the ball back and forth between us.","The tiger paced back and forth in its cage."],"media":[]},{"name":"repeatedly changing one's mind about something; having trouble settling on an opinion or decision","examples":["Should we change our company health care plan? I can't make up my mind. I go back and forth on the issue.","There are pros and cons to moving it to China. I've been back and forth on this issue for months."],"media":[]}]

name: mean something (to someone)
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to make sense to someone","examples":["Does this line mean anything to you?","a dark sky means rain."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. [for someone] to cause important emotional feelings in another person; to have an important emotional effect on someone","examples":["You mean a lot to me. ","This job means a lot to Ann.","Her children mean all the world to her.","Jane means nothing to me now."],"media":[]}]

name: meant to (be/do something) / mean to (do something)
meanings: [{"name":"intended to (do or be something)","examples":["I was never meant to teach.","These batteries are meant to last for a year.","You are meant to rub the medicine on the affected area.","He went to India for what was meant to have been a 10-day visit.","Did you mean to do that?","No, it was an accident. I didn't mean to."],"media":[]}]

name: catch something
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to see or listen to something","examples":["I will try to catch that new movie this weekend.","Did you catch that radio program about robots last night?","I've to catch a game on TV."],"media":[]}]

name: I didn't (quite) catch that (last) remark / I didn't get that / I didn't hear you
meanings: [{"name":"I didn't hear what you said, so would you please repeat it.","examples":["John: What did you say? I didn't quite catch that last remark. \nJane: I said it's really a hot day.","Bill: Have a nice time, if you can. \nSally: I didn't get that. Bill: Have a nice time! Enjoy!"],"media":[]}]

name: put/set something in motion
meanings: [{"name":"to start a machine or process; to begin (something, such as a plan or process); to start something moving","examples":["The mayor set the project in motion by digging the first shovelful of soil. ","I cannot set the procedure in motion until I receive a purchase order.","We filled in a form to set the whole process in motion.","Once the printing processes have been put in motion, they're not so easy to stop."],"media":[]}]

name: oneself again
meanings: [{"name":"showing signs of being healthy again or restored","examples":["After such a long illness, it's good to be myself again.","I'm sorry that I lost my temper. I think I feel like myself again now.","I'm feeling like my old self again."],"media":[]}]
origin: Typically: act like ~; be ~; feel like ~; seem like ~.

name: ups and downs
meanings: [{"name":"good and bad things that happen to someone or something during a period; alternating rise and fall especially in fortune","examples":["All people have their ups and downs.","I've had my ups and downs, but in general life has been good to me","Like most married couples we've had our ups and downs, but life's like that."],"media":[]}]

name: walk in the park
meanings: [{"name":"an easy or pleasurable experience; something that is very easy to do, and usually pleasant","examples":["He's used to hard physical work - this is a walk in the park to him.","This is no walk in the park for him either, you know.","“Is it difficult to surf the net?” six-year-old Tommy asked of his twelve-year-old brother. “No, not at all, it's a walk in the park.”"],"media":[]}]

name: just because
meanings: [{"name":"for the simple or single reason that","examples":["Don't get nervous just because the teacher might ask you a question.","Just because your friends do it, that doesn't mean that you should do it, too.","Just because I didn't show up, didn't mean I didn't care. I did. And I still do.","But you can't give him stuff just because he says he wants it."],"media":[]}]

name: God forbid
meanings: [{"name":"I hope this does not happen; used in speech to say that one hopes a bad thing will not happen","examples":["This is the number you should call if, God forbid, you should get into an accident.","God forbid that something bad should happen.","If there was a fire, God forbid, we'd be able to respond to the disaster.","God forbid (that) his parents should ever find out."],"media":[]}]

name: toss aside someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to throw someone or something aside or out of the way; to throw away or get rid of something","examples":["The kidnapper tossed the child aside and reached for his gun.","The soldier tossed aside the helpless civilian and ran into the house.","Fred tossed the can aside and Alice picked it up."],"media":[]}]

name: for some reason / for whatever reason
meanings: [{"name":"used to say it isn't known why someone does something","examples":["He is always late, for some/whatever reason.","But, for whatever reason, Sara doesn't see staying put as an option.","But for some reason, I'm here trying to help you.","He's keeping me in the dark for some reason."],"media":[]}]

name: spare no expense
meanings: [{"name":"to spend as much money as needed in order to make something as good as possible; ","examples":["When they go on vacation, they spare no expense.","They spared no expense in building the house."],"media":[]}]

name: bask in something
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to enjoy or revel in something, such as praise, fame, etc. (Alludes to a person or animal resting in the warming rays of the sun.); to take pleasure from something that makes you feel good","examples":["He basked in his moment of glory, holding the trophy up to the crowd.","Alice enjoyed basking in her newfound fame.","Lily loves basking in praise.","Look, we spent a lot of money on that present. The least you can do is open it so we can bask in your happy expression.","He stood before the audience, basking in their applause."],"media":[]},{"name":"to lie or relax in a pleasant warmth or atmosphere","examples":["She's basking in the warmth of the sun.","We sat basking in the sun.","Tourists were basking on the beaches."],"media":[]}]

name: hit up
meanings: [{"name":"to ask (someone) for something (such as money); to ask someone for a loan of money or for some other favor","examples":["She's waiting for the right moment to hit up her father for a loan.","I donated money to that charity a few months ago, and they're already hitting me up for more.","The tramp hit up each tourist for a dollar.","My brother hit up Harry for a couple of hundred bucks."],"media":[]}]

name: measure up (to someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"to be the equal (as in ability); to be good enough, or as good as someone or something else; to compare well to someone or something","examples":["She could never measure up to her mother's expectations.","He just doesn't measure up to Sarah in intelligence.","This meal doesn't measure up to my expectations.","If new staff measure up after six months, they are offered a permanent contract.","Unfortunately, the production quality didn't measure up to our expectations."],"media":[]}]

name: all in one's head / all in one's head
meanings: [{"name":"in one's imagination; not real; existing only in one's imagination","examples":["The problem is all in his head.","Nobody cares about this except you. This embarrassment thing is all in your head.","Jane: This house is so quiet.\nKate: This is all in your head, Jane. This house ain't quiet.","He thinks he's very sick, but it's all in his mind."],"media":[]}]

name: add in(to)
meanings: [{"name":"to introduce something into something else","examples":["Now, add the eggs into the mixture. ","Add in some more eggs."],"media":[]}]

name: anything of the sort / something of the sort
meanings: [{"name":"something like the person or thing mentioned; something of the kind just mentioned","examples":["I'd like to go to a movie or a concert, or something of the sort.","The tree isn't exactly a spruce tree, just something of the sort.","Jane has a cold or something of the sort.","He said I hung up on him, but I never did anything of the kind!","This technology is completely new. I've never seen anything of the kind before."],"media":[]}]

name: make someone look good
meanings: [{"name":"to cause someone to appear successful or competent (especially when this is not the case)","examples":["John arranges all his affairs to make himself look good.","The manager didn't like the quarterly report because it didn't make her look good.","Jane: You want me to lie? Make you look good?\nKate: I actually don't want anything of the sort."],"media":[]}]

name: from the get-go
meanings: [{"name":"from the very beginning","examples":["She didn't like me from the get-go.","The latest research shows that babies can be taught the difference between night and day from the get-go.","That trashy girl has been lying to us from the get-go."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782491685/phrases/j4hvluwe2hmcae4tkd7n.mp4","publicId":"phrases/j4hvluwe2hmcae4tkd7n","type":"video"},{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782491694/phrases/ihwlwgtitnpfgcsykjsj.mp4","publicId":"phrases/ihwlwgtitnpfgcsykjsj","type":"video"}]}]

name: drag into
meanings: [{"name":"to involve (a person, group, etc.) in (a difficult or complicated situation)","examples":["I'm sorry for dragging you into this.","I don't know why I have to get dragged into this.","Please don't drag me into your argument.","It is a serious dispute, and please don't drag me in."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to haul or pull someone or something into something or some place","examples":["She dragged in the child to make him put on this jacket.","Despite his broken leg, he dragged himself into the shelter."],"media":[]}]

name: hell of a / one hell of a
meanings: [{"name":"used to make a statement more forceful","examples":["It was one hell of a good fight.","He is one hell of a nice guy."],"media":[]},{"name":"very good","examples":["She's a hell of a player.","Jane: Well, I don't like to brag, but I am famous for my orange-glazed muffins.\nTom: Yeah. Bob said that you were one hell of a baker."],"media":[]},{"name":"very bad or difficult","examples":["We've been having a hell of a time trying to finish on schedule.","This is a hell of a mess we're in.","Well, I'm guessing you must be having one hell of a bad day, huh?"],"media":[]}]

name: take matters into one's own hands
meanings: [{"name":"to do something oneself instead of waiting for other people to do something; to deal with a problem yourself because the people who should have dealt with it have failed to do so","examples":["When the police failed to catch the thief, she decided to take matters into her own hands."],"media":[]}]

name: call off
meanings: [{"name":"cancel; divert","examples":["She was about to tell me the big news when her attention was called off by the arrival of another guest.","They called off the party after half of those invited couldn't make it.","Tomorrow's match has been called off because of the icy weather.","It's too late to call the party off. The first guests have already arrived."],"media":[]},{"name":"to request that someone or an animal stop bothering or pursuing someone or something; to call a halt to an attack by someone or an animal","examples":["I shouted to him to call his dog off, but he just laughed at me.","Call off your thugs, and I'll show you where the money is."],"media":[]}]

name: the ball is in one's court
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to be someone else's move, play, or turn. (From tennis.); burdened with expectations or requirements for something","examples":["What do you think we should do about the project? The ball is in your court.","It's up to you what to do - the ball is in your court now.","I can't do anything as long as the ball is in John's court.","John put the ball in Jane's court."],"media":[]}]

name: just as
meanings: [{"name":"to an equal degree as","examples":["Our house is just as nice as theirs.","This one is just as good as that one.","She performs just as well as he does."],"media":[]},{"name":"in the same way as","examples":["Just as we hope to be forgiven, so we should forgive others.","Just as I thought/suspected, the door is locked."],"media":[]}]

name: just as well
meanings: [{"name":"it is a good thing; good even if not expected or intended","examples":["It's beginning to rain - it's just as well that we brought our umbrellas.","It's just as well she didn't get that job, since she will now be closer to home.","I really didn't want to stay home this weekend, but it's just as well. I have a lot to do."],"media":[]}]

name: (to do) whatever it takes
meanings: [{"name":"(to do) all that is necessary","examples":["I am ready to do whatever it takes. Just tell me the necessary action and I'll do it.","If you want to remake yourself, you have to do whatever it takes.","We're gonna put this family back together. Whatever it takes.","I'll do whatever it takes to stay in the company."],"media":[]}]

name: tug at someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to pull at someone or something","examples":["Stop tugging at me! I'll talk to you in a minute.","The dog tugged at my pants cuff."],"media":[]}]

name: tug at one's heartstrings / pull at one's heartstrings
meanings: [{"name":"to stir one's emotions; to cause strong feelings of love or sympathy","examples":["That movie really tugs/pulls at your heartstrings.","It's the story of a lost child - guaranteed to tug at the heartstrings.","Oh, well, your concern for my social standing really tugs at my heartstrings."],"media":[]}]

name: blow one's mind
meanings: [{"name":"to overwhelm one with wonder or bafflement; If something blows your mind, you find it very exciting and unusual","examples":["There was one scene in the film that really blew my mind.","The concert was so good, it blew my mind.","It was so beautiful, it nearly blew my mind."],"media":[]},{"name":"Sl. to disturb or distract; to destroy the function of one's brain","examples":["It was a terrible experience. It nearly blew my mind.","She blew her mind on drugs."],"media":[]}]

name: in the flesh
meanings: [{"name":"in person and alive; physically in front of you; bodily present; in person; totally real","examples":["I've seen her perform on television, but never in the flesh.","I've heard that the queen is coming here in the flesh.","I've wanted a flat-screen TV for years, and now I've got one right here in the flesh.","Wow, I can't believe I'm finally seeing the man himself in the flesh.","Jane: You must be Bob Smith?\nBob: In the flesh.\n"],"media":[]}]

name: do one's hair/nails/make-up
meanings: [{"name":"to do something that improves one's appearance","examples":["I have to do my hair now.","It must take her ages to do her make-up in the mornings.","Who does your hair?","Now, do you want me to do your make-up, or not?"],"media":[]}]

name: comb out
meanings: [{"name":"to make (hair) neat and smooth with a comb","examples":["She sat in front of the mirror combing out her hair."],"media":[]},{"name":"to smooth out (tangles in hair) with a comb; to remove substances or knots and snarls from something by combing","examples":["Her mother combed the tangles out.","I had to comb the gum out of her hair.","It took me over an hour to comb out the gum."],"media":[]}]

name: make something right / put something right / set something right / make something good
meanings: [{"name":"to correct something; to alter a situation to make it more fair","examples":["This is a very unfortunate situation. I'll ask the people responsible to set this matter right.","I'm sorry that we overcharged you. We'll try to put it right.","I know I owe you some money, but don't worry, I'll make it good.","I know I said some things I shouldn't have, so I'm here to make things right between us.","Well, there've been problems. It's my fault. I keep trying to make things right, but I don't know how.","Jane: I still don't want to talk to you.\nKate: Tell me how to make things right. I mess up, you tell me how to fix it and I do."],"media":[]}]

name: luck out
meanings: [{"name":"to have good luck; to be fortunate; to strike it lucky","examples":["We arrived late but we lucked out—there were still a few tickets left.","I really lucked out when I ordered the chicken curry. It's excellent.","I didn't luck out at all. I rarely make the right choice.","My wife lucked out – she left town just before the hurricane hit."],"media":[]}]

name: for someone's sake / for the sake of someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"for the purpose or benefit of someone or something; to satisfy the demands of someone or something; for someone's good or benefit; in honor of someone","examples":["I made a meatless dinner for John's sake; he's a vegetarian.","The teacher repeated the assignment for the sake of the slower students.","Let's not disagree for the sake of (= because of) a few dollars.","You're only arguing for the sake of arguing (= because you like arguing)."],"media":[]}]

name: come to terms (about/on someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"[for two or more people] to reach an accord on someone or something","examples":["Ed and Alice came to terms about money.","They did not come to terms on the price.","We finally managed to come to terms."],"media":[]}]

name: come to terms (with someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"to come to an agreement with someone; to reach an agreement with someone","examples":["I finally came to terms with my lawyer about his fee.","Bob, you have to come to terms with your father."],"media":[]},{"name":"to learn to accept someone or something; to become adjusted especially emotionally or intellectually","examples":["You have to come to terms with modern life.","She had to come to terms with the loss of her sight.","He made little effort to come to terms with his critics."],"media":[]}]

name: likewise
meanings:
[{"name":"in the same way or manner; similarly","examples":["We put up a fence, and other neighbors did likewise.","Just water these plants twice a week, and likewise the ones in the bedroom.",""I don't have time to spend hours preparing one dish!" "Likewise (= it's the same for me).""],"media":[]},{"name":"in addition","examples":["He is an acclaimed painter who is likewise a sculptor.","Bob is the owner of the restaurant is likewise the owner of the deli next door."],"media":[]},{"name":"similarly so with me (A hackneyed phrase said in greeting someone)","examples":["Jane: You must be Kate. Pleasure to meet you. 
Kate: Oh, likewise.","Alice: I'm delighted to make your acquaintance. 
Bob: Likewise, I'm sure.","John: How nice to see you!
Sue: Likewise. John: Where are you from, Sue?"],"media":[]}]

name: needless to say
meanings: [{"name":"obviously; It is so obvious that it doesn't need to be said, but....; as you would expect; added to, or used to introduce, a remark giving information that is expected and not surprising","examples":["Needless to say, because of the accident he won't be at work for a while.","Needless to say, I should have spent more time on the report, but I just didn't have it.","Needless to say, the agreement between us is off.","Needless to say, it didn't work out."],"media":[]}]

name: rage at someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to direct one's anger at someone or something","examples":["Why are you raging at me? What on earth did I do?","Nothing can be solved by raging at the police department.","He raged at (= spoke angrily to) us for forgetting to order a replacement."],"media":[]}]

name: go to great lengths / go to any lengths
meanings: [{"name":"to use a lot of effort to get or achieve something;  to work very hard to accomplish something; to expend great efforts in trying to do something","examples":["He went to extreme/great lengths to learn the truth.","Some people go to great lengths to make their homes attractive.","He'll go to any lengths to get what he wants.","I went to great lengths to explain to him that he was not in any trouble.","She'll go to any length(s) to avoid doing work."],"media":[]}]

name: go to waste
meanings: [{"name":"to be wasted; to not be used, eaten, etc.","examples":["Eat your potatoes! Don't let them go to waste.","Jane: You've got to eat something. Kate: I don't have an appetite.\nJane: In fact, this is all gonna go to waste.","It's not fair to say that all the money and hard work went to waste.","A lot of time and money have gone to waste because of a flawed design."],"media":[]}]

name: waste no time
meanings: [{"name":"to do something quickly; to immediately begin an activity","examples":["We wasted no time getting our tickets.","Caroline wasted no time in tackling her new responsibilities.","The board wasted no time in appointing a successor.","Well, you've certainly wasted no time welcoming Sam to the family."],"media":[]}]

name: waste one's breath
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to waste one's time talking; to talk in vain; to accomplish nothing by speaking; to say something that will likely be ignored; If you waste your breath, you spend time and energy trying to give advice that is ignored","examples":["Honestly, you're wasting your breath - he doesn't want to hear what anyone else has got to say.","Don't waste your breath arguing with him.","Don't waste your breath talking to her. She won't listen.","You can't persuade me. You're just wasting your breath."],"media":[]}]

name: waste of space
meanings: [{"name":"a person or thing that is not useful or helpful; a worthless person or thing","examples":["That man is a total waste of space.","The wrecked furniture in here is just a waste of space.","This broken-down car is a waste of space!"],"media":[]}]

name: waste away
meanings: [{"name":"(of a person or animal) to become thinner and weaker because of illness or lack of food","examples":["It was hard to watch her waste away.","You get thinner every time I see you, Sara - you're wasting away!","She's stopped eating, and I can't just stand by and watch her waste away."],"media":[]},{"name":"to use something up wastefully; to dissipate something; to wither or dwindle away","examples":["Our money just seemed to waste away.","He wasted all his money away and had to live in poverty.","They wasted away everything and regretted it later."],"media":[]}]

name: in all fairness / in fairness
meanings: [{"name":"considering everything that has an effect on a situation, so that a fair judgment can be made","examples":["In all fairness, he has been a hard worker.","In fairness to Diana, she has at least been honest with you.","He did poorly, but in (all) fairness [=to be fair to him], he was tired.","In all fairness, the results of the survey could have been different at another time.","Their new album is very weak, but in fairness, it's not all the singer's fault."],"media":[]}]

name: in all honesty
meanings: [{"name":"used to stress that a statement is true","examples":["In all honesty, I don't know what you're talking about.","I don't like him, but in all honesty, I don't know why.","In all honesty, I did go a little out of bounds."],"media":[]}]

name: scrape together
meanings: [{"name":"to get with great difficulty; to manage with great difficulty to collect enough of something, especially money, or to find the things or people that you need","examples":["We're barely scraping together a living on the farm.","He's trying to scrape together enough money to buy a computer."],"media":[]},{"name":"to gather things together by scraping","examples":["The waiter scraped all the crumbs together and removed them from the table with a little gadget.","Karen scraped together all the trimmings and set them aside."],"media":[]}]

name: a matter of
meanings: [{"name":"used to refer to a small amount","examples":["It cooks in a matter of (a few) minutes.","The crisis was resolved in a matter of a few hours.","The ball was foul by a matter of inches.","In a matter of seconds, the building was in flames."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that one thing results from or requires another","examples":["Learning to ride a bicycle is a matter of practice.","His success was just a matter of being in the right place at the right time.","It's only a matter of time before/until we catch him."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to explain the reason for something","examples":["She insists on honesty as a matter of principle.","All requests for free tickets are turned down as a matter of policy."],"media":[]}]

name: house of cards
meanings: [{"name":"a structure, situation, or institution that is insubstantial, shaky, or in constant danger of collapse; a complicated organization or plan that is very weak and can easily be destroyed or easily go wrong","examples":["He knows this place will go down like a house of cards without me.","I always knew your house of cards would collapse eventually,"],"media":[]}]

name: dig in(to something)
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to use a shovel to penetrate a mass of something","examples":["He dug into the soft soil and made a hole for the roots of the bush. ","He grabbed a shovel and dug in where he thought the tree ought to go."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to begin to process something; to go to work on something","examples":["I have to dig into all these applications today and process at least half of them.","Jed got out the stack of unanswered mail and dug in."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to begin to eat food","examples":["We dug into the huge pile of fried chicken.","I stuck the corner of my napkin in my collar and dug in."],"media":[]}]

extraDetails: [["Origin",["Aboard a ship, a boatswain's pipe, or whistle, is used to summon a crew or to relay orders."," The sounding of this instrument is referred to as piping. ","A crew would be \"piped\" to a meal, for example. ","To dismiss a crew, the boatswain's pipe is sounded and the command \"pipe down\" is given.","The \"pipe down\" signal specifically indicated that the day's duties were over and it was time for sailors to go below decks to sleep (\"turn in\").","Since this signal marked the time for silence and rest, the phrase evolved from a literal naval command into a general idiom for demanding quiet."]],["Usage",["It is commonly used in casual settings among friends, by parents to children, or by teachers in a classroom.","Unlike \"shut up,\" which strictly means \"stop talking,\" \"pipe down\" can imply either stopping completely or simply reducing the volume of noise. "]]]

","Do I have to twist your arm, or will you cooperate?"],"media":[]}]

meanings: [{"name":"getting better; improving; becoming healthy again","examples":["She's still in the hospital, but she's definitely on the mend.","I cared for my father while he was on the mend.","Jane: How's the arm? Kate: Uh, on the mend.","A marriage was on the mend."],"media":[]}]

name: in bad shape
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. injured or debilitated in any manner; in poor physical condition","examples":["Fred had a little accident, and he's in bad shape.","Tom needs exercise. He's in bad shape.","I was in bad shape back then.","I'm in bad shape. i was exhausted after running to catch the bus."],"media":[]}]

name: just what the doctor ordered
meanings: [{"name":"exactly what is wanted or needed, especially for health or comfort","examples":["A day at the beach was just what the doctor ordered.","Thanks, a strong cup of coffee in the morning is just what the doctor ordered.","That meal was delicious, Bob. Just what the doctor ordered.","Bob: Would you like something to drink? \nMary: Yes, a cold glass of water would be just what the doctor ordered."],"media":[]}]

name: recharge one's batteries
meanings: [{"name":"to rest and relax in order to regain energy and strength","examples":["We took a nap after work to recharge our batteries before going out dancing.","She took a trip to the South of France to recharge her batteries.","I get four weeks holiday a year to recharge my batteries."],"media":[]}]

name: the picture of health
meanings: [{"name":"very healthy","examples":["Jane: Lily looks amazing, doesn't she?\nKate: Yeah, she is the picture of health.","Each of the children is the picture of health.","The doctor says I am the picture of good health."],"media":[]}]

name: brush up
meanings: [{"name":"to improve one's knowledge of something or one's ability to do something; to renew one's skill; to refresh one's memory","examples":["I need to brush up my French.","I need to brush my French up a little bit.","My German is weak. I had better brush up.","I should brush up on math."],"media":[]}]

name: over someone's head
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. [of the intellectual content of something] too difficult for someone to understand","examples":["All that talk about computers went over my head.","I hope my lecture didn't go over the students' heads. "],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. to an authority higher than someone","examples":["I don't want to have to go over your head, but I will if necessary.","I had to go over Fran to get it done.","My boss wouldn't listen to my complaint, so I went above her."],"media":[]}]

name: know something inside out
meanings: [{"name":"know something completely","examples":["She knows the business inside out.","After 20 years of employment there, he has come to know the company inside out"],"media":[]}]

name: know something like the back of one's hand
meanings: [{"name":"to know something completely; to know something thoroughly, inside out","examples":["I know this town like the back of my hand.","John is a man-about-town; he knows London like the back of his hand.","I mean, he knows this job like the back of his hand."],"media":[]}]

name: by heart
meanings: [{"name":"by rote or from memory; exactly and from your memory","examples":["I think you know it by heart.","She baked muffins from recipes she knew by heart.","After all these years, I know that pre deployment checklist by heart.","I've heard the speech. I know it by heart."],"media":[]}]

name: scrape by
meanings: [{"name":"to live with barely enough money; to be able to buy only the things most needed","examples":["Money was tight, but we somehow managed to scrape by.","We're barely scraping by."],"media":[]},{"name":"to succeed at doing something but just barely","examples":["He didn't study for the exam and just barely scraped by."],"media":[]}]

name: state of the art / state-of-the-art
meanings: [{"name":"the best and most modern of its type; very modern and using the latest ideas and methods","examples":["The TV has all the newest technology and is considered state-of-the-art.","I spent two years developing this machine. It's absolutely state of the art.","Our university is known for its state-of-the-art facilities."],"media":[]}]

name: shop around
meanings: [{"name":"to look for the most suitable item or service for the lowest price; to compare the prices and quality of different things before deciding which one to buy","examples":["Did you shop around when you were looking for your car? Shop around first before you buy a car.","She is shopping around for a bank with low fees.","You can get good rates if you shop around on the internet."],"media":[]}]

name: bargain hunting
meanings: [{"name":"looking for a place to buy something at a price that is cheaper than usual","examples":["I think you better stop with the bargain hunting.","I'm not gonna blow this by bargain hunting.","Bob loves to go bargain hunting at his local market."],"media":[]}]

name: bargain basement
meanings: [{"name":"(of prices) extremely low, or (of products) of low quality; a section of a store (such as the basement) where merchandise is sold at reduced prices","examples":["Bob manages to buy all his clothes at bargain-basement prices (= very cheaply).","Throughout the trip we ate at bargain-basement restaurants in order to save money.","Farmers bought up the land at bargain-basement prices.","Act now if you want to buy bargain-basement shares."],"media":[]}]

name: retail therapy
meanings: [{"name":"the activity of going shopping in order to make yourself feel better when you are unhappy","examples":["She enjoyed a little retail therapy in  yesterday.","Jane: Kate, What are you wishing for?\nKate: When you asked me on this trip, you promised me retail therapy."],"media":[]}]

name: roll up one's sleeves
meanings: [{"name":"to prepare to work hard","examples":["It's time to roll up our sleeves and get the job done.","There's a lot of work to do, so roll up your sleeves and get busy.","We've planned everything – now it's time to roll up our sleeves and get started.","Jane rolled up her sleeves and got to work."],"media":[]},{"name":"Lit. to turn one's sleeves upward, exposing the arm; to fold up the ends of one's shirt sleeves to make them shorter","examples":["He rolled his sleeves up and began to wash the dishes","Don rolled up his sleeves so he would be cooler.","I rolled up my sleeves and began to wash the dishes."],"media":[]}]

name: roll up (into something)
meanings: [{"name":"to coil or rotate something into a coil or roll of something","examples":["I rolled the poster up and put it back in its mailing tube.","I have to roll up this paper."],"media":[]},{"name":"to make something into a round shape by rolling it.","examples":["He rolled the gum up into a ball and tossed it away.","Jane rolled up the dough into a ball."],"media":[]}]

name: take a breath
meanings: [{"name":"to pause and rest; have a short break and a rest","examples":["I've barely had time to (stop and/to) take a breath since they got here.","We stopped to take a breath before loading the rest of the boxes into the van."],"media":[]}]

name: stretch one's legs
meanings: [{"name":" to take a walk in order to relieve stiffness caused by prolonged sitting; to stand or walk after sitting for a long time","examples":["We drove there in five hours, including a couple of stops to stretch our legs.","We wanted to stretch our legs during intermission.","After sitting in the car all day, the travelers decided to stretch their legs."],"media":[]}]

name: on the run
meanings: [{"name":"in haste; without pausing; while walking or traveling; while one is moving from place to place","examples":["I was late for the office, so I had to eat breakfast on the run. ","He ate on the run, downing an apple in his car.","I will try to pick up some aspirin today on the run.","I will think about it on the run. "],"media":[]},{"name":"running from the police; in retreat; in flight (as from the law)","examples":["The escaped convict was on the run for three weeks before being caught by police.","Are you on the run from the mob?","You've been on the run 18 years, and you and your wife don't even exchange a phone call, huh?"],"media":[]}]

name: slowly but surely
meanings: [{"name":"slow but unstoppable; slow but definite progress —used to stress that something is happening or being done even though it is not happening or being done quickly","examples":["We're getting the work done, slowly but surely.","The doctors say I'll keep improving slowly but surely.","Nancy is finishing the paint job on her house, slowly but surely."],"media":[]}]

name: bend the rules
meanings: [{"name":"to change or ignore rules; relax the rules a little; to cheat a little bit without breaking the law","examples":["We cannot bend the rules just for you.","You've got to know when to bend the rules a little.","I didn't break the rules. I just bent the rules a little.","You can't bend the rules just once?"],"media":[]}]

name: big time / big-time
meanings: [{"name":"relating to someone or something that is famous or successful; the state of being famous or successful","examples":["Masha is a big-time real estate developer.","You've really made the big time now (= become famous or successful).","She finally hit the big time (= became famous or successful) with her latest novel."],"media":[]},{"name":"to a great extent or degree; in a major or large-scale way","examples":["I owe you big time. OK, bye.","I need you big time.","Kate: Are you in trouble? \nJane: Big time!"],"media":[]}]

name: work like a charm
meanings: [{"name":"to work very well; to produce a desired result very easily and effectively; very impressive","examples":["The cleaning fluid worked like a charm on the carpet stain.","You little speech to Kate worked like a charm.","Jane's presentation worked like a charm with the management. They loved the designs."],"media":[]}]

name: The gloves are off
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. There is going to be a serious fight, dispute or competition. (As if boxers had removed their gloves in order to inflict more damage.)","examples":["We've played it by their rules so far, but now the gloves are off.","Bob got mad and yelled, “Ok, the gloves are off!” and started cussing and pounding the table.","Now, the gloves are off between the two presidential candidates. "],"media":[]}]

name: ball game / ballgame
meanings: [{"name":"situation; a set of circumstances","examples":["Driving in Australia is a different ball game.","We'd done a lot of climbing in Switzerland but the Himalayas were a whole new ballgame."],"media":[]}]

name: per se
meanings: [{"name":"as such; by itself; of itself; in itself; intrinsically","examples":["It is not a pretty town per se, but it is where my family comes from, so I like it.","I wouldn't say there's a villain, per se.","I'm not saying you're overreacting per se.","Don't get me wrong. I'm not against environmental issues, per se.","Jane: Is there a problem with Bob?\nKate: Not a problem, per se.","I have no objection to educational testing per se, but rather to the way testing is done.","When the police chief decided to crack down on small crimes, it wasn't the small crimes per se that were his target, but instead the larger crimes which he believed would be reduced because of this new approach.","I don't dislike meetings per se, but I find many of them unproductive.","The movie wasn't bad per se, but it lacked originality."],"media":[]}]
origin: We generally use per se to distinguish between something in its narrow sense and some larger thing that it represents.

name: come first
meanings: [{"name":"to be more important than something else; to be the most important person or thing to someone","examples":["He cares about his job, but his family comes first.","Her family will always come first with her."],"media":[]}]

name: come in first, second, etc
meanings: [{"name":"to finish a race in first, second, etc. position","examples":["Kate came in second in the 100 metres.","She came in fourth overall but posted her best time yet.","The horse was favoured to win, but thanks to jockey error came in dead last."],"media":[]}]

name: come to the rescue / go to the rescue
meanings: [{"name":"to rescue; to save (someone or something) from danger or harm","examples":["The policeman came/went to the rescue of the lost boy.","We were stranded on the rocks until lifeguards came to the rescue."],"media":[]}]

name: pay one's way / pay one's own way
meanings: [{"name":"to pay one's share of expenses; contribute toward the cost of something; to pay for one's own transportation, entrance fees, tickets, room, board, etc","examples":["She took a part-time job to pay her own way through college.","I wanted to go to Florida this spring, but my parents say I have to pay my own way.","I live with my parents but I pay my way by buying groceries."],"media":[]}]

name: bear a grudge / have a grudge / hold a grudge (against someone)
meanings: [{"name":"to continue feeling an old resentment for someone; to harbor continual anger for someone","examples":["I don't bear any grudge against you.","I have a grudge against my landlord for not fixing the leaky faucet.","Amanda still holds a grudge against me for refusing to lend her that money.","The message was clearly posted by someone with a grudge against the company."],"media":[]}]

name: catch a glimpse of / get a glimpse of
meanings: [{"name":"to see someone or something briefly; to get a quick look at someone or something; to manage to see someone or something for a short time","examples":["I caught glimpse of the plane just before it flew out of sight.","Ann caught a glimpse of the robber as he ran out of the bank.","We caught a glimpse of him through the window as his car sped past.","I only got a glimpse of him as we drove by."],"media":[]}]

name: the blues
meanings: [{"name":"sadness; a mood of depression","examples":["You'll have to excuse Bill. He's getting the blues thinking about his puppy.","I get the blues every time I hear that song.","I've got (a case of) the blues.","Do you know what is a great cure for the blues?"],"media":[]}]

name: keep score
meanings: [{"name":"to officially record the number of points, goals, runs, etc., that each player or team gets in a game or contest —sometimes used figuratively","examples":["If you're keeping score, this is the third time that he has run for mayor and lost.","Who's going to keep score when we play bridge?","Could you keep (= record) the score at this afternoon's game?"],"media":[]}]

name: Behind you!
meanings: [{"name":"Look behind you!; There is danger behind you!","examples":["“Behind you!” shouted Tom just as a car raced past and nearly knocked Mary over.","Alice shouted, “Behind you!” just as the pickpocket made off with Fred's wallet."],"media":[]}]

name: (I'd) better be going
meanings: [{"name":"an expression announcing the need to depart","examples":["Bob: Better be going. Got to get home. Bill: Well, if you must, you must. Bye.","Fred: It's midnight. I'd better be going. Henry: Okay. Bye, Fred.","Henry: Better be going. It's starting to snow. John: Yes, it looks bad out."],"media":[]}]

name: Can you imagine?
meanings: [{"name":"Can you believe that?; Imagine that!","examples":["She wore jeans to the dance. Can you imagine?","Billy was eating the houseplant! Can you imagine?"],"media":[]}]

name: (I) can't argue with that
meanings: [{"name":"I agree with what you said.; It sounds like a good idea","examples":["Tom: This sure is good cake. Bob: Can't argue with that.","Sue: What do you say we go for a swim? Fred: I can't argue with that."],"media":[]}]

name: can't complain
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one is fine; a response to a greeting inquiry asking how one is or how things are going for one","examples":["\"How are you feeling?\" \"I can't complain.\"","Jane: How are things going with you?\nKate: Can't complain.","Sue: Hi Mary, How are you doing? \nMary: I can't complain. "],"media":[]}]

name: (I) can't say that I have
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. a vague response to a question about whether one has ever done something or been somewhere. (A polite way of saying no.)","examples":["Kate: Have you seen the umbrella? \nJane: No, can't say that I have.","Bill: Have you ever been to a real opera? Bob: I can't say as I have."],"media":[]}]

name: (I'll) catch you later
meanings: [{"name":"I will talk to you later","examples":["Mary: Got to fly. See you around. Sally: Bye. Catch you later.","John: I have to go to class now. Bill: Okay, catch you later.","Jane: Can I catch you later? Kate: No. \nJane: All right, hold on."],"media":[]}]

name: see you later / later
meanings: [{"name":"used to say goodbye; Good-bye until I see you again","examples":["\"I guess I'll be going now.\" \"OK. (I'll) See you later.\"","John: Good-bye, Sally. I'll see you later. Sally: Until later, then.","Bob: Time to go. Later.  Mary: Later.","Bob: All right. Bye. Mary: Later."],"media":[]}]

name: (I'll) see you around
meanings: [{"name":"I will see you again somewhere","examples":["Bob: Bye for now. Jane: See you around."," Tom: See you around, Fred. Fred: Sure, Tom. See you."],"media":[]}]

name: make the bed / make a bed
meanings: [{"name":"to neatly arrange the sheets, blankets, and bedspread on the bed","examples":["Don't forget to make the bed.","That man has never made a bed in his life.","They taught us the proper way to make a bed.","By the time we returned from our run, she had made the beds and prepared breakfast.","Masha: Jane, I'll have Kate make up Chuck's bed for you."],"media":[]}]

name: change the bed
meanings: [{"name":"to remove dirty sheets from a bed and replace them with clean ones","examples":["Jane: Kate, could you change the bed?"],"media":[]}]

name: (You) mind if I join you? / Can I join you?
meanings: [{"name":"Will you permit me to sit with you? (An inquiry seeking permission to sit at someone's table or join someone else in some activity.)","examples":["“Do you mind if I join you?” asked the lady. “There are no other seats.”","You mind if I join you? I could use a little company today.","Bob: Where you going, Mike? Mike: For a walk.\nBob: You mind if I join you? Mike: Actually, I'd rather be alone."],"media":[]}]

name: that's something/someone for you
meanings: [{"name":"used say that something is very good, very disappointing, or very common","examples":["They brought me the package on Christmas Day! Now that's real service for you!","He stays up late, playing video games and listening to music. That's a teenager for you.","Jane: Jack called. He's backing out of the whole plan.\nKate: Well, that's Jack for you.\nJane: I told you he couldn't be trusted."],"media":[]}]

name: Don't bother
meanings: [{"name":"Please don't do it. It is not necessary.","examples":["Mary: I don't know what to say. Jane: Don't bother saying anything. I wouldn't believe you anyway.","Sue: Do you want me to save this spoonful of mashed potatoes? \nJane: No, don't bother. It isn't worth it. Sue: I hate to waste it.","Jane: Don't bother running upstairs. I already found your book.","Jane: I'll call you when it's done.\nKate: Don't bother! I won't pick up.","Mike: Mama, if you say one more critical thing about Jane, don't bother coming to our wedding."],"media":[]}]

name: Don't get up
meanings: [{"name":"Please, there is no need to rise to greet me.","examples":["Tom (rising): Hello, Mike. Good to see you. Mike (standing): Don't get up. How are you?","You know what? Don't get up. Just sit there.","Jane: Don't get up. What do you need? Kate: Nothing.\nJane: Come on. I'm here to take care of you."],"media":[]}]

name: Don't give up!
meanings: [{"name":"Do not stop trying!; Keep trying!","examples":["You don't give up just because things are hard, not in business, or if your family is depending on you.","Well, don't give up, Jane. It's never too late.","Jane: I asked the boss for a raise, but he said no. \nTom: Don't give up. Try again later."],"media":[]}]

name: Don't mind me.
meanings: [{"name":"Don't pay any attention to me.; Just ignore me.; said to tell someone who is in the same room as you not to pay any attention to you, because you do not want to interrupt what they are doing","examples":["Don't mind me - I'm just sorting out some files here.","Hey Bob, don't mind me. Just coming in for a quick cup of coffee.","Bill and Jane were watching television when Jane's mother walked through the room, grabbing the newspaper on the way. “Don't mind me,” she said.","Anyway, don't mind me, I'm just blowing off steam."],"media":[]}]

name: if you don't mind me saying so / if you don't mind my saying so
meanings: [{"name":"used with a statement as a polite way of saying something that could be annoying or offensive","examples":["You look a bit old for this job, if you don't mind me saying so.","If you don't mind me saying so, you seem confused.","Well, um, if you don't mind me saying so, when you left here, you kind of broke our hearts.","If you don't mind my saying so, you two worry too much."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage context",["Possessive (\"my\"): Treats \"saying\" as a noun; preferred in formal written texts.","Objective Pronoun (\"me\"): Treats \"saying\" as a verb participle; considered more natural in speech and increasingly common. "]]]

name: Don't ask me
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one does not know the answer to a question","examples":["\"Why are they having a company meeting?\" \"Don't ask me. I only work here.\"","Don't ask me why they're changing the system. I think it's fine the way it is."],"media":[]}]

name: Don't push me
meanings: [{"name":"Don't put pressure on me to do something! (Also a literal meaning.)","examples":["Sue: You really must go to the dentist, you know.  \nJohn: Don't push me. I'll go when I'm good and ready.","Bob: Come on! You can finish. Keep trying. \nBill: Don't push me! I have to do it under my own steam!"],"media":[]}]

name: Don't rush me
meanings:
[{"name":"Don't try to hurry me!","examples":["Bill: Hurry up! Make up your mind! 
Bob: Don't rush me! 
Bill: I want to get out of here before midnight.","Bill: The waiter wants to take your order. What do you want? 
Jane: Don't rush me! I can't make up my mind. 
Waiter: I'll come back in a minute."],"media":[]}]

name: Don't tell me what to do!
meanings:
[{"name":"Do not give me orders.","examples":["Bob: Get over there and pick up those papers before they blow away. 
Sally: Don't tell me what to do! 
Bob: Better hurry. One of those papers is your paycheck. But it's no skin off my nose if you don't.","Sue: Next, you should get a haircut, then get some new clothes. You really need to fix yourself up. 
Sally: Don't tell me what to do! Maybe I like me the way I am!"],"media":[]}]

name: drop names
meanings: [{"name":"to say the names of famous people one knows to try to impress others; to mention the names of important or famous people as if they were personal friends","examples":["Mary always tries to impress people by dropping the names of well-known film stars.","You won't have to say a word. Just smile while I drop a few names, see how he reacts.","Bill's such a snob. Leave it to him to drop the names of all the local gentry."],"media":[]}]

name: enough to go around / plenty to go around
meanings: [{"name":"enough of something for all of the people who want or need it; enough to serve a need; enough to serve all who have a need","examples":["There aren't enough jobs to go around.","There's plenty of work to go around.","There's not enough coffee to go around. ","Will there be enough chocolates to go around?"],"media":[]}]

name: enough is enough
meanings: [{"name":"That is enough, and there should be no more.; Stop!; I won't stand for any more!; used to say that one wants something to stop because one can no longer accept or deal with it","examples":["Stop asking for money! Enough is enough!","Sue: That color of lipstick is all wrong for you, Sally. \nSally: Enough is enough! Sue, get lost!  Sue: I was just trying to help.","Bob: Enough is enough! I'm leaving! \nBill: What on earth did I do? Bob: Good-bye"],"media":[]}]

name: every other
meanings: [{"name":"all those that are different or separate from the person or thing that has already been mentioned","examples":["It's a problem that's affecting this town and every other one in the state.","He acts just like every other politician I have known.","It is small, but it performs better than every other car in its class."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that some repeated activity, event, etc., alternately happens and does not happen in consecutive named periods","examples":["I run every other day.","The contest is held every other year.","The conference used to be held every year, but now it takes place every other year.","We get together every other Saturday for lunch."],"media":[]}]

name: Fire away!
meanings: [{"name":"Start doing something, especially to ask questions! ; used to tell someone they may begin asking questions","examples":["Andy: Dad, do you mind if I ask you a few questions? Father: Fire away! ","Jane: The mayor will now take a few questions from reporters. Mayor: Fire away!"],"media":[]}]
origin: (As if giving soldiers the instructions to start firing.)

name: fire away (at someone)
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. to ask many questions of someone; to criticize someone severely","examples":["When it came time for questions, the reporters began firing away at the mayor.","Members of the opposite party are always firing away at the president."],"media":[]}]

name: Flattery will get you nowhere
meanings: [{"name":"You can praise me, but I'm not going to give you what you want; Flattering me will not increase your chances of success","examples":["A: You are beautiful and talented. B: Flattery will get you nowhere, but keep talking.","Flattery will get you nowhere, but that doesn't mean you should stop flattering me!"],"media":[]}]

name: flavor food with something
meanings: [{"name":"to season a food with something","examples":["He flavors his gravy with a little cilantro.","Save room for a small dish of malai kulfi, a homemade ice cream flavored with cardamom and garnished with almond flakes.","Can you flavor the soup with a little less pepper next time?"],"media":[]}]

name: For shame!
meanings: [{"name":"That is shameful!","examples":["Sue: Did you hear that Tom was in jail? Fred: For shame! What did he do? Sue: Nobody knows.","Mary: I've decided not to go to the conference.  John: For shame! Who will represent us?"],"media":[]}]

name: for your information
meanings: [{"name":"sometimes used informally in speech when responding to an annoying statement or question by someone who has accused or blamed one wrongly; used to tell someone that they are wrong about something","examples":["\"Are these the best tickets you could get?\" \"For your information, I had to stand in line for two hours to get these!\"","Mary: What is this one? Sue: For your information, it is exactly the same as the one you just asked about.","Bob: How long do I have to wait here? Bill: For your information, we will be here until the bus driver feels that it is safe to travel.","For your information, I don't even have a car."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that you are telling or giving someone something because they might not know or have it and it could be useful for them","examples":["A copy of the document is enclosed for your information.","Like the summary, comments will not print with the text but can be displayed on the screen for your information."],"media":[]}]

name: generally speaking
meanings: [{"name":"used to show that what you are saying is true in a general way; used to say that a statement describes a general feeling or opinion relating to or affecting all the people or things in a group","examples":["Generally speaking, the more you pay, the more you get.","Generally speaking, people like her as a leader.","I'm just saying, generally speaking, when you order breakfast and hey give you the wrong order, send it back and get the right order."],"media":[]}]

name: (quite) frankly
meanings: [{"name":"in truth; indeed; used when giving an honest and direct opinion, often one that might upset someone","examples":["Frankly, I don't know.","Quite frankly, I think this whole situation is ridiculous.","And, quite frankly, your lifestyle choices are making me just a little nervous.","You guys have shown a lot of interest in me tonight, and I'm flattered and quite frankly, a little frightened."],"media":[]}]

name: fear not
meanings: [{"name":"Don't worry!; Do not fret about it!; used in speech to say that there is no reason to be afraid or worried","examples":["Fear not—I'll protect you.","Fear not, Ms. Swan. Kate may be powerful, but something tells me you're more powerful than you know.","Mary: Oh, look at the clock! I'm going to be late for my appointment! Bob: Fear not! I'll drive you.","Fear not!” said Sally. “We're almost there!”"],"media":[]}]

name: speak for someone / speak for oneself
meanings: [{"name":"to express the opinions or wishes of someone or oneself","examples":["They chose him to speak for the group.","I can't speak for the others.","Speaking only for myself, I'm against the plan.","I can speak for myself. I don't need you to speak for me."],"media":[]}]

name: speak for yourself
meanings: [{"name":"I disagree with what you have just said","examples":["None of us like the hotel.\" \"Speak for yourself – I think it's OK.\"","\"We don't want any dessert.\" \"Speak for yourself. I want some.\"","“We didn't play very well.” “Speak for yourself!” (= I think that I played well.)"],"media":[]}]

name: speak for itself / speak for themselves
meanings: [{"name":"[for something] not to need explaining; to have an obvious meaning","examples":["The facts speak for themselves. Tom is guilty.","Your results speak for themselves. You need to work harder.","Recent events speak for themselves.","Her success speaks for itself."],"media":[]}]

name: from now on / going forward
meanings: [{"name":"from this moment and forever into the future","examples":["I promise, from now on, I'll always tell you the truth.","But, from now on, I swear this is strictly professional.","In fact, from now on, I'm going to take the high road.","From this point going forward, the cut will be 60/40. I'm the 60.","Perhaps I should reconsider going forward.","We'll use this procedure going forward. [=from now on]"],"media":[]}]
origin: Going forward is a little formal.

name: from nowhere
meanings: [{"name":"from an unlikely beginning","examples":["Starting from nowhere, he built a very successful business.","Carter rose from nowhere, and became a president."],"media":[]},{"name":"in a sudden and unexpected way","examples":["The horse came from nowhere to win the race.","From out of nowhere he asked her if she was an actress.","A huge flock of sheep seemed to appear from nowhere."],"media":[]}]

name: not take no for an answer
meanings: [{"name":"to insist on something; not allow someone to refuse what you have offered; not to accept someone's refusal. (A polite way of being insistent.)","examples":["I told him that I couldn't come to the party, but he wouldn't take no for an answer.","Now, you must drop over and see us tomorrow. We won't take no for an answer.","I had to go to their party. They just wouldn't take no for an answer.","Great friends don't take no for an answer."],"media":[]}]

name: here to stay
meanings: [{"name":"likely to last or be present for a long time; permanent; If something is here to stay, it has stopped being unusual and has become generally used or accepted","examples":["Mobile phones are definitely here to stay.","Get ready, kids. I'm back, and this time, I'm here to stay.","Are video games a fad, or are they here to stay?"],"media":[]}]

name: stay loose
meanings: [{"name":"to relax and stay calm; to remain calm; to not worry","examples":["It's OK—stay loose and stay cool.","Just stay loose, man. Everything'll be all right.","Now maybe I just wanna stay loose."],"media":[]}]

name: join the club / welcome to the club
meanings: [{"name":"I am in the same bad situation as you are; often used to suggest that a person's problems or feelings are not unusual and do not deserve much sympathy","examples":["If you don't understand the rules, join the club: no one else does either!","So you think you deserve to be paid more money for your work? Well, join the club.","Okay, So you have a void in your life. Welcome to the club. Don't fill it with wine. Fill it with work, with accomplishments."],"media":[]}]

name: stay the course
meanings: [{"name":"to continue with a process, effort, etc., even though it is difficult; to continue doing something until it is finished or until you achieve something you have planned to do","examples":["We'll succeed in the end if we just stay the course.","Very few of the trainees have stayed the course.","You stay the course, she will come around in time.","But no matter what, you still have to stay the course and forge(= create with effort) your own path."],"media":[]}]

name: stay the night
meanings: [{"name":"to sleep at another person's house for the night","examples":["After the party she was too exhausted to drive so she stayed the night.","They stayed the night at her brother's.","Jane asked me if I wanted to stay the night.","Jane: Are you planning on staying the night? Kate: No, no. Believe me, I'm leaving as soon as possible.\nJane: Good. Not that we don't want you to stay. Obviously, you're welcome."],"media":[]}]

name: stay home
meanings: [{"name":"to not go out for an activity","examples":["Let's stay home tonight.","She got croup, so she had to stay home.","We're just gonna stay home and study."],"media":[]}]

name: Give it up!
meanings:
[{"name":"Stop trying. You are wasting your time","examples":["Bob: Today was too much! I just can't do calculus! 
Bill: Give it up! Get out of that course and get into something less cruel. 
Bob: I think I will.","Tom: I'm just not a very good singer, I guess. Sue: It's no good, Tom. Give it up! 
Tom: Don't you think I'm doing better, though? Sue: Give it up, Tom!"],"media":[]}]

name: God only knows
meanings: [{"name":"it is impossible to say; No one knows but God","examples":["Tom: How long is all this going to take? Alice: God only knows! ","If we don't keep an eye on the kids,, God only knows what kind of trouble they'll get into.","God only knows how he managed to find out where I lived."],"media":[]}]

name: good heavens / my heavens
meanings: [{"name":"an exclamation of surprise, shock, or amazement.","examples":["My heavens, you've grown!","My heavens, is that penguin surfing?","John: Good heavens! A diamond ring! Bill: I bet it's not real.","Jane: Ouch! John: Good heavens! What happened? Jane: I just stubbed my toe."],"media":[]}]

name: (It) hasn't been easy
meanings: [{"name":"Things have been difficult, but I have gotten through.","examples":["Bill: I'm so sorry about all your troubles. I hope things are all right now. \nBob: It hasn't been easy, but things are okay now.","And now I'm not gonna lie to you and say it's always been easy.","Look, the night shift hasn't been easy on any of us. ","I know this hasn't been easy on you lately, and that doesn't make me feel good."],"media":[]}]

name: Have I got something for you!
meanings: [{"name":"I have something really exciting for you! (Said earnestly, before saying or showing something surprising or exciting.)","examples":["A: \"Have I got something for you!\" B: \"Brownies! Yay, thank you!\"","Have I got some dessert for you with sugar on top.","A: \"I've always wanted to see Paris.\" B: \"Well then have I got news for you! We're going there this summer for your birthday!\""],"media":[]}]

name: have some more
meanings: [{"name":"a polite invitation or request to take more of something, usually food or drink","examples":["Jane: What a lovely, light cake. \nMary: Oh, have some more. Otherwise the boys will just wolf it down ","Jane: Can I have some more popcorn?\nKate: Oh, sure.","Well, in that case, have some more fries.","Maybe I will have some more f that, uh, potato stuff."],"media":[]}]

name: Have you met someone?
meanings: [{"name":"a question asked when introducing someone to someone else. (The question need not be answered. The someone is usually a person's name.)","examples":["Tom: Hello, Mary. Have you met Fred? Mary: Hello, Fred. Glad to meet you. Fred: Glad to meet you, Mary.","Tom: Hey, Mary! Good to see you. Have you met Fred? Mary: No, I don't believe I have. Hello, Fred. Glad to meet you. Fred: Hello, Mary."],"media":[]}]

name: help me understand
meanings: [{"name":"Please explain this further because it isn't clear or because it seems senseless. (Also literal.)","examples":["Now, help me understand. When you say that the bridge is wobbly, do you mean it's dangerous or just a little scary?","Help me understand, if you don't mind. If I agree to pay your tax bill, you will supply me with a dozen fresh eggs per week for three years. What's the guarantee?","Jane, help me understand. Are you upset because of what you did or because you can't remember it?","Please, help me understand what's going on here."],"media":[]}]

name: help yourself / help oneself
meanings: [{"name":"to serve oneself as much food or drink as one would like; to take something for yourself","examples":["There's plenty of food, so help yourself.","Help yourself to some dessert.","Bob: Mind if I have a fry, Jane?  \nJane: No, no, go ahead, help yourself.","I told my kids to help themselves to anything in the fridge."],"media":[]},{"name":"to take something without permission","examples":["He saw the money lying on the table, and he helped himself.","He helped himself to the car keys.","He was accused of helping himself to millions of dollars of his clients' money."],"media":[]}]

name: here goes nothing
meanings: [{"name":"used when one is about to try doing something new, difficult, or unpleasant that may end up failing","examples":["I've never skied before, so here goes nothing.","\"Here goes nothing,\" he muttered, as he began the final exam.","Q: Are you ready? Have you done your safety check? It's your turn to jump! Do it now! \nA: Okay. Here goes nothing!"],"media":[]}]

name: hold it
meanings: [{"name":"to go no further; Stop right there.; stop and do not continue what you are doing; used to tell someone to wait or stop doing something","examples":["Hold it right there. Where do you think you're going?","Tom: Hold it! Mary: What's wrong? \nTom: You almost stepped on my contact lens.","Hold it! You're putting too much pepper in the soup.","Mom, hold it! You are not getting into the car alone with those two. You barely know them."],"media":[]}]

name: how about you
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask someone to tell one something in response to what one has just said; What is your choice?","examples":["I like skiing and hiking. How about you? What do you like?","I'm ready to go. How about you?","Waiter: Can I take your order? Bill: I'll have the chef's salad and ice tea. \nWaiter (turning to Sue): How about you? Sue: I'll have the same."],"media":[]}]

name: how about it
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask if someone will do something","examples":["Well, how about it, are you coming?","That's such a good idea. How about it, girls? Wanna spend next weekend here?"],"media":[]}]

name: how about
meanings: [{"name":"what do you say to or what do you think of","examples":["You don't eat meat, do you? How about fish?","How about going out for a walk after dinner?"],"media":[]}]

name: how can / how could
meanings: [{"name":"used to show that one thinks that someone has done or said something shocking or wrong","examples":["\"We don't need his help anyway.\" \"How can you say that?!\"","How could she just walk away from her children like that?","Jane: I had a fight in the school.\nMom: How could you not tell me?"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to express doubt that something will happen, is possible, etc.","examples":["How could I (ever/possibly) leave this job?","How can I (ever/possibly) thank you?"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to show disappointment in someone's actions, thoughts, words, etc.","examples":["He threw away my gift? Oh, how could he?","How could you do this to me?","How could you Iet this happen?"],"media":[]}]

name: how do you like that
meanings: [{"name":"used for emphasis to show surprise","examples":["He's moving to Hawaii? Well, how do you like that!","Jane: Kate!\nKate: Surprised to see me? Mike brought me. How do you like that?"],"media":[]},{"name":"used for emphasis to show disapproval","examples":["She canceled at the last minute. How do you like that?"],"media":[]}]

name: how do you like
meanings: [{"name":"used when asking someone how they like their drinks made","examples":["How do you like the soup?","\"How do you like your tea?\" \"Milk and one sugar, please.\""],"media":[]},{"name":"used when asking someone for an opinion","examples":["How do you like my new shoes?"],"media":[]}]

name: How (have) you been?
meanings: [{"name":"one of the standard greeting inquiries.","examples":["Bob: Hi, Fred! How have you been? Fred: Great! What about you? Bob: Fine.","Bob: How you been? Sue: Okay, I guess. You okay? Bob: Yup."],"media":[]}]

name: how should I know / how would I know
meanings: [{"name":"I don't know; Why should I be expected to know? (Shows impatience or rudeness.)","examples":["\"Is it going to rain?\" \"How should/would I know?\"","Bill: Why is the orca called the killer whale? Mary: How should I know?","\"Where are the neighbors going? \" \"How would I know?!\"","Bob: John! Did you know this town was on the market for 20 years before we bought it?\nJohn: How would I know that? why would I know that? I didn't know that."],"media":[]}]

name: How something is that!
meanings: [{"name":"Isn't that wonderful or awesome? (The something = cool, good, great, awesome, yummy, etc. More of an exclamation than a question, and either the question mark or the exclamation mark can be used.)","examples":["A: Here is my new jacket. Isn't the red bright? \nB: How cool is that?","Now here is my latest creation. How great is that?"],"media":[]}]

name: how's that?
meanings: [{"name":"used to ask someone if something is acceptable","examples":["I can bring it over tomorrow. How's that?","Jane: I could help with the engagement party. How's that?\nKate: Well, I wasn't planning on inviting you."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to ask someone if something is good; used when asking if something you have done for someone is satisfactory","examples":["Let me get you another blanket. There, how's that?","Let me put a cushion behind your back. How's that?","\"Could you close the window slightly?\" \"Sure. How's that?\"","\"The water's a bit too hot.\" \"OK, how's that? Is it better?\""],"media":[]}]

name: How's it going?
meanings: [{"name":"one of the standard informal greeting inquiries.","examples":["Sue: How's it going? Bill: Just great! How are you? Sue: Fine, thanks.","Jane: So, how's it going?\nKate: Really, really good."],"media":[]}]

name: How's that working out (for you)?
meanings: [{"name":"And how did that so-called promising idea work out? (Sometimes sarcastic or ironic.)","examples":["Jane: How's that working out for ya?\nKate: Pretty poorly, thank you.","Bob: I tried to lose weight by giving up desserts. \nJane: How's that working out for you?"],"media":[]}]

name: live with something
meanings: [{"name":"to experience and accept an unpleasant event, decision, or situation; to put up with something; tolerate","examples":["I can't change the situation so I'm going to have to learn to live with it.","That is not acceptable. I can't live with that. Please change it.","Mary refused to live with the proposed changes.","She had to live with their decision."],"media":[]}]

name: I (can) promise you
meanings: [{"name":"used to emphasize a statement","examples":["He's only concerned about himself, I promise you.","I can promise you, you won't be disappointed."],"media":[]}]

name: could be better
meanings:
[{"name":"a response to a greeting meaning “My state is not as good as it might be.”","examples":["John: How are things going, Fred? Fred: Things could be better. And you? 
John: About the same.","Bob: Hi, Bill! How are you? Bill: I could be better. What's new with you? 
Bob: Nothing much.","Jane: How's it going?
Kate: It could be better."],"media":[]}]

name: could be worse
meanings:
[{"name":"a response to a greeting meaning “My state is not as bad as it might be.”","examples":["John: How are you, Fred? Fred: Things could be worse. And you? 
John: Okay, I guess.","Bill: Hi, Bob! What's happening?
Bob: I could be worse. What's new with you?","Jane: My hair is very amused.
Kate: Come on, things could be worse."],"media":[]}]

name: could use something
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that you would like something","examples":["I could use some help putting these decorations up if you're not too busy.","Can I get you anything?\" \"Thanks. I could use a drink.\"","Jane: Would you like to have a coffee with me?\nKate: Yeah. I could use a coffee, actually."],"media":[]},{"name":"used to say that something or someone needs something","examples":["Their website could use an upgrade.","He could use a new suit for work."],"media":[]}]

name: could do with / do with
meanings: [{"name":"to make good use of; If something could do with something, it needs it very much","examples":["I could do with a cup of coffee.","You could do with a haircut."],"media":[]}]

name: (I) don't believe I've had the pleasure
meanings: [{"name":"an expression meaning I haven't met you yet.","examples":["Tom: I'm Tom. I don't believe I've had the pleasure. Bill: Hello. I'm Bill. \nTom: Nice to meet you, Bill. Bill: Likewise.","Bob: Looks like rain. Fred: Sure does. Oh, I don't believe I've had the pleasure. \nBob: I'm Bob. Fred: My name is Fred. Glad to meet you."],"media":[]}]

name: I don't believe this!
meanings: [{"name":"This is very strange!; I do not believe that this is happening.","examples":["“I don't believe this!” muttered Sally as all the doors in the house slammed at the same time.","Sally: You're expected to get here early and make my coffee every morning. John: I don't believe this.","I don't believe this. You called the police?"],"media":[]}]

name: I don't care
meanings: [{"name":"It doesn't matter to me.","examples":["Mary: Can I take these papers away? Tom: I don't care. Do what you want.","Bill: Should this room be white or yellow? Sally: I don't care."],"media":[]}]

name: (I) don't mind if I do
meanings: [{"name":"Yes, I would like to.; used as a polite way of accepting something","examples":["\"Would you like another cup of coffee?\" \"Thank you: I don't mind if I do.\"","Sally: Have some more coffee? Bob: Don't mind if I do.","Jane: Here are some lovely roses. Would you like to take a few blossoms with you? \nJohn: I don't mind if I do."],"media":[]}]

name: I don't think we've met
meanings: [{"name":"Hello, I don't know your name, but I want to greet you.","examples":["A: I'm Jane. I don't think we've met. B: I'm Kate.","A: I've seen you here often, but I don't think we've met. \nB: I'm Bob. I own this place.","Jane: Hello. I don't think we've met. \nKate: I'm Katherine, your new neighbor."],"media":[]}]

name: I got it
