meanings: [{"name":"I'll do this!; This is my task!; I'll do it!","examples":["Sam (moving ahead of Jane to open the door): I got it!","Jane: Could you guys help me? It's really heavy.\nBob: I got it.","Jane: Hey, the phone.\nKate: I got it."],"media":[]}]

name: (I) hope not
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one wants something not to happen or to not be true","examples":["\"Will you have to miss the party?\" \"I hope not.\"","John: It looks like it's going to rain. Jane: Hope not.","Bob: The Johnsons said they might come over this evening. \nJane: I hope not. I've got things to do.","Jane: So is Bob gone for good? \nKate: I don't know. God, I hope not."],"media":[]}]

name: (I) hope so
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one wants something to happen or be true and thinks it could happen or be true","examples":["Jane: You'll be out selling your candy in no time.\nKate: I hope so. I gotta win.","Bill: Is this the right house? Bob: Hope so.","John: Will you be coming to dinner Friday? Sue: Yes, I hope so."],"media":[]}]

name: I know what you mean
meanings: [{"name":"used to express agreement; I know exactly what you are talking about, and I feel the same way about it.","examples":["\"He can be a little difficult.\" \"I know what you mean.\"","John: These final exams are just terrible. Bob: I know what you mean. \nJohn: Why do we have to go through this?","Mary: What a pain! I hate annual inventories. \nJohn: I know what you mean. It's really boring."],"media":[]}]

name: look in on someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"to make a brief social visit to someone or something; to see to the welfare of someone or something; to check briefly on someone or something","examples":["I plan to look in on some old friends when I'm in town.","Jane: Hey, maybe you could look in on him.\nKate: I know what you meant. I'll stop by tomorrow and see him.","Bob: I'll stop by your house and look in on things while you're on vacation. \nMike: Yes, just look in and make sure nothing is wrong.","If you're working late, I can look in on him."],"media":[]}]

name: (you) know what I mean
meanings: [{"name":"used when you think that the person listening understands and so you do not need to say any more; Do you understand me?; Do you agree? ","examples":["I grew up there, you know what I mean, so I know what it's like.","He's kind of strange. Do you know what I mean?","You've got to give him a chance, you know what I mean?"],"media":[]}]

name: I've got it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one suddenly remembers, understands, or has found something","examples":["Now, what was his name? Tony? Tom? No, I've got it! Tim. His name was Tim."],"media":[]}]

name: owe you one / owe someone one
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that someone should help or give something to another person in return for help given","examples":["Thanks for your help. I owe you one.","You owe your sister one after all she has done for you."],"media":[]}]

name: speak out of turn / talk out of turn
meanings: [{"name":"to say something that you should not because it is the wrong situation or because it offends someone","examples":["Did I speak out of turn?","Bill: You said I was the one who did it. Mary: I'm sorry. I spoke out of turn. I was mistaken.","Bill: I seem to have said the wrong thing. Bob: You certainly did. \nBill: I spoke out of turn, and I'm sorry.","He enjoys talking out of turn.","Unfortunately, even though he is speaking out of turn, he's right."],"media":[]}]

name: shove it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one will not accept or do something; a rude expression showing that you are angry about something that you have been offered or asked to do","examples":["They can take their suggestion and shove it.","We're all waiting for you to tell Bob to shove it.","Take your stinking deal and shove it."],"media":[]}]

name: if I were someone
meanings: [{"name":"used when expressing an opinion as to how another person should act or behave; putting myself in someone's situation","examples":["If I were you, I'd accept his apology.","I think I'd take the money if I were you.","I'd be careful if I were you.","I'm just saying I wouldn't trust him if I were you."],"media":[]}]

name: I wouldn't bet on it / I wouldn't count on it
meanings: [{"name":"said to indicate the listener's disagreement with a statement; I do not believe that something will happen. (Also with that or some specific happening.)","examples":["\"The economy will improve next year.\" \"I wouldn't bet on it if I were you.\"","John: I'll be a vice president in a year or two.\nMary: I wouldn't bet on that.","John: I'll pick up a turkey on the day before Thanksgiving. Mary: Did you order one ahead of time? \nJohn: No. Mary: Then I wouldn't count on it."],"media":[]}]

name: if you must (know)
meanings: [{"name":"All right, if you have to.","examples":["Sally: It's late. I have to move along. Mary: If you must. Good-bye. See you tomorrow.","Alice: I'm taking these things with me. Jane: If you must. All right. They can stay here, though.","Joke if you must, but I am not the woman you once knew.","If you must knock on my door, limit yourself to two raps."],"media":[]},{"name":" used when one is answering a question that one does not want to answer because the information is personal, embarrassing, etc.","examples":["We're in the midst of a family crisis, if you must know!","Bob: Just tell us where you were at lunch.\nBill: Well, if you must know, I was having lunch with Mike.","Jane: And are you married?\nMike: Well, if you must know, I'm a widower."],"media":[]}]

name: I'll have the same / The same for me
meanings: [{"name":"I would like the same thing that the last person chose.","examples":["Waitress: What would you like? Tom: Sandwich, fries, and coffee. Jane: I'll have the same.","John: For dessert, I'll have strawberry ice cream. Bill: I'll have the same."],"media":[]}]

name: I'll have you know
meanings: [{"name":"used to emphasize something in a somewhat annoyed or angry way;  used to assert a fact, often in a confrontational or indignant manner, typically to correct someone or emphasize one's own knowledge or status; It is commonly used when the speaker feels they need to inform someone of something important, often in response to a perceived slight or incorrect assumption.","examples":["Jane: Did your son go to college?, Did he go to college?  \nKate: I'll have you know that he was given a full scholarship to Harvard!","She's a very nice person, I'll have you know.","I may look young, but I'll have you know I'm old enough to be your mother.","Bob: I'll have you know you're speaking to your Captain.\nBill: Well, I'll have you know that we don't report to you. We report to the Commissioner's office."],"media":[]}]

name: (I'm) glad you could come / glad you could make it
meanings: [{"name":"a phrase said by the host or hostess (or both) to a guest","examples":["Tom: Thank you so much for having me. Sally: We're glad you could come. John: Yes, we are. Bye.","Bill: Bye. Sally: Bye, Bill. Glad you could come.","I'm so glad you could make it."],"media":[]}]

name: I told you / I told you so
meanings: [{"name":"used to say to someone that one was right about something especially when that person disagreed; said when something bad happens after you warned someone that it would happen","examples":["\"You were right after all.\" \"See. I told you so!\"","Bob: Jane, Are you ready for this one? Taylors' daughter Kate's getting married. Hate to say \"I told you so,\" but I told you so.","Don't worry. I'm not gonna say, \"I told you so.\""],"media":[]}]

name: I'm dying to know
meanings: [{"name":"I am very eager to find something out","examples":["Jan: I'm not sure if I am supposed to tell you when Mary is leaving for New York. \nAnn: Oh, please! I'm just dying to know.","I'm just dying to know what our new address will be. I'm hoping for Paris.","Aren't you dying to know what he wrote?"],"media":[]}]

name: I'm all ears / I'm listening
meanings:
[{"name":"to be waiting eagerly to hear about something; You have my attention, so you should talk.","examples":["Bob: Look, old pal. I want to talk to you about something. 
Tom: I'm listening.","Bill: I guess I owe you an apology. 
Jane: I'm all ears.","I'm all ears - tell us what they had to say.","Bob: What should we play now? Bill: Oh, I got an idea.
Bob: Oh okay, I'm listening.
"],"media":[]}]

name: finish with something / finish something with something
meanings: [{"name":"to have no further need for (something); to stop using (something);  to become done with something","examples":["Could I see the newspaper when you finish with it?","If everyone has finished with the tomato sauce, I'll put it away."," When will this be finished with?","If you've finished with the gravy, could you pass it down this end of the table?"],"media":[]},{"name":"to complete something by doing, eating, saying, singing, etc. something","examples":["They finished the evening with some food and drinks at a local bar.","He finished the race with a sprint to the finishing line.","I'd like to finish with a few words of thanks.","We ate four courses, and finished with a cup of coffee."],"media":[]}]

name: finish with someone
meanings: [{"name":"to stop dealing with, working on, or punishing someone","examples":["When I finish with him he'll be sorry!","I haven't finished with you yet!","I'm not finished with you.","Come on, Kate. Finish with your customer first."],"media":[]}]

name: I'm not kidding
meanings: [{"name":"I am telling the truth.; I am not trying to fool you.","examples":["Mary: Those guys are all suspects in the robbery.  Sue: No! They can't be! \nMary: I'm not kidding!","John (gesturing): The fish I caught was this big! Jane: I don't believe it! \nJohn: I'm not kidding!","I'm not kidding, old woman! Stay away from me! Don't touch me!"],"media":[]}]

name: I'm not having this conversation
meanings: [{"name":"I don't like discussing this with you.; I can't believe I'm discussing this with you.","examples":["Don: You are late again, and your workspace is a mess. We are all angry with you. \nHanna: I'm not having this conversation.","Isabel: This is so embarrassing! I'm not having this conversation! \nDan: I'm so sorry."],"media":[]}]

name: I'm off
meanings: [{"name":"an expression said by someone who is just leaving","examples":["Bob: Time to go. I'm off. \nMary: Bye.","Sue: Well, it's been great. Good-bye. Got to go. \nMary: I'm off too. Bye."],"media":[]}]

name: I'm not picky
meanings: [{"name":"What you are offering me or suggesting is quite sat- isfactory, since I am easy to please.","examples":["Mother: These cookies are a little brown on the bottom, but they're quite tasty. \nHanna: Thanks. I'm not picky. They look great to me.","Dan (speaking to the room clerk): I'm not picky, but I really would prefer a room that doesn't look out on all the trash cans."],"media":[]}]

name: someone on it / I'm on it
meanings: [{"name":"someone is actively dealing with a problem, job, etc.; someone doing something that needs to be done, or trying to solve a problem","examples":["\"We need to get this paperwork done.\" \"Don't worry; I'm on it.\"","\"We need help with web design.\" \"Don't worry, I'm on it.\"","Bob: I'll be back in half an hour. Make sure it's on my desk by then.\nKate: Will do, sir. I got it. I'm on it.\n"],"media":[]}]

name: in other words
meanings: [{"name":"to explain it more clearly; used to introduce a statement that repeats what has been said in a different and usually a simpler or more exact way","examples":["\"She said the movie was a bit predictable.\" \"In other words, she didn't like it.\"","He was economical with the truth – in other words, he lied."],"media":[]}]

name: going on
meanings: [{"name":"approaching; nearly or almost (a particular number, age, time, or amount)","examples":["Jane is 16 going on 17.","Kate is six years old going on seven.","It was going on midnight when we left the party."],"media":[]}]

name: Will that be all? /  Is that everything? /  Is there anything else?
meanings:
[{"name":"Is there anything else you want?; Is there any other mater you wish to discuss?; Is there any other request? (These phrases are used by shopkeepers, clerks, and food service personnel to find out if the customer wants anything more.)","examples":["Clerk: Here's the roast you ordered. Will there be anything else? 
Rachel: No, that's all.","Waiter: Anything else? 
Bill: Just coffee.","The clerk rang up the last item and asked, “Will that be all?”","Waiter: Anything else? 
Jane: No, that's everything."],"media":[]}]

name: Is that so? / Is that right?
meanings:
[{"name":"Is what you said correct? (With rising question intonation.)","examples":["Henry: These are the ones we need. 
Andrew: Is that right? They don't look so good to me. ","Fred: Tom is the one who came in late. 
Rachel: Is that so? It looked like Bill to me."],"media":[]},{"name":"That is what you say, but I do not believe you. (No rising question intonation. Slightly rude.)","examples":["Mary: You are making a mess of this. 
Alice: Is that so? And I suppose that you're perfect?","Bob: I found your performance to be weak in a number of places. 
Henry: Is that right? Why don't you tell me about those weaknesses."],"media":[]}]

name: is that a fact?
meanings: [{"name":"used to respond to a statement that is thought to be surprising or unlikely","examples":["\"He looks much younger, but he's actually almost 60 years old.\" \"Is that a fact?\"","\"A lot of people agree with me.\" \"Is that a fact?\"","Jane: I was assailed this morning.\nKate: Is that a fact?","Bob: I've never been accused of impropriety.\nBill: Oh, is that a fact?"],"media":[]}]

name: you got me / you've got me / you got me there / you've got me there
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one doesn't have an answer, solution, etc.; something that you say when you do not know the answer to a question","examples":["That's a good question. You've got me.","\"How many ounces in a kilo?\" \"You got me.\"","You got me there. I don't know.","That's a good question. You've got me there.","You got me there. I have no idea what the answer is."],"media":[]}]

name: can't be helped
meanings: [{"name":"to be unavoidable; Nothing can be done to help the situation.; It isn't anyone's fault","examples":["It's too bad that we have to leave, but it can't be helped.","Bill: My goodness, the lawn looks dead! \nSue: It can't be helped. There's no rain, and water is rationed"],"media":[]}]

name: (It) doesn't bother me at all
meanings: [{"name":"It does not trouble me at all.; I have no objection.","examples":["John: Do you mind if I sit here? \nJane: Doesn't bother me at all."],"media":[]}]

name: (It) (really) doesn't matter to me
meanings: [{"name":"I do not care.","examples":["Andrew: What shall I do? What shall I do? \nAlice: Do whatever you like. Jump off a bridge. Go live in the jungle. It really doesn't matter to me.","It doesn't matter to me which way you do it. It's six of one and half a dozen of the other."],"media":[]}]

name: know better (than someone)
meanings: [{"name":"to know or understand more than other people; to know more than someone else because you have more experience and more skill","examples":["You can't tell him what to do. He always thinks that he knows better.","They thought the painting was a fake, but Masha knew better."],"media":[]}]

name: know better / know any better (than to do something)
meanings: [{"name":"to be wise or moral enough not to do something; to be smart or sensible enough not to do something","examples":["Mom: Well, look, I've told her off, Kate. Kate: But she's not even saying \"Sorry\"!\nMom: She's only 1. She doesn't know any better yet. We have to teach her.\n","You walked home alone? Don't you know better (than that)?","Mary should have known better than to accept a lift from a stranger.","Children should know better than to play in the road.","Sure, she's only six, but she's old enough to know better than to run off without us."],"media":[]}]

name: (It) works for me
meanings: [{"name":"It is fine with me.","examples":["Bob: Is it okay if I sign us up for the party? Sally: It works for me.","Tom: Is Friday all right for the party? Bill: Works for me. Bob: It works for me, too."],"media":[]}]

name: (I've) seen worse
meanings: [{"name":"It is often used to indicate that the current situation, while unpleasant, is not the worst possible scenario; what you are currently experiencing  is not as bad as something you have experienced before","examples":["Alice: How did you like the movie? John: I've seen worse.","Bill: What do you think about this weather? Bob: Seen worse. Can't remember when, though.","Bob: Boy, we've got our work cut out for us. \nMike: But I've seen worse. It's not a problem."],"media":[]}]

name: (I've) never been better / (I've) never felt better
meanings: [{"name":"This is the best I have ever been.; used to say that you are doing very well, or that your day/week/month/year has been great. Use this when you are feeling happy, and things are going very well in your life.","examples":["Mary: How are you, Sally? Sally: Never been better, sweetie"," Doctor: How are you, Jane? Jane: Never felt better. Doctor: Then, why are you here?","Jane: Uh, is everything okay, Mr. Bob?\nBob: Yeah, never felt better. I feel invigorated!","Jane: You all right?\nKate: Never been better."],"media":[]}]

name: I've been better
meanings:
[{"name":"is used to say that you are not well, or that your day/week/month/year has not been good; Use this in polite conversation when you are not doing well, but it is not appropriate to complain.","examples":["Bob: You all right?
Jane: I've been better.","Jane: You doing okay?
Kate: Well, I've been better, but I'm all right.","Masha: How you holding up?
Jane: Well, Masha, I've been better."],"media":[]}]

name: I've got work to do
meanings: [{"name":"I'm too busy to stay here any longer","examples":["Jane: Time to go. I've got work to do. John: Me, too. See you.","Bob: I have to leave now. Bill: So soon? Bob: Yes, I've got work to do. "],"media":[]},{"name":"Do not bother me. I'm busy.","examples":["Bill: Can I ask you a question? Jane: I've got work to do.","Mary: There are some things we have to get straightened out on this Wilson contract. \nJohn: I've got work to do. It will have to wait."],"media":[]}]

name: have to go / have got to go
meanings: [{"name":"to be required to leave","examples":["I've got to go. I have a doctor's appointment.","Sorry to break up this party, but I've got to go send some documents before work.","All right, I got to go. I have another call, Jane."],"media":[]},{"name":"to need to be gotten rid of","examples":["These old boxes have (got) to go.","I gave him another chance, but Tim has got to go."],"media":[]},{"name":"to use the toilet","examples":["One of the children said he had to go.","All right, I got to go to the bathroom."],"media":[]}]

name: (I've) got to run
meanings: [{"name":" a phrase announcing one's need to depart","examples":["John: Got to run. It's late.  \nJane: Me, too. See ya, bye-bye.","Mary: Want to watch another movie?  \nBill: No, thanks. I've got to run."],"media":[]}]

name: (I've) got to go home
meanings: [{"name":"a phrase announcing one's need to depart.","examples":["Sue: Leaving so early? John: I've got to go home.","Bye, everyone! I've got to go home now!"],"media":[]}]

name: (I've) got to get moving
meanings: [{"name":"a phrase announcing one's need to depart","examples":["Bill: Time to go. Got to get moving.  \nSally: Bye, Tom.","Mary: It's late and I've got to get moving. Sue: Well, if you must, okay. Come again sometime. \nMary: Bye.","Jane: Kate, what's the holdup? We've got to get moving here."],"media":[]}]

name: I have better things to do
meanings: [{"name":"There are better ways to spend my time.; I cannot waste any more time on this matter.","examples":["Andrew: Good-bye. I've got better things to do than stand around here listening to you brag. \nHenry: Well, good-bye and good riddance.","I have better things to do with my time than baby-sit.","Don't you think I have better things to do than to bring you checks every day,","Now, uh, if you'll excuse me, I have better things to do."],"media":[]}]

name: (It's) time to move on / (Let's) just move on
meanings: [{"name":"Let's stop worrying, complaining, or feeling guilty (about something) and let things return to normal","examples":["Don: Yes, it was a bad accident, but it's time to move on.","Hanna: It's over. It can't be undone. Andrew: Let's just move on.","Bob: Let's not fight about it. It's over. Let's just move on to the next one.\nJane: No. No, no, no.","Please, Bob, just move on and be happy."],"media":[]}]

name: take care of business
meanings: [{"name":"to do what needs to be done","examples":["Sarah is good at taking care of business, so she's been put in charge of organizing the event."],"media":[]}]

name: just you wait / just wait /  Just you wait and see / You just wait and see
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that one is sure that something will happen; Wait and see what will happen.; If you wait, you will see that what I predict will be true.","examples":["He'll be a star someday—just (you) wait.","John: You'll get what you deserve! Just you wait!  \nJane: Mind your own business.","Bill: Things will get better. You just wait and see! \nSue: Sure, but when?"],"media":[]}]

name: wait until / wait till
meanings: [{"name":"used to emphasize that a future event is going to be very surprising, important, troublesome, etc.","examples":["Wait till you see their new house. It's just beautiful!","You think you're in trouble now? Just wait until your father finds out what you did, young lady!"],"media":[]}]

name: just what you need / that's all someone needs
meanings:
[{"name":"Someone does not need that at all.; That's the last straw! (Always sarcastic. The someone can be a person's name or a pronoun.)","examples":["Jane: The dog died and the basement is just starting to flood. 
Fred: That's all we need.","Sally: Bill, the check you wrote to the Jane was returned. There's no more money in the bank. 
Bill: That's all we need.","Bob: On top of having too many bills to pay, now I have car trouble! 
Mary: That's just what you need!"],"media":[]}]

name: (I was) just wondering
meanings: [{"name":"a comment made after hearing a response to a previous question; just curious or thinking; to think about things in a questioning and sometimes doubting way","examples":["John: Do you always keep your film in the refrigerator? Mary: Yes, why? John: I was just wondering.","Bob: Did this cost a lot? Sue: I really don't think you need to know that. \nBob: Sorry. Just wondering."],"media":[]}]

name: keep a secret
meanings: [{"name":"to know a secret and not tell anyone; to not tell anyone a secret that you know","examples":["He knows how to keep a secret.","It's hard to keep a secret in a school.","I asked him if he could keep a secret.","Please keep our little secret private."],"media":[]}]

name: keep in touch
meanings: [{"name":"to continue to talk to or write to someone","examples":["My school friend and I still keep in touch.","Have you kept in touch with your college roommate?","Jane: Good-bye, Fred. Keep in touch. Fred: Bye, Jane."],"media":[]}]

name: keep up on
meanings: [{"name":"to continue to know the newest information about (something); ","examples":["I find it hard to keep up on international affairs.","You know, I've been keeping up on what's been happening here since I left through Kate."],"media":[]}]

name: keep it up
meanings: [{"name":"used to encourage someone to continue doing something","examples":["You're doing very well everybody. Keep it up!"],"media":[]}]

name: keep one's opinions to oneself
meanings: [{"name":"to stop mentioning one's own opinions, especially when they disagree with someone else's","examples":["Please keep your rude opinions to yourself!","I should work on keeping my opinions to myself."],"media":[]}]

name: stay out of someone's way/ get out of the way / stay out of the way
meanings: [{"name":"to not block someone's path","examples":["He asked the children to stay out of his way while he made dinner.","John: Stay out of my way. I'm carrying a heavy load. \nBill: Sorry.","I'm just trying to stay out of the way of all those sparks that are flying.","Now you can either help me or you can get out of the way."],"media":[]}]

name: Stay out of this!
meanings: [{"name":"This is not your business, so do not try to get involved.","examples":["Stay out of this, Jane. This is between me and my mother.","Can you stay out of this? This is between me and my daughter.","I told myself to stay out of this, but I can't.","Stay out of this, Jane. You've done enough damage."],"media":[]}]

name: Keep still
meanings: [{"name":"Get quiet and stay that way","examples":["Child: I want some candy! \nMother: Keep still.","You gotta close that mouth, Bob. Keep still and quiet."],"media":[]}]

name: keep quiet
meanings: [{"name":"to not say anything or make any noise","examples":["He thought about telling the police what he knew, but he decided to keep quiet.","Please keep quiet during the movie."],"media":[]},{"name":" to not say anything about (something)","examples":["She kept her plans quiet."],"media":[]},{"name":"to prevent (someone or something) from making noise","examples":["She gave the dog a bone to keep him quiet."],"media":[]},{"name":"to prevent (someone) from revealing information about something","examples":["They paid money to the witness to keep him quiet."],"media":[]}]

name: keep quiet about / keep still about
meanings: [{"name":"to not say anything about (something)","examples":["She kept quiet about her plans to change jobs.","Bill: Are you really going to sell your car? Mary: Yes, but keep quiet about it.","John: Someone said you're looking for a new job. Sue: That's right, but keep still about it."],"media":[]}]

name: better still / better yet / even better
meanings: [{"name":"even more satisfactory; used to say that a particular choice would be more satisfactory","examples":["OK. I'll be firm. Better still, be brutal.","Try a bean burger instead of a regular burger. Better still, choose a grilled mushroom.","We could meet for a cup of coffee or, better still, for lunch.","Maybe we should postpone the project. Or even better, cancel it.","Give me the list. Better yet, leave it on the table.","You want to talk to someone, you talk to me. Better yet, you just keep your mouth shut."],"media":[]}]

name: take it from me / take my word for it
meanings: [{"name":"Believe me!; used to tell someone he or she should believe what one is saying","examples":["Take it from me. He would love to go to the concert with you.","It won't work - take it from me.","It's true! Take it from me! ","Take it from me. This is a very good day for this part of the country."],"media":[]}]

name: You ain't seen nothing yet
meanings: [{"name":"said to mean that more surprising or exciting things are likely to happen; The best, most exciting, or cleverest part is yet to come!","examples":["Alice: Well, the first act was simply divine. Sue: Stick around. You ain't seen nothing yet!","That was just the start - you ain't seen nothing yet.","Mary: This part of the city is really beautiful. Bill: You ain't seen nothing yet!","I've only just begun - you ain't seen nothing yet."],"media":[]}]

name: you name it
meanings: [{"name":"anything; anything you could say or think of","examples":["You name it, we sell it!","I like all kinds of music: rock, blues, reggae, classical—you name it!","I've tried every diet going - you name it, I've tried it.","So basically I want a whole new look, new furniture, new paint, you name it.","Jane: But there is something I want you to do for me. \nKate: Of course. Anything. You name it. What?"],"media":[]}]

name: so clean you could eat off the floor
meanings: [{"name":"[of a room or a house] very clean","examples":["Her kitchen is so clean you could eat off the floor!","It's so clean here you could eat off the floor. I prefer a little mess, myself.","Bet your apartment's immaculate. Could probably eat off the floor."],"media":[]}]

name: You can't win them all
meanings: [{"name":"a catch phrase said when someone, including the speaker, has lost in a contest or failed at something. (The you is impersonal, meaning one, anyone.)","examples":["Mary: Gee, I came in last again!  \nJane: Oh, well. You can't win them all.","“Can't win 'em all,” muttered Alice as she left the boss's office with nothing accomplished."],"media":[]}]

name: can't win
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that success is not possible for someone in a particular situation","examples":["I feel like I can't win. Nothing I do seems to make any difference.","You can't win when you're dealing with someone so unreasonable."],"media":[]}]

name: change one's mind
meanings: [{"name":"to change one's decision or opinion about something","examples":["He wasn't going to come, but at the last minute he changed his mind.","Sally: As of last week, they said you are leaving. Changed your mind?  \nBill: No. I'm leaving for sure.","Tom: Well, have you changed your mind?  \nSally: Absolutely not!"],"media":[]}]

name: You clean up well / You clean up good
meanings:
[{"name":"appears decent and well-groomed after a little effort.","examples":["Kate: How do I look? 
Jane: You clean up pretty well, Kate.","Jane: It's just been a while since I've seen you like this. You clean up good. 
Kate: Really? Well, thank you.","Jane: It took me a couple to find one in my size. 
Kate: But um... you clean up well."],"media":[]}]

name: You couldn't  / You wouldn't / You wouldn't do that
meanings: [{"name":"an indication of disbelief that someone might do something.","examples":["Bill: I'm going to run away from home! Jane: You wouldn't!","Bill: I get so mad at my brother, I could just strangle him. Tom: You couldn't do that!","Jane: Do I need to shout it out in the airport? Kate: You wouldn't do that.\nJane: Oh, I will."],"media":[]}]

name: you/you'd better believe it
meanings: [{"name":"used to indicate that the speaker emphatically agrees with a statement or sentiment; a way of emphasizing a previous statement","examples":["\"Do you think they can win?\" \"You/You'd better believe it!\"","Bill: This food is so bad. It will probably stunt my growth.  \nTom: You'd better believe it!"],"media":[]}]

name: get onto
meanings: [{"name":"to start to do or deal with (something)","examples":["\"We need someone to send out the invitations.\" \"I'll get onto it right away.\""],"media":[]},{"name":"to start to talk about something","examples":["How did we get onto this topic?","How did we get on to (the subject of) your grandmother's cat?","Every time I talk to her, we seem to get onto the subject of work."],"media":[]}]

name: the place to be
meanings: [{"name":"a place where many people go and where exciting things happen","examples":["This restaurant is the place to be on Saturday nights.","Switzerland is going to be the place to be this summer."],"media":[]}]

name: vamoose
meanings: [{"name":"to go away or disappear; to depart quickly; Get out!; Go away! (From Spanish vamos, “let's go.”)","examples":["Go on, you kids, vamoose!","His wife vamoosed to California.","It's getting late, so we had better vamoose.","Bob: Now, come on. Vamoose. Get out of the way. \nBill:  I'm going! I'm going!"],"media":[]}]

name: You wanna know something? / You know something?
meanings: [{"name":"used to get someone's attention; an expression used to open a conversation or switch to a new topic; ","examples":["John: Do you want to know something? Sue: What? \nJohn: Your hem is torn.","Hey, you know something? I'm hungry.","Bill: Hey, Tom! Know something? Tom: What is it?\nBill: It's really hot today. Tom: Don't I know it!"],"media":[]},{"name":"used to emphasize the statement that comes after it","examples":["You know something? I never trusted her.","She lied to me again, but you know something? I really just don't care anymore."],"media":[]}]

name: We all gotta go sometime
meanings: [{"name":"Death is inevitable. (A way to make light of death. Never said in sympathy.)","examples":["Bob: I was very surprised to hear of Fred's death. Jane: Yes, it was so sudden. \nBob: Well, we all gotta go sometime.","Ann: Careful, Tom, you'll fall and kill yourself!  \nTom: So? We all gotta go sometime."],"media":[]}]

name: do dinner / do lunch
meanings:
[{"name":"have dinner or lunch together","examples":["We should do dinner some time.","Amy: Well, I was thinking we could have a ladies lunch today.
Jane: Amy, I wish I could do lunch today, but I'm currently out of town.","I couldn't get a reservation for the night of my birthday. so we'll have to do dinner Friday night.","Jane: Just meet my friend Amy for lunch at the Southern Grill.
Kate: No, I can't do lunch. I already made plans with Sophie.","Sophie: What are your plans tonight? You should come to Kate's fashion show.
Amy: Oh, no. Actually, We're just gonna be doing dinner at the loft.","Grandma gets here at noon. Are you sure you won't do lunch?"],"media":[]}]

name: Well said
meanings: [{"name":"You said that very well, and I agree.","examples":["As Sally sat down, Mary complimented her, “Well said, Sally. You made your point very well.”","Jane: I think what John is doing is terrible.\nKate: Yes, well said, Jane."],"media":[]}]

name: We're all standing behind you / We're all behind you / We're behind you
meanings: [{"name":"Everyone is supporting you and is on your side","examples":["I know that things are going badly for you, but you have our support. We're all standing behind you.","I promise, your father and I will stand behind you","Just know we're 100% behind you.","Your mum and I are behind you all the way, 'cause we're a family, and you mean the world to us."],"media":[]}]

name: stand behind
meanings: [{"name":"to support (someone or something)","examples":["I'll stand behind you no matter what you decide to do.","I'll stand behind your decision 100 percent."],"media":[]}]

name: What does that prove? / What would that prove?
meanings: [{"name":"So what?; That does not mean anything. (A defensive expression. The heaviest stress is on that.)","examples":["Tom: It seems that you were in the apartment the same night that it was robbed. Bob: So, what does that prove?  \nTom: Nothing, really. It's just something we need to keep in mind.","Rachel: You're late again on your car payment.  \nJane: What does that prove? Rachel: Simply that you can't afford the car, and we are going to repossess it."],"media":[]}]

name: what's new?
meanings: [{"name":"used as a friendly greeting; What things have happened since we last met?","examples":["Hey man, what's new?","Mary: Greetings, Jane. What's new? Jane: Nothing much.","Bob: What's new? Tom: Not a whole lot."],"media":[]}]

name: Where can I wash up?
meanings: [{"name":"a way of asking where the toilet or bathroom is without referring to one's need to use it. (Of course, this is also appropriate to ask where one can wash one's hands.)","examples":["The minute Joe got to the house, he asked Fred, “Where can I wash up?”","Bob: Where can I wash up? \nBill: Let me show you."],"media":[]}]

name: thanks a million
meanings: [{"name":"thank you very much","examples":["Hey, thanks a million for your help.","\"I've done what you asked.\" \"Thanks a million!\"","(humorous) \"I'll let you wash the dishes today.\" \"Thanks a million.\""],"media":[]}]

name: That's enough for now
meanings: [{"name":"No more of that for now.; Please stop for a while.","examples":["Mary: Here, have some more cake. Do you want a larger piece?  \nBill: Oh, no. That's enough for now.","Bill: Shall I cut a little more off this tree, lady, or save the rest till spring?  \nJane: No, that's enough for now."],"media":[]}]

name: old-school / old school
meanings: [{"name":"old-fashioned; not modern","examples":["He was very old-school in his approach to management.","Your Nana's old school.","Dude, he's totally old school, not to mention just plain old.","Technology means hackers. We're going old school."],"media":[]}]

name: too bad
meanings: [{"name":"used to show that one is sorry or feels bad about something","examples":["It's too bad that Jane and Kate are leaving the city.","That's too bad. I wanna go to his concert Friday, but it's sold out."],"media":[]},{"name":"used in an ironic way to show that one is not sorry or does not feel bad about something","examples":["\"But I need your help!\" \"(That's just) Too bad.\""],"media":[]}]

name: That's what I'm talking about
meanings: [{"name":"This (or that) is definitely what I want or mean. (Often the speaker has not actually talked about the subject before.) ","examples":["Andy: Well, Don, it's eight o'clock, and here I am. Right on time. \nDon: That's what I'm talking about. Promptness!","Hey, I think I like the red one best. Yeah! That's what I'm talking about."],"media":[]}]

name: that's why
meanings: [{"name":"a tag on the end of a statement that is an answer to a question beginning with why. (Shows a little impatience.)","examples":["Mary: Why do you eat that awful peppermint candy? \nTom: Because I like it, that's why!","Jane: You broke Kate's chair?\nBob: I thought I did, that's why I replaced it with mine."],"media":[]}]

name: by chance
meanings: [{"name":"accidentally; randomly; without planning; If something happens by chance, it happens without being planned or intended, or without any known cause","examples":["They met by chance.","Did you by chance read my article?","We met, quite by chance, in the supermarket.","The date was not chosen by chance."],"media":[]}]

name: (There's) no point in
meanings: [{"name":"There is (no longer) any purpose in doing something","examples":["So there is no point in being here, you can start the car.","No point in hanging on to it.","I see no point in discussing this further.","No point in dragging it out."],"media":[]}]

name: those days
meanings: [{"name":"a period of time in the past","examples":["Remember when we were kids and life was easy? Well, those days are gone.","In those days, women weren't allowed to own property.","No one knew in those days what caused the disease."],"media":[]}]

name: turn things around
meanings: [{"name":"to reorganize and improve something","examples":["They've just hired a really energetic new CEO who did very well at her last post. They're hoping she can really turn things around.","As far as future profits go, another quarter of high earnings will turn things around."],"media":[]}]

name: says who?
meanings:
[{"name":"used when you are arguing with someone, to show that you do not accept or agree with what they say; Who do you think you are to say that? ","examples":["You're the best? Says who?","Tom: Fred, you sure can be dumb sometimes. Fred: Says who? 
Tom: Says me!","Bill: Custom coasters a very effective marketing tool. 
Bob: Says who? The guy who invented custom teapot cozies?
","Jane: I'm the boss now. Kate: What? Says who?
Jane: Says this."],"media":[]}]

name: Says you!
meanings: [{"name":"It is just you who are saying that, so it does not matter","examples":["Bill: I think you're headed for some real trouble. Bob: Says you!","Fred: Says who? Tom: Says me! Fred: Aw, says you!","Jane: That's a very bad idea.\nKate: Says you."],"media":[]}]

name: see someone as
meanings: [{"name":"to consider someone to be someone or something; to picture someone as someone or something","examples":["Don 't take this wrong, I just don't see you as a mom somehow.","I don't see her as a 12-year-old girl.","I'm just... I'm so tired of you seeing me as a failure."],"media":[]}]

name: see someone around
meanings: [{"name":"to notice someone in some of the places one often goes to","examples":["\"Have you met the new guy yet?\" \"No, but I've seen him around.\""," Ooh, I haven't seen you around. Are you new?","Jane: Yeah, that's her daughter Masha.\nKate: Really? iIhaven't seen her around here. Where is she visiting from?","My friend saw him around here this morning."],"media":[]}]

name: (I'll) see you in a little while/bit
meanings: [{"name":"a phrase indicating that the speaker will see the person spoken to within a few hours at the most","examples":["John: I'll see you in a little while. Jane: Okay. Bye till later.","Sally: I have to get dressed for tonight. Jane: I'll pick you up about nine. See you in a little while. \nSally: See you.","Okay, I'll see you in a little bit."],"media":[]}]

name: Seriously? / Honestly?
meanings: [{"name":"Do you really mean that?","examples":["Father: I got a raise today, but higher taxes will eat up almost all of it. \nMother: Seriously? How can we ever expect to get ahead?","Honestly? You really think you've finished this report? No way!"],"media":[]}]

name: shut up about it
meanings:
[{"name":"Do not tell anyone about it.","examples":["Bill: I heard that you had a little trouble with the police. 
Tom: Just shut up about it! Do you hear?","Andrew: Didn't you once appear in a movie? 
Alice: Shut up about it. No one has to know.","Jane: People who surf in that beach never shut up about it. 
Kate: Kinda true."],"media":[]}]

name: Slip me some skin! / Give me five!
meanings: [{"name":"Sl. Slap my hand! (As a greeting or to show joy, etc.)","examples":["“Yo, Tom! Give me five!” shouted Henry, raising his hand.","Bob: Hey, man! Slip me some skin.\nBill: How you doing, Bob?"],"media":[]}]

name: so much as

extraDetails: [["Usage today",["As long as → more common in everyday English.","So long as → slightly more formal or old-fashioned, but still widely understood."]],["Grammatical Distinction",["\"So long as\" and \"as long as\" are usually interchangeable when they mean \"provided that\" or \"on the condition that.\"","\"As long as\" can be used for literal comparisons of length (e.g., \"The rope is as long as the tree\"). ","\"So long as\" cannot be used for literal length comparisons, except in negative constructions (e.g., \"not so long as\").","\"As long as\" has another very common meaning related to duration (\"for the entire time that\"), while \"so long as\" is less commonly used that way in modern English."]]]

name: in a long time
meanings: [{"name":"typically follows negative constructions like \"have not,\" \"did not,\" or \"had not,\" indicating that the last occurrence of an action was far in the past; measures the time elapsed between two points, such as the last time you did something and now","examples":["He said that he hasn't been happy in a long time.","I haven't heard you sing that in a long time.","I haven't thought about him in a long time.","I know that we haven't talked in a long time.","I haven't felt this happy in a long time..","We haven't been happy in a long time.","I haven't worked this hard in a long time."],"media":[]},{"name":"used with phrases like: \"for the first time in a long time\"","examples":["I'll tell you, Jane, for the first time in a long time I feel happy.","I saw Masha for the first time in a long time.","For the first time in a long time, they're going on a vacation.","For the first time in a long time, I'm finishing on time or even a little early.","I think for the first time in a long time, I might actually be happy."],"media":[]},{"name":"can be used with a comparative or superlative form","examples":["I probably had the most fun that I have had in a long time.","This is the sunniest day we've had in a long time.","This is the best meal I've had in a long time.","Well, you've seemed happier than I've seen you in a long time.","I want this hospital more than I've wanted anything in a long time."],"media":[]}]

name: ever since

name: center around / center on

name: stand down

name: lift off
meanings: [{"name":"[for a plane or rocket] to move upward, leaving the ground","examples":["The rocket lifted off exactly on time.","As the plane was lifting off, a piece of the fuel tank broke off and hit the wing.","The rocket blew up shortly after lift-off.","Living in Florida, we get to see lift-offs up close."],"media":[]}]

name: at last / at long last
meanings: [{"name":"finally; after a long wait","examples":["The train has come at last."," At last, we have gotten something to eat.","At last you've come home.","He has agreed, at long last, to give his version of events.","Here we are. extraDetails: [["Emphasis on Duration",["Unlike the simpler \"finally\" or \"at last,\" adding the word \"long\" specifically highlights that the wait felt interminable or that significant obstacles were overcome. "," It emphasizes the extended duration of the anticipation and often conveys a strong sense of relief, satisfaction, or impatience that the event has finally occurred."]],["Emotional Weight",[" It frequently carries an emotional tone, suggesting the speaker is relieved or pleased that the wait is over."]],["Positioning",["It can be placed at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence for emphasis (e.g., \"At long last, the rain stopped,\" or \"The rain stopped at long last\"). "]]]

name: spin out
meanings: [{"name":"If a vehicle spins out, it loses control and slides around and around, usually fast, and often leaves the road","examples":["He lost control of the wheel and jammed on the brakes as the car spun out in a full 360 degrees.","The car spun out, slamming into a concrete wall and bursting into flame."],"media":[]},{"name":"to prolong something; to make something such as an activity or story last longer than usual or necessary, or as long as possible","examples":["Was there really any need to spin the whole process out so long?","Why did they spin out the graduation ceremony for such a long time?","Can we spin our holiday out for a few more days?","Somehow, she managed to spin her story out so that it took her the whole train journey to tell it."],"media":[]}]

name: spoiling for a fight

name: spot check
meanings: [{"name":"a quick examination of a few members of a group instead of the whole group","examples":["The police are doing spot checks on motorists to test alcohol levels.","A spot check revealed that many students are out with flu.","Lenders can make spot checks to see whether you have defaulted on past loans."],"media":[]}]

name: spread like wildfire
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. [for something] to spread rapidly; If disease or news spreads like wildfire, it quickly affects or becomes known by more and more people","examples":["The news spread like wildfire.","Once one child in the school has the infection, it spreads like wildfire.","Rumors spread like wildfire when people are excited.","This disease will spread like wildfire when it gets going."],"media":[]}]

name: squared away / square away
meanings: [{"name":"arranged or properly taken care of; to complete all necessary arrangements for something or someone; to finish dealing with a piece of work or a problem","examples":["Is Ann squared away in her dorm room yet?","I will talk to you when I am squared away.","I've got my tickets and hotel squared away.","The dishes are done and the kids are all squared away.","If the budget is not squared away by July 1 the state plans to lay off employees.","He took that boy's death pretty hard, but he's squared away.","Let me just square all this stuff away, okay?"],"media":[]}]

extraDetails: [["Origin",["The verb \"mull\" originally referred to grinding grain or spices into powder, or heating and spicing wine (mulled wine). ","The metaphor suggests that just as spices need time to infuse into wine, ideas need time to \"steep\" in the mind to be fully understood."," It implies a slow, deliberate process of weighing pros and cons, rather than making a quick or impulsive choice.","You cannot \"mull over\" something instantly; the phrase inherently requires a passage of time (hours, days, or weeks)."]],["Quick comparison",["Mull over → Suggests more prolonged, careful thought.","Think over → General, everyday expression.","Sleep on it → Delay the decision until after some time, often overnight.","Ponder →  Think deeply "]]]

name: cloud over
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. ","The day will start warm and sunny, but it will start to cloud over before lunchtime.","It's starting to cloud over and I'm afraid it's going to rain."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. [for something once clear] to become opaque; to become clouded; to become blurry, dubious, or ominous","examples":["My vision seemed to cloud over, and I could see very little.","The mirror clouded over as the steam rose from the hot water in the sink.","The outlook is clouding over."],"media":[]},{"name":"If a person's face clouds over, they suddenly look unhappy or worried:","examples":["At the mention of her dead husband, her face clouded over."],"media":[]}]

name: cloud up
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. name: pour down (on someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to flow or flood into something","examples":["The rain poured into the open window.","I left the window open and the rain just poured in."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. [for people or things] to continue to arrive in great numbers","examples":["Cards and letters are still pouring in.","Bob had just started his practice, and, apparently, the money was pouring in."],"media":[]},{"name":"to guide a flow of liquid into something","examples":["She poured the lemonade into the pitcher and carried it to the porch.","She held the glass and poured in the lemonade."],"media":[]}]

name: pour out one's feelings/heart/soul

name: pour out
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. name: pour over
meanings: [{"name":"to flood over someone or something","examples":["The water from the broken dam poured all over the rocks standing at its base.","The spilled milk poured over my lap."],"media":[]},{"name":"to cover or douse someone or something with something","examples":["As I poured the cooling water over myself, I felt relaxed for the first time since I began the long hike.","Mary poured some milk over her cereal."],"media":[]}]

name: pouring rain
meanings: [{"name":"very heavy rain; rain falling in large drops and with a lot of force","examples":["I waited in the pouring rain for the next bus.","The children's clothes were soaked after they played out in the pouring rain."],"media":[]}]

name: agree with someone
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to hold the same opinion or judgment as someone else; If you agree with someone, you believe that they are right.","examples":["I simply do not agree with you!","Are you saying you agree with them?","I'm agreeing with you."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. [for something] to be acceptable to someone as food. extraDetails: [["Origin",["Cockney Rhyming Slang (Most Accepted): The term likely derives from the Cockney rhyme \"Duke of Yorks\" → \"forks\".  In 18th and 19th-century slang, \"forks\" referred to fingers or hands (resembling the prongs of a fork). Over time, \"Duke of Yorks\" was shortened to \"dukes\". ","Late 19th Century: The phrase \"put up your dukes\" (raise your fists to fight) became common in both the UK and US.","1960s: The specific phrasal verb \"duke it out\" emerged in American English.  One of the earliest printed uses appeared in The San Mateo Times in 1964, referring to baseball teams competing for a title.  This marked the shift from purely physical fighting to broader competitive contexts."]]]

It was an accident.","Mary is in a snit because they didn't ask her to come to the shindig.","He left in a snit when they told him he'd have to wait another hour.","She got in a snit when she found out he was late.","One night, his trophy bimbo wife got into a snit, lit a curtain on fire with a cigarette, and burned the place to the ground."],"media":[]}]

name: in a stupor
meanings: [{"name":" in a dazed condition; in a condition in which one cannot concentrate or think","examples":["The drunk driver walked away from the car accident in a stupor.","In the morning, Mary remains in a stupor until she drinks coffee.","Bob, you drank yourself into a stupor and passed out?"],"media":[]}]

name: in advance
meanings: [{"name":" [of something given, paid, or provided] before it is due; before something happens","examples":["If you're coming to the party, please let me know in advance.","The bill isn't due for a month, but I paid it in advance.","I want my pay in advance.","I'm sorry in advance if this is putting too much pressure on you.","I had to book them weeks in advance.","So, thank you in advance for making us all feel welcome."],"media":[]}]

name: clear conscience
meanings: [{"name":"a knowledge or belief that one has done nothing bad or wrong; If you have a clear conscience about something, you do not feel guilty about it","examples":["At least now I can face him with a clear conscience.","I have no regrets, and can leave the company with a clear conscience.","She said that she had a completely clear conscience about her decision.","I'm finding it hard to continue to drive a petrol car with a clear conscience.","These desserts are great for people watching their weight as you can eat them with a clear conscience.","Well, I'm glad your conscience is clear."],"media":[]}]

name: guilty conscience
meanings: [{"name":"a feeling of guilt; a feeling of worry or unhappiness about something bad that you have done or feel responsible for","examples":["She had a guilty conscience.","You've got a guilty conscience - that's why you can't sleep.","His reaction suggests he may have a guilty conscience over the incident."],"media":[]}]

name: in addition (to something)
meanings: [{"name":"additionally; further; moreover; as an additional thing or person","examples":["The job requires a college degree and, in addition, at least two years of experience.","In addition, I would like for you to sweep the kitchen floor.","I put the books away, and in addition to that, I cleaned up my desk."],"media":[]}]

name: in any way, shape, or form
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. in any manner; under any circumstances or conditions (often used in negative statements)","examples":["That behavior is not acceptable in any way, shape, or form.","In no way shape or form was he ever involved with the Mafia.","I refuse to tell a lie in any way, shape, or form!","Please hear me. If I want your input in my life in any way, shape or form, I will ask for it. Until then, do us all a favor and shut up!","I assure you, no one is dying. The substance causing this odor is not toxic in any way, shape, or form. It's pickles.","It's not gonna help us in any way, shape or form."],"media":[]}]

name: in bad faith
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. without sincerity; with bad or dishonest intent; with duplicity; with no intention of honoring a promise","examples":["She signed the contract in bad faith.","It appears that you acted in bad faith and didn't live up to the terms of our agreement.","If you do things in bad faith, you'll get a bad reputation.","The company broke state laws and acted in bad faith when it cancelled the policy."],"media":[]}]

name: in broad daylight
meanings: [{"name":"during the day when people and things can be easily seen rather than at night; in the open light of day; clearly visible","examples":["The crime was committed in broad daylight.","Bill stood there in broad daylight, but we never saw him.","Bob, you could rob a bank in broad daylight?","I'm standing out on the street in broad daylight.","Someone stole a truck in broad daylight."],"media":[]}]

name: in between / in-between
meanings: [{"name":"located in the middle of two things, states, or possibilities; between the two times mentioned","examples":["The bath water is not hot or cold. It's in between.","A sandwich consists of two slices of bread with some other food in between.","I have breakfast at 7.30, lunch at 1.00, and sometimes a snack in between.","Classes are 40 minutes long with a 10 minute break in between.","I was born in India, moved to Germany in 2018, and worked for a few months in Denmark in between.","He knows quite a lot of French, but he's at an in-between stage and not fluent yet.","This suit isn't gray or blue, it's in-between."],"media":[]}]

name: in bulk
meanings: [{"name":"in large quantities","examples":["She buys rice in bulk.","I buy the same brand in bulk, and I've been doing this for as long as I can remember.","I found a website that sells tofu in bulk.","Jane: You buy that stuff in bulk, six months at a time, right?\nKate: Yeah.","Jane always bought office supplies in bulk to save money."],"media":[]}]

name: in case of something
meanings: [{"name":"in the event of something; if a problem occurs; if something happens; in the event that something happens","examples":["What do we do in case of fire?","In case of an accident, call the police.","In case of trouble, yell.","In case of fire, stairs are that way."],"media":[]}]

name: (hold someone/something) in contempt (of court)
meanings: [{"name":"showing disrespect for a judge or courtroom procedures; willful disobedience to or open disrespect of a court, judge, or legislative body","examples":["The judge found the juror in contempt of court when she screamed at the attorney.","He was refused to appear and was held in contempt.","If you don't comply, you could be found in contempt of court."],"media":[]},{"name":"feel contempt for someone or something; despise or strongly disapprove of someone or something; feel intense dislike for someone or something regarded as unworthy of respect or approval","examples":["I have long held them in contempt. [= I have long felt contempt for them.]","She glared at them in contempt.","I would never hold someone in contempt for making a few mistakes in English.","I think history will hold us in contempt for what we are doing to the planet.","He had always held sport in contempt, preferring intellectual pursuits."],"media":[]}]

name: in flight
meanings: [{"name":"while flying","examples":["A passenger became ill in flight and the pilot had to return to the airport.","I really don't care to eat in flight. I am too nervous.","Moments later, the rocket broke up in flight.","Dragonflies adjust their front and back wings in flight to conserve energy.","That bird is really taking off in flight."],"media":[]}]

name: in for it
meanings: [{"name":"certain to be punished; in trouble","examples":["If his parents find out what he's done, he'll be in for it.","Oh, you're in for it this time, Bob.","You'll be in for it when she finds out!","If your dad finds out where you've been, you'll be in for it!","If I don't get these figures to John by the end of today, I'll be in for it."],"media":[]}]

name: in denial
meanings: [{"name":"refusing to admit the truth or reality of something unpleasant; in a state of refusing to believe something that is true","examples":["People are in denial - they don't want to change.","I was in total denial about the real cause of the problems.","They have been in denial for the last ten years, and have totally refused to change the way they do things.","Mary was in denial about her illness and refused treatment.","Tom doesn't think he's an alcoholic because he's still in denial."],"media":[]}]

name: in dire straits
meanings: [{"name":"in a very bad or difficult situation","examples":["With its best player out of the game, the team found itself in dire straits.","We are nearly broke and need money for medicine. We are in dire straits.","We are in dire straits here, okay? We need a change of plan.","These kids are in dire straits, and the schools are doing nothing to help them!"],"media":[]}]

name: in disguise
meanings: [{"name":"wearing a disguise","examples":["I've heard that she sometimes travels around the country in disguise.","Everyone in disguise in this old ballroom.","Did you buy them in disguise? or Did someone buy them for you?"],"media":[]},{"name":"made to look like something else; presented as another thing","examples":["He says that the new fee is really just a tax increase in disguise.","A problem is just an opportunity in disguise.","Some confessions are just bragging in disguise.","You think Mike is a Bob in disguise?","Santa Claus was really the little child's father in disguise."],"media":[]}]

name: in due course / in due time / in good time / in the course of time / in time
meanings: [{"name":"in a normal or expected amount of time","examples":["The roses will bloom in due course.","Jane: Can we wrap this up at some point?\nBob: In due time.","The vice president will become president in due course.","I'll retire in due time.","Jane: Maybe you and I should do something.\nMike:  All in good time, Jane.","In time, things will improve.","It'll all work out in the course of time. "],"media":[]}]

name: in effect
meanings: [{"name":"in fact, or in practice; in substance; virtually; effectively","examples":["So in effect the government have lowered taxes for the rich and raised them for the poor.","There was fluid in his lungs, in effect reducing their capacity.","The report said, in effect, that if there was no change, the company would go under.","These measures would, in effect, nationalize the industry.","In effect, this new law will raise taxes for most people.","This policy harms domestic manufacturers. In effect, all our clothing will be made in foreign countries."],"media":[]}]

name: in exchange (for someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"in return for someone or something","examples":["I gave him chocolate in exchange for some cookies.","John gave Mary a book and got a sweater in exchange.","We will love you and support you and take care of you, but in exchange, you will show us a little bit of respect and obey our rules, which means doing your own chores.","She hires her abandoned daughter to fold laundry in exchange for paying her tuition?"],"media":[]}]

name: in existence
meanings: [{"name":"now existing; currently and actually being","examples":["Our city's getting a visit from Cleopatra's candy dish, the most priceless candy dish in existence.","The theatre company that they started is still in existence today.","All the oil in existence will not last the world for another century."],"media":[]}]

name: in good spirits
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. happy and cheerful; positive and looking toward the future, despite unhappy circumstances","examples":["The patient is in good spirits and that will speed her recovery.","Tom wasn't in very good spirits after he heard the bad news.","If you don't mind my asking, you seem in pretty good spirits."],"media":[]}]

name: high hopes
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. expecting something; a strong feeling that something good will happen or be true","examples":["We had high hopes of winning the game.","I was in hopes of getting there early.","We are in high hopes that John and Mary will have a girl.","I don't have high hopes for it, if that's what you're thinking.","I really have high hopes for my band."],"media":[]}]

name: in hock
meanings: [{"name":"in the possession of a pawnbroker; having something pawned","examples":["His gold watch is in hock.","Everything I own is in hock to the bank."],"media":[]},{"name":"in debt","examples":["After buying the luxury car, Bob was in hock for years.","We're already in hock up to our eyeballs.","He's in hock to the wrong people. (Implies danger as well as debt.)","We're always in hock to somebody.","The company's in hock after that deal.","He's in hock because he can't stop betting."],"media":[]}]

name: in someone's honor
meanings: [{"name":"as a way to show respect and admiration for (someone)","examples":["Susan, we wanna give you and Bob a proper welcome home, so we are having a dinner party in your honor.","I will continue to wear it, in his honor.","This is a party in your honor.","Whoever collects the most recyclable items will have the new playground renamed and dedicated in their honor.","Do you know she's throwing a party in Bob's honor?","How was your grandparents' party? Were there great huzzahs in your honor?"],"media":[]}]

name: in honor of someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"showing respect or admiration for someone or something","examples":["They're having a dinner in honor of the new coach.","The building was named in honor of the city's founder.","In honor of you coming home, we are making your favorite meal."],"media":[]}]

name: in its entirety / in their entirety
meanings: [{"name":"completely; until completely done or gone; with nothing left out","examples":["He played the song in its entirety.","His comments will be broadcast in their entirety.","But after being threatened with legal repercussions, the outlet deleted the story in its entirety.","My friends and I ate the two large pizzas in their entirety."],"media":[]}]

name: in league (with someone)
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. [of people] secretly cooperating, often to do something bad or illegal; working with someone especially to do something dishonest","examples":["He suspects that they are in league together against him.","She denies that she is in league with corrupt officials.","The county sheriff is in league with criminals.","The car thieves and some crooked police are in league to make money from stolen cars."],"media":[]}]

name: in spades
meanings: [{"name":"in large amounts or to a very great degree; in the best or most extreme way possible; extravagantly; If you have something in spades, you have a lot of it. If something happens in spades, it happens to a great degree.","examples":["A con artist needs charm, and she had it in spades.","They were having money problems in spades.","Last year we harvested almost no potatoes, but this year we're getting them in spades.","He succeeded at life in spades—honors degree, great career, rich wife, lovely children, and early retirement."],"media":[]}]

name: off-the-books / off the books
meanings: [{"name":"not reported or recorded; in a way that is not officially written down in a person's or company's financial records","examples":["Why would all the negotiations happen completely off the books? If he's hiding something, I don't know what.","These workers are getting paid in cash off the books.","Is he cheating the welfare and tax systems by earning money \"off the books\"?"],"media":[]},{"name":"removed from an official record, especially as a law","examples":["Civil rights groups worry that, once enacted, tough new laws may be difficult to get off the books.","The best part is, we can finally get Bob off the books."],"media":[]}]

name: pace back and forth / pace up and down
meanings: [{"name":"walk over and over the same short route nervously or anxiously; walk back and forth (in or around some place), as in fear, anger, anxiety, frustration, etc.","examples":["The leopard paced back and forth in its cage.","Later in Bob's bed room lair, Bob paced back and forth.","He paced up and down, waiting for the doctor to call.","She paced back and forth outside the courtroom."],"media":[]}]

name: like sardines
meanings: [{"name":"without enough room to move around","examples":["A large crowd of reporters was crammed/packed like sardines into a small room.","It was terribly crowded there. We were packed in like sardines.","The bus was full. The passengers were packed like sardines.","They packed us in like sardines. There was no room to breathe.","They packed us in like sardines. There was no room to breathe."],"media":[]}]
origin: From the way that many sardines are packed into a can.

name: paint over
meanings: [{"name":"cover (something) with a layer of paint","examples":["The suspect also defaced two religious statues, painting over their faces, police said.","Some kids messed up the display. They painted over the word \"good\". Then they rearranged the figures.","I just painted over one of the old paintings that he gave me","Bob painted over the rusty part of the fence.","The work crew was told to paint over the graffiti."],"media":[]}]

name: power play
meanings: [{"name":"a situation in which a person or organization tries to get an advantage by showing that they are more powerful than another","examples":["He made a power play to seize control of the company.","There may be a bit of power play going on here.","He engaged in endless machinations, negotiations, and power plays.","Bob: A power move? Some kind of power play?\nKate: Come on, guys. No.  It's not a power move! We're having a conversation.","Mr. Bob? But your power play go kaput."],"media":[]}]

name: go kaput
meanings: [{"name":"break; severely damaged, broken, or not working correctly","examples":["Our washing machine was working perfectly, and then suddenly it went kaput.","For instance, in situations where colleges or universities go bankrupt or go kaput, the law is pretty clear."],"media":[]}]

name: pander to someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"say, do or provide exactly what a person or group wants, especially when it is not acceptable, reasonable, or approved of, usually in order to get some personal advantage","examples":["It's not good the way she panders to his every whim.","Political leaders almost inevitably pander to big business.","She accused the other candidate of pandering to radical environmental groups."],"media":[]}]

name: parcel out
meanings: [{"name":"divide or share (something) among different people, groups, etc.;  divide something and give the separate parts to different people or at different times","examples":["The money was parceled out to local charities.","We need to stop parceling out the blame for this problem and start working on a solution.","She parcelled out the gifts to the other children.","More than $13,000 in awards will be parceled out, with $6000 going to the first-prize winner.","The grant was to be parceled out at $200,000 per year over five years."],"media":[]}]

name: paper trail
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. a series of records that is possible to examine to find out the sequence of things that happen. (*Typically: have ~; leave ~; make ~.)","examples":["You are required to keep a paper trail so that auditors may look over your work.","All I'm asking for is $5,000...Cash. That way there's no paper trail, nothing leading back to you.","We're gonna take whatever we want for free. There's gonna be no paper trail.","Jane: What did you do? Bob: I paid the judges in cash. There's no paper trail. \nJane: You bribed the judges?"],"media":[]}]

name: parlay something into something
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. exploit an asset in such a way as to increase its value to some higher amount; achieve success by using a small advantage or opportunity in an effective way","examples":["She is trying to parlay her temporary job into a full-time position. ","Alice parlayed her inheritance into a small fortune by investing in the stock market.","She parlayed $5,000 and years of hard work into a multimillion-dollar company.","He hoped to parlay his football skills into a college scholarship."],"media":[]}]

name: park it (somewhere)
meanings: [{"name":"sit down somewhere; sit down and get out of the way","examples":["Hey, park it! You're in the way.","Bob, park it over there in the corner. Stop pacing around. You make me nervous.","Kate: You can park it there. Oh, don't kid around here.\nJane: Your life's at stake. I wouldn't kid around."],"media":[]}]

name: partake in something
meanings: [{"name":"participate in something; take part in or experience something along with others","examples":["Jane does not care to partake in those childish games.","I would like to partake in the fun."],"media":[]}]

name: hail a cab / hail a taxi
meanings: [{"name":"wave or call for a cab or taxi to pull over and stop; signal to a taxi that you want to be picked up","examples":["You will stand in the cold and hail me a cab. Call me when it's curbside.","Do you mind hailing me a cab?","See if you can hail a cab. I don't want to walk home in the rain."],"media":[]}]

name: hoof it
meanings: [{"name":"move or travel on foot; walk or run","examples":["We quickly hoofed it down to the subway station.","If nobody gives us a ride, we'll have to hoof it.","She hoofed it home from the dance in her high-heeled shoes.","This has been really fun, but I think we'll just hoof it the rest of the way."],"media":[]}]

name: hone for someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"long for someone or something","examples":["Jimmy was honing for the red bicycle in the toy store window."],"media":[]}]

name: home free
meanings: [{"name":"safe and without problems; out of jeopardy; in a comfortable position with respect to some objective; having finished the difficult or dangerous part of an activity and sure of finishing it successfully","examples":["Once you get past the essay questions on the test, you're home free.","Everyone else had a lot of trouble with the bureaucrats, but we got home free.","The one man who could have put us all in jail is gone. We're home free.","I guess we got away. We're home free."],"media":[]}]

name: hot off the press
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. freshly printed; just released by a publisher; News that is hot off the press has just been printed and often contains the most recent information about something","examples":["Here is a copy of the new Harry Potter novel. It's hot off the press.","The leasing agreement, hot off the press."],"media":[]}]

name: for the rest
meanings: [{"name":"with regard to remaining issues or needs; used when you have already mentioned the important parts of something and you now want to mention the other less important parts","examples":["The salary in my new job is great, but (as) for the rest, I'm not impressed.","Take these now and come back tonight for the rest."],"media":[]}]

name: in the whole wide world
meanings: [{"name":"in the world","examples":["I felt like the luckiest girl in the whole wide world that day.","Who wants to meet the best chef in the whole wide world?","You are the bestest girl in the whole wide world.","I've never had a bestest friend in the whole wide world.","I'd be the proudest dad in the whole wide world."],"media":[]}]

name: go the distance
meanings: [{"name":"complete a course of action; manage to continue until the end of a competition; do the whole amount; play the entire game; run the whole race. (Originally sports use.)","examples":["This is going to be a long, hard project. I hope I can go the distance.","Actually, I think he got beat in that one. Well, he, uh, went the distance anyway."],"media":[]}]

name: in no mood to do something
meanings: [{"name":"not feeling like doing something; not wishing to do something","examples":["I'm in no mood to cook dinner tonight.","Mother is in no mood to put up with our arguing."],"media":[]}]

name: in one's glory
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. at one's happiest or best; in one's most happy, most beautiful, or most successful state","examples":["When she's on stage, she's in her glory.","The autumn leaves are in their glory now.","Are you here to revel in your glory?","When I go to the beach on vacation, I'm in my glory.","Sally is a good teacher. name: in one's mind's eye
meanings: [{"name":"in one's imagination or memory; in one's mind or imagination.
