She decided to design such a building.","Who's wearing that wedding dress in your mind's eye, Mom? Kate? Or me?"],"media":[]}]

name: in one's right mind
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. sane; rational and sensible. (Often in the negative.)","examples":["That was a stupid thing to do. You're not in your right mind.","You can't be in your right mind! That sounds crazy!","Betty was not in her right mind when she signed those forms.","I mean, who in their right mind... throws away a perfectly good case of eggs, this day and age?"],"media":[]}]

name: spare time
meanings: [{"name":"free time; the time when one is not working","examples":["I went to classes in my spare time.","In my spare time I garden.","How about when you're not working? What do you do in your spare time?","I'll try to paint the house in my spare time."],"media":[]}]

name: languish in some place
meanings: [{"name":"become dispirited in some place; weaken and fade away in some place; live in a state of depression or decreasing vitality","examples":["Kate languished in prison for her crime.","I spent over three days languishing in a stuffy hotel room.","We languished in the airport waiting room while they refueled the plane.","Plants languish in the drought."],"media":[]},{"name":"suffer neglect in a place","examples":["The bill languished in the Senate for months on end.","The children languished in the squalid conditions until the court intervened."],"media":[]}]

name: lash at someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"thrash or beat someone or something violently","examples":["The rain lashed at the windowpanes.","The mule driver lashed at his beasts with his whip."],"media":[]}]

name: lash against something
meanings: [{"name":"[for something, such as wind or water] to beat or whip heavily against something; hit with a lot of force against something","examples":["The angry waves lashed against the hull of the boat, frightening the people huddled inside.","The wind lashed against the house and kept us awake all night.","The sound of the rain lashing against the windows was deafening."],"media":[]}]

name: last-ditch
meanings: [{"name":"used to describe an act that is made at the end of a series of failures to solve a problem, and is not expected to succeed","examples":["They are now involved in a last-ditch attempt to save the steel plant.","It's a last-ditch attempt to raise the money.","This is a stunt, a last-ditch effort to save his client.","In a last-ditch attempt to win the election, he promised sweeping tax cuts."],"media":[]}]

name: late bloomer
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. a plant that blooms later than sim- ilar plants or that blooms late in the season","examples":["There are a few late bloomers in the garden, but by fall, we don't care much anymore about flowers."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. a person who finally develops a useful or superior skill or talents later than expected or desired; someone who becomes successful, attractive, etc., at a later time in life than other people","examples":["She was a late bloomer as a writer.","I guess I was a late bloomer.","At school she was a late bloomer, and it wasn't until she went to college that her talents became apparent."],"media":[]}]

name: lather up
meanings: [{"name":"[for soap] to develop thick suds when rubbed in water","examples":["This soap won't lather up, even when I rub it hard.","When the soap lathers up, spread the lather on your face and rub."],"media":[]},{"name":"[for one] to apply soap lather to one's body","examples":["He will spend a few minutes lathering himself up before he rinses.","He lathered up and then shaved.","He lathered up his face.","He lathered his face up in preparation for shaving."],"media":[]}]

name: laugh about someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"chuckle or giggle loudly about someone or something","examples":["Please don't laugh about Sue. It's not funny.","They were laughing about my haircut.","As tough as things got, we could always find something to laugh about.","What the hell are you laughing about, Bob?"],"media":[]}]

name: laughingstock
meanings: [{"name":"someone or something that is the target of ridicule; an object of ridicule","examples":["The mayor became a laughingstock.","After he passed out at the president's dinner, he became the laughingstock of all his colleagues.","He got utterly dominated by her in front of the whole school and was made a laughingstock."],"media":[]}]

name: launch into something
meanings: [{"name":"suddenly begin doing or saying (something) in an energetic way; start in doing something;  start saying something or criticizing something with a lot of energy or anger","examples":["He launched into a speech about doing one's duty.","He launched into a verbal attack on her handling of the finances.","Now, don't launch into lecturing me about manners again!","Tim's mother launched into a sermon about how to behave at the dinner table."],"media":[]},{"name":"start involving (oneself) in (something) in an energetic way","examples":["She launched herself enthusiastically into the campaign."],"media":[]}]

name: lavish on
meanings: [{"name":"give a large amount of (something) to (someone); give someone a lot, or too much, of something such as money, presents, or attention","examples":["She lavishes money on her grandchildren.","The committee lavished praise on the project.","She lavishes more attention on that dog than she does on her children.","The manager lavished all sorts of favors upon the new employee.","Susan lavished compliments on the cook."],"media":[]}]

name: lay a finger on / lay a hand on
meanings: [{"name":"harm someone even slightly; touch or hit (someone) —usually used in negative statements","examples":["I don't know what he's complaining about. I never laid a finger on him.","If you lay one finger on Ana, Bob will knock every tooth out of your mouth.","Don't you dare lay a finger on me.","If you lay a finger on her, you'll live to regret it!","He claims that he never laid a hand on her."],"media":[]}]

name: lay down
meanings: [{"name":"give up","examples":["Do you expect me to just lay down?","You really think I should just lay down and let them walk all over me?"],"media":[]}]

name: lay down one's arms
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. put one's gun, sword, club, etc., down; stop fighting; surrender; put down one's weapons and stop fighting","examples":["The prisoners were instructed to lay down their arms.","The soldiers laid down their arms and surrendered.","Bob, lay down your arms.","The soldiers refused to lay down their arms."],"media":[]}]

name: lay down one's life
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. sacrifice one's life for someone or something; give up one's life for a good purpose; die for a good cause","examples":["Would you lay down your life for your country?","There aren't many things for which I'd lay down my life.","Today we remember those who laid down their lives for their country."],"media":[]}]

name: play into the hands of someone / play into someone's hands
meanings: [{"name":"do something that one does not realize will hurt oneself and help someone else","examples":["You're playing into the hands of the enemy.","You're only playing into your accusers' hands by making accusations in return.","You played right into her hands. name: lay into someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"attack especially verbally;  attack, consume, or scold someone or something","examples":["Bob laid into the big plate of fried chicken.","The bear laid into the hunter.","My father really laid into me when I got home."],"media":[]}]

name: lay off (someone or something)
meanings: [{"name":"leave someone alone; leave undisturbed","examples":["I wish you'd just lay off.","Lay off me! name: wrestle with something
meanings: [{"name":"struggle with something large to move it around","examples":["He wrestled with the piano and finally got it to move.","The two men were wrestling with the heavy trunk for nearly ten minutes, trying to get it up the stairs."],"media":[]},{"name":"struggle with a difficult problem; struggle with a moral decision; give serious and careful thought to something","examples":["It's something you're going to have to wrestle with all of your life.","We wrestled with the problem and finally decided to go ahead.","I've been wrestling with the idea of switching careers for quite some time","Let me wrestle with this matter for a while longer."],"media":[]}]

name: the devil is in the details
meanings: [{"name":"overlooking small elements can lead to failure, requiring thorough attention to detail to ensure success; small details can cause unexpected problems or difficulties, even when something seems simple or successful at first.","examples":["Before signing the contract, read everything carefully — the devil is in the details.","Planning a wedding sounds fun, but the devil is in the details.","Cooking this recipe seems easy, but the devil is in the details.","Sounds simple, but the devil is in the details.","Be careful — the devil is in the details."],"media":[]}]

name: have a lot of ground to cover
meanings: [{"name":"There is a lot to do, discuss, learn, or complete in a limited time.","examples":["We have a lot of ground to cover before the deadline.","Well, we should probably get going. We've got a lot of ground to cover.","Let's start the meeting early — we have a lot of ground to cover.","I have a lot of ground to cover for tomorrow's exam.","We covered a lot of ground during the road trip. (= traveled many places)","We don't have much time, and there's a lot of ground to cover."],"media":[]}]

name: rust out
meanings: [{"name":"become damaged by rust; become thoroughly damaged by rust, resulting in holes or causing a machine to stop working correctly","examples":["My old bike rusted out after years in the rain.","The car's exhaust pipe rusted out.”","Our hot water heater rusted out and flooded the basement."],"media":[]}]

name: spaced it / spaced that / space something
meanings: [{"name":"forget something","examples":["Again, look, sorry about the gift. I totally spaced.","I totally spaced that!","Bob: Is there any way that you can scrape the money together today?\nJane: We have it. I took an extra shift yesterday, and I just spaced it."],"media":[]}]

name: swing back
meanings: [{"name":"return to a previous position, opinion, condition, direction, or state after changing away from it. (It suggests a movement from one side/state/opinion to another and then back again)","examples":["After experimenting with minimalism, designers swung back to colorful styles.","The door swung back and hit the wall.","She felt sad for a while but eventually swung back to her cheerful self.","I drop them to the safe house and swing back and take you to the pharmacy.","Call my cell phone when you pay it, I'll swing back at the end of the day."],"media":[]}]

name: whack job
meanings: [{"name":"someone who is very strange or has mental problems","examples":["Stay away from him - he's a real whack job.","Oh, yeah, he's a real deranged person. This kid's a real whack job."],"media":[]}]

name: all for someone or something / for someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"Fig. (completely) in favor of someone or something; supporting someone or something. (often used to express strong agreement with a proposal or idea,)","examples":["I am all for freedom of speech.","I'm all for anything that brings more customers.","Jane: Mike, I want to finish my law degree.\nMike: I'm all for it.","I am all for Kate spending time with her dad.","Hey, I'm all for anyone getting married if they want to.","Tom: There can't be any mistakes like before.\nBob: I'm all for that."],"media":[]}]

name: the stakes are high
meanings: [{"name":"a situation is very important because the possible consequences — success or failure — are serious or significant","examples":["The stakes are high because the loser today is walking off the mountain for 30 years.","This TV debate could determine who becomes president, so the stakes are high.","The stakes are high for the company because losing this contract could mean layoffs."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["“Stakes” originally refers to what can be won or lost in gambling, but in everyday English it means the risks, consequences, or importance involved."]]]

name: get in gear / put it in gear
meanings: [{"name":"get moving, speed up, or start working effectively; cause (something) to start working or becoming successful","examples":["We need to get in gear if we want to finish this project on time.","You better get in gear, young lady. You'll be late for school.","She finally got her career in gear.","Jane, the boys are waiting! Put it in gear.","Let's go do something. All right, ready? Let's put it in gear."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["It is a metaphor derived from driving a vehicle, where shifting from neutral into a gear is necessary for the car to move forward."]]]

name: to my eye
meanings: [{"name":"used when giving your opinion about the appearance of something or someone","examples":["You see, to my eye, she looks better without make-up.","Jane: She looks stunning in the clothes, don't you agree?\nKate: Mm-hmm, to my eye,like a goddess."],"media":[]}]

name: catch a movie
meanings: [{"name":"watch a movie, typically at a cinema.  It implies a casual, spontaneous plan to see a film, often with someone else, rather than a formal or pre-planned event.","examples":["Let's catch a movie this weekend.","Jane: What are you doing?\nKate: I'm gonna go catch a movie.","Hey, wanna catch a movie later?","Call it a day, maybe catch a movie or something?","I haven't caught a movie in theaters for months.","They decided to catch a movie while waiting for their train."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage",["It emphasizes the opportunity to see a movie while it is in release. It carries a sense of not missing out, similar to \"catching a train\" or \"catching a glimpse.\""]]]

name: on the down-low / on the down low
meanings: [{"name":"secret or secretly, so that only a small number of people know about something or someone; keeping something secret, private, or discreet","examples":["Jane: Uh, word to the wise?\nKate: Go ahead. I'd keep this on the down low.","I just think we should keep things on the down low.","He's on the down low, you know?","He told me on the down-low: \"This guy is dangerous.\""],"media":[]}]

name: I'm wired / she's wired
meanings: [{"name":"nervous or excited, for example because of a future event, or because you have drunk coffee or taken drugs","examples":["After their big day at the amusement park, the kids were too wired to sleep.","I guess it's just the way I'm wired. I got a job over in greenwood.","I'm wired. No way I'm falling asleep tonight.","You're supercharged. You're wired. You're ready for action.","I was totally wired before the interview.","She was wired. Looked like she'd been drinking coffee all night."],"media":[]}]

name: go back to one's old ways
meanings: [{"name":"return to previous habits or behaviors after a period of change","examples":["Promise we won't go back to our old ways.","He'll go back to his old ways and I don't want you two getting hurt.","So you're going back to your old ways?"],"media":[]}]

name: set the curve
meanings: [{"name":"achieve the highest score on a test or assignment; establish the standard, trend, direction, or expected level for others to follow","examples":["Bob is top of his class. He set the curve.","Her high exam score set the curve for the class.","This smartphone set the curve in mobile photography."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase comes from the idea of a grading curve or a performance curve, where one result influences how others are judged."]],["Synonyms",["set the standard","raise the bar","lead the trend","establish the benchmark"]]]

name: hippie-dippie
meanings: [{"name":"of, relating to, or reflecting the far-out styles and values of hippies","examples":["So you're into all that hippie-dippie healing thing?","Among all the hippie-dippie nonsense, ahem, I find this."],"media":[]}]

name: lo and behold
meanings: [{"name":"something that you say when you tell someone about something surprising that happened; used to express wonder or surprise","examples":["I was in Vienna sitting quietly in a café when, lo and behold, my cousin walked in.","I thought the meeting was canceled, but lo and behold, everyone was there."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The word \"lo\" is an archaic shortening of \"look\" , while \"behold\" means to see or observe. It functions as a dramatic or humorous cue that something significant has occurred, often contrasting with expectations. "]],["Usage",["It is frequently used in storytelling or conversation to emphasize a twist or an unexpected appearance."]]]

name: get hairy
meanings: [{"name":"a situation is becoming stressful, difficult, complicated, or dangerous. It is commonly used in casual conversation, especially when a situation starts becoming hard to manage.","examples":["The taxi ride got a little hairy.","When the deadline approaches, things can get a little hairy.","Driving home is going to get hairy if there is ice on the road.","The project got hairy after the deadline was moved up.","Things got hairy during the storm.","The game got hairy in the final minutes."],"media":[]}]

name: fly too close to the sun
meanings: [{"name":"become overly ambitious, overconfident, or reckless, leading to failure or trouble","examples":["The company flew too close to the sun by expanding too quickly.","I think you've been flying too close to the sun.","Yeah, well, you flew too close to the sun, my friend.","He flew too close to the sun with risky investments.","I tried handling too many responsibilities at once and flew too close to the sun."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase originates from the Greek myth of Icarus, who ignored his father's advice and flew too high in wings made of feathers and wax, causing the sun's heat to melt the wax and plunge him into the sea."]]]

name: too close to call
meanings: [{"name":"too close to say who will win","examples":["The election is still too close to call.","As of Wednesday evening, that race is too close to call because the vote counts are nearly tied.","I honestly don't know which dress I prefer; they are both fantastic, so it is too close to call."],"media":[]}]
origin: used to describe a situation, such as a sports match or political election, where the outcome is so uncertain and the margin between competitors is so narrow that it is impossible to predict a clear winner.

name: make it easy on someone / make things easy on someone
meanings: [{"name":"simplify a task or reduce the effort required to save time or work; reduce someone's burden, stress, or difficulty","examples":["I'll make it easy on you by organizing the files before the meeting.","It's all hard. But that's why we're here. To help make it easy on each other.","Why would anyone in this house make things easy on me?","I decided to make it easy on myself.","We made it easy on the customers by simplifying the checkout process."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Comparison with \"Go Easy On\"",["Make it easy on: Focuses on simplifying tasks and reducing workload. ","Go easy on: Focuses on reducing pressure or criticism, often as a magnanimous gesture to spare someone hardship."]]]

name: playing house / play house
meanings: [{"name":"children pretending to be adults in a domestic setting, such as mimicking family roles like cooking, cleaning, or caring for dolls.","examples":["The kids were playing house in the living room.","You gave up a brilliant career to play house in the suburbs.","She always wanted to be the mom when they played house."],"media":[]}]

name: that was then, this is now
meanings: [{"name":"Things were different in the past, but the situation has changed now.","examples":["I used to trust him completely, but after the betrayal, that was then, this is now.","We were close friends in high school, but that was then, this is now—we've grown apart.","Back then we had no money. That was then, this is now.","Yes, we argued a lot before, but that was then, this is now.","Bob: No, are you serious? You can't even do two sit-ups.\nJane: That was then. This is now."],"media":[]}]

name: twist up
meanings: [{"name":"move upward in a twisting path","examples":["The smoke twisted up into the sky.","As the car twisted up the narrow path, we got a good view of the valley. "],"media":[]},{"name":"become twisted","examples":["The rope twisted up and had to be unwound."],"media":[]}]

name: what's done is done
meanings: [{"name":"past actions or events cannot be changed and must be accepted as final and move forward; Something has already happened and cannot be changed, so there's no use worrying about it anymore, so accept the past and move forward.","examples":["Bob, what's done is done. You need to let it go.","Mike: I'm really sorry about tonight.\nJane: What's done is done. The question is, what's next?","I'm sorry for what I did. But I don't intend to keep apologizing for it. What's done is done, and Tom and I are moving on.","What's done is done, and if you can't get over it, There's nothing I can say that'll make you stop hating me."],"media":[]}]

name: never hear the end of it
meanings: [{"name":"used to say that someone will keep talking about something for a long time; be told repeatedly about something","examples":["We'll never hear the last of it if they win that competition.","If you tell your mother, I would never, never hear the end of it, so please... can we just keep this between us?","If we lose to the other team, we'll never hear the end of it."],"media":[]}]

name: and so on / and so forth
meanings: [{"name":"with additional related or similar things mentioned (but not specified); and other things; and the rest","examples":["We can analyze the food for calories, cholesterol, minerals, and so forth.","Economic growth makes us all richer, provides jobs, and so on.","Next time, don't stand there like an idiot. Move your feet, run and so forth.","I need some help getting ready for dinner, setting the table, and so on."],"media":[]}]

name: while it lasts
meanings: [{"name":"enjoy or take advantage of something because it is temporary and won't continue indefinitely","examples":["The weather is perfect—enjoy it while it lasts!","This deal is only valid today—grab it while it lasts.","Well, It was fun while it lasted. (positive experience that has now ended, often with nostalgia or resignation.)","He got promoted but was demoted a month later. It was good while it lasted.","You better go enjoy your party while it lasts.","You having a good time, lady? Enjoy it while it lasts.","I'm enjoying it while it lasts."],"media":[]}]

name: in the wind
meanings: [{"name":"about to happen; If something is in the wind, people are talking about it and it may happen, but no one is sure","examples":["Rumors of a takeover are in the wind.","There is something in the wind. We'll find out what it is soon.","There are some major changes in the wind. Expect these changes to happen soon."],"media":[]},{"name":"If someone is in the wind, they are missing, especially after escaping","examples":["The suspects are in the wind.","Jane: Still nothing from Bob?\nKate: In the wind. Not a word.","Bob heard that Tom wasn't at his place and word is, he asked for time off at Cho's. The guy's in the wind."],"media":[]}]

name: not a word
meanings:
[{"name":"tell someone to stay completely silent about something or not reveal a secret; Don't tell anyone; Keep it secret; Say nothing about it","examples":["Not a word to anyone.","I bought her a birthday gift — not a word to her, okay?","They're planning to change jobs, but not a word has been announced yet.","If you tell Dad, I'm in trouble. Not a word!","You saw nothing and heard nothing — not a word.","Bob, not a word of this to anyone, you understand?","I promise, not a word of this to your father."],"media":[]},{"name":"complete silence","examples":["He sat through the whole meeting and said not a word. (= he didn't speak at all)","Jane: Did she say anything?
Kate: No, not a word.","Jane: Nobody's heard from Bob?
Kate: Not a word.
"],"media":[]}]

name: butter the wrong bread
meanings: [{"name":"support, prioritize, or depend on the wrong person, opportunity, or choice — especially when resources, time, or consequences matter; invest time and energy in the wrong person or opportunity","examples":["He can't afford to butter the wrong bread right now","I can't afford to butter the wrong bread here."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The imagery comes from buttering bread: butter is limited, so wasting it on the “wrong bread” symbolizes wasting effort or resources on the wrong target."]]]

name: never heard from again / never heard from someone again
meanings: [{"name":"a person disappeared from contact or public attention, and nobody received any more news, messages, or information about them afterward","examples":["John left work early one day and was never heard from again.","He left town and was never heard from again.","After the scandal, the company was never heard from again.","The sailor went out during the storm and was never heard from again.(Nobody ever got news about him afterward.)","I went home with you. The next morning, you were gone, and I never heard from you again.","My wife left me. And no one ever heard from her again. Not me, not her family.","She ran off, sweetie. We never heard from her again."],"media":[]}]

name: quit it
meanings: [{"name":"Stop it; used to tell someone to stop doing something usually because it is annoying or irritating","examples":["He was kicking the back of her seat until she finally told him to quit it.","Will you quit it?","My brother keeps poking me; I told him to quit it or I'd hit him.","Quit it! Mom will hear if you keep shouting."],"media":[]}]

name: keep it that way
meanings: [{"name":"maintain a current situation or condition exactly as it is, without making changes","examples":["You have a great understanding with your colleagues, so keep it that way.","This place is now secure. We're gonna keep it that way.","We are having a nice time. Let's try and keep it that way.","When you find something that isn't yours, keep it that way."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Synonyms",["\"leave it as it is\" ","\"maintain the status quo\"","\"don't change a thing\""]]]

name: good for it
meanings: [{"name":"able to pay back a loan","examples":["Why won't you lend me the money? You know I'm good for it.","I can personally guarantee that she's good for it.","Well, I'm a bit cash-strapped at the moment, but, Karen knows I'm good for it.","We're good for it. We pay our debts.","Bob, he'll pay you the rest later. He's totally good for it. Tom's a stand-up guy."],"media":[]}]

name: thin out
meanings: [{"name":"spread out; become less dense; make something less dense, crowded, or thick by removing some of them","examples":["The crowd began to thin out as we got a little farther from the theater. (= People leaving a space, making it less crowded )","The trees began to thin out as we got higher up the mountain.","Thin out the seedlings. (= Removing excess plants to allow remaining ones to grow better)","Thin out the sauce with broth. (= Diluting a mixture or liquid to reduce its strength or thickness)","The fog thinned out."],"media":[]}]

name: because I say so / because I said so
meanings:
[{"name":"used to assert authority or demand obedience without providing an explanation or justification. ","examples":["We are leaving now because I said so.","Bob: You have to stay inside. Jane: Why? They said it was safe out now.
Bob: Because I said so. Now stop your sass. Go play.","Bob: Why should we leave now?
Mike: Because I said so. No more questions, okay, buddy?","Bob: Why do I have to do it?
Jane: 'Cause I said so. Bob: You can't just tell me what to do.","Jane: Clean it now. Kate: Why?
Jane: Because I said so."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Typical usage",["Parents telling children to obey without questioning.","Beyond parenting, it can be used in broader social or professional settings to assert power and avoid accountability, reinforcing the idea that the person in charge is always right. "]]]

name: When I say so / until I say so
meanings:
[{"name":"used to indicate that an action should occur specifically when the speaker gives the order","examples":["When I say so, you must jump.","Don't start the meeting until I say so.","Nurse: If you don't rest, it'll never get better. Patient: I shouldn't have been exercising.
Nurse: No, ma'am. Not till the doctor says so.
","Jane: You're not going anywhere. Kate: For how long?
Jane: Until I say so.","But you have to wait until I say so to open it."],"media":[]}]

name: if you say so / you say so
meanings:
[{"name":"If that's what you believe/say; used to acknowledge a statement while privately doubting or disagreeing with it. It serves as a polite way to end a conversation or concede a point without engaging in further argument","examples":["Jane: I only studied for ten minutes, but I'm sure I'll get an A.
Kate: If you say so. (Meaning: I doubt this is true, but I won't argue.)","Bob: This new coffee shop is the best in the city.
Mike: Okay, if you say so!  I'll give it a try. (Meaning: I haven't been there, but I trust your taste.)","Jane: You definitely knocked that vase over.
Bob: If you say so. (Meaning: I deny this, but I'm done discussing it.)","Bob: I'm the best cook in the family.
Jane: If you say so. (Meaning: I don't really agree.)","Bob: We're friends.
Jane: You say so."],"media":[]}]

name: you said so / as you said
meanings: [{"name":"That is what you previously said.; Because you said it.","examples":["No, we're not kids, we're monkeys, you said so.","Jane: Big sister, I think he's a cheeky fox. Kate: A what?!\nJane: He said so."],"media":[]}]

name: I hear things / be hearing things
meanings: [{"name":"I've heard rumors; I know some information","examples":["Jane: Well, are you okay? Bob: I'm fine.\nJane: But I've been hearing things, that I just can't believe. So it's true?","I hear things about what's going on in the office\"","I hear things about the new teacher. I'm sorry, I must be hearing things. (indicating doubt about the sound's existence) ","There's no one at the door. You're hearing things.","I thought someone called my name, but I must be hearing things.”","She swears she heard someone open the door, but I think she's just hearing things."],"media":[]}]

name: get enough spunk up / get the spunk up (to do something)
meanings: [{"name":"work up enough courage to do something; show spirit or courage","examples":["I wanted to do it, but I couldn't get the spunk up.","You've got to spunk up and tell your boss you deserve that promotion.”"],"media":[]}]

name: feel my head / feel my forehead / feel one's head / feel one's forehead
meanings: [{"name":"Touch my head and tell whether it's hot or not.","examples":["My arm's kind of numb. Bob, can you feel my head? Am I hot?","Feel my head one more time. I'm sure I'm running hot this time.","Jane: It feels like bees are buzzing in my head. Feel my head. Kate: Why?\nJane: I just want you to know how hot I am.","Jane: I don't feel so good.\nKate: Let me feel your forehead."],"media":[]}]

name: spread around something
meanings: [{"name":"distribute news, gossip, money, work, etc.","examples":["Don't spread around that story!","What's the point of making the big bucks if you can't spread it around?","Don't spread it around.","You know, you should spread the load around."],"media":[]}]

name: take something on the chin
meanings: [{"name":"Lit. to absorb a blow on the chin","examples":["The boxer tried to duck but took the blow on the chin."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. accept criticism, financial loss, sports defeats, or unpleasant news bravely and without complaining","examples":["The bad news was a real shock, but John took it on the chin.","She took the criticism on the chin and used the feedback to improve her work.","When the company's stock plummeted, the employees had to take it on the chin and wait for recovery."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase originates from boxing slang in the early 20th century, where taking a punch to the chin without falling down symbolized toughness and endurance.  While it literally refers to receiving a physical blow, it is most commonly used metaphorically in personal, professional, or competitive contexts to describe handling setbacks like job loss, rejection, or harsh feedback with composure."]]]

name: crash into someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"bump or ram into someone or something accidentally or roughly; If a vehicle or a driver crashes into something, they hit it, especially in a way that damages the vehicle and hurts someone","examples":["The student crashed into the door when it opened suddenly.","The car crashed into a bus.","I know nothing about football. It's just boys crashing into one another.","I crashed into some tables.","Well, I was driving my car one night. I crashed into a utility pole."],"media":[]}]

name: pop by / pop over / pop in (for a visit)
meanings: [{"name":"come by [someone's residence / shop / place ] for a visit","examples":["I just popped by to grab a jacket.","We can pop in real quick.","We got to pop by the department store, pick up the mattress.","We're gonna pop over to the boat store real quick.","Jane: Did you know that a fish and chip shop just opened next door?\nKate: We'll have to pop over.","Jane: I just thought I'd pop by.\nKate: It's so good to see you. Come in.","We got plenty of burgers if you want to pop over.","Just do a quick pop in, say hello.","Hey, can you pop over to the house and see if Betty's there?"],"media":[]}]

name: It's probably time
meanings: [{"name":"used to suggest that the appropriate moment has arrived to perform a specific action or make a decision, often implying that the action is due or overdue","examples":["It's probably time to go, huh?","You think it's funny to call me Tommy, but I think it's probably time to give it a rest.","I think it's probably time for us to make our move."],"media":[]}]

name: as opposed to
meanings: [{"name":"instead of; rather than; used to refer to something that is different from what has just been mentioned","examples":["I guess it got sent to the billing address as opposed to the shipping address.","The car gets 30 miles per gallon, as opposed to last year's model, which got only 25.","They use fresh fish, as opposed to fish that has been frozen.","I'd say she is a good player, as opposed to a great one.","I'd prefer to go in May, as opposed to September.","The box is made of plastic, as opposed to wood.","People should be able to get out into nature and experience it, as opposed to glimpsing it from afar."],"media":[]}]

name: bring by
meanings: [{"name":"bring someone or something to a place for a short visit or delivery","examples":["Can you bring by the documents tomorrow?","I'll bring by the cake this evening.","Tom brought by coffees and his wife.","Can you bring the documents by my office on your way out?","Who are you talking about? name: weasel into
meanings: [{"name":"get into (a place or situation) by being dishonest, by persuading someone in a clever way, etc.","examples":["He managed to weasel his way into the restaurant even though he didn't have a reservation.","You're hanging around to try and weasel your way back into my life. Do not use these kids to do it.","He weasels his way into every area of my life."],"media":[]}]

name: rot out
meanings: [{"name":"decompose and fall out","examples":["If you don't clean your teeth regularly, they'll rot out!","A second popsicle? His teeth are gonna rot out of his head.","The water from the leaky sink rotted out the floorboards."],"media":[]}]

name: rotten to the core
meanings: [{"name":"(of a person) very bad or dishonest; really bad; corrupt","examples":["That lousy lady is rotten to the core.","The entire administration is rotten to the core.","The whole legal system is rotten to the core."],"media":[]}]

name: keep off
meanings: [{"name":"stop or prevent (someone or something) from being on (something); remain off something; stay off of something","examples":["Keep off the grass.","Please keep the dog off the sofa.","You had better keep off of my property."],"media":[]},{"name":"not talk about (something); prevent (someone) from talking about (something)","examples":["I think we'd better keep off the subject of the war.","We tried to keep them off (the subject of) the war."],"media":[]}]

name: keep the weight off / keep it off
meanings: [{"name":"continue to weigh a lower amount than one formerly weighed; not regain weight that one has lost","examples":["Give me a call mid-May, and keep the weight off.","Now i'm gonna get fat again. name: rife with something
meanings: [{"name":"full of something bad or unpleasant","examples":["Life is rife with questions that baffle.","The school was rife with rumors.","This government is rife with cronyism.","It seems to me that this whole area is rife with misinformation.","It turned out that the entire system was rife with corruption."],"media":[]}]

name: kick up a notch / crank it up a notch / step it up a notch
meanings: [{"name":"increase the intensity, effort, or excitement of a situation to take it to the next level","examples":["She just wants to kick it up a notch. ","I finally got my life back under control. I'm kicking it up a notch.","Let's kick things up a notch."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782493620/phrases/zfugpevy0embexhvhctd.mp4","publicId":"phrases/zfugpevy0embexhvhctd","type":"video"}]}]

name: be of help / be of any help / be of much help / be of some help
meanings: [{"name":"is a slightly more formal, polite idiom used to offer specific assistance or indicate usefulness in a particular situation.","examples":["I'm glad I could be of help. [=I'm glad I could help.]","We heard about your husband and wondered if we could be of any help.","I believe I can also be of some help in this area.","Maybe I could be of some help.","I can't say that I'm a big fan of mediterranean cuisine, so I may not be of much help.","Well, I'm sorry you couldn't be of more help too."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage - Offering Assistance",[" \"I can be of help with the research\" (polite offer) vs. \"I can help with the research\" (direct offer)."]],["Usage - Acknowledging Help",["\"Glad to be of help\" is a standard response to thanks, while \"Glad to help\" is also common but slightly less formal."]],["Usage - Negative Contexts",["Sorry we couldn't be of help\" (specific instance) vs. \"Sorry we weren't helpful\" (general attitude). "]]]

name: be much help / be any help
meanings:
[{"name":"used to describe the degree or extent of assistance, typically in negative or interrogative contexts to indicate limited or significant help","examples":["This tool won't be much help.","Jane: Was he any help to them?
Kate: No, he wasn't any help."," I'm not sure I'd be much help, Jane.","He's not gonna be a help to us.","He's not gonna be any help planning this wedding.","Jane: I'll wake you up early.
Kate: I don't mind getting up before dawn, if I can be any help.","Bob: I thought I could be some help.
Tom: Thanks, but I have it under control."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage",["\"Help\" is neutral and common in all registers. \"Be much help\" is often used to emphasize impact (positive or negative) and can sound overly formal in casual speech.","\"Of any help\", or \"of much help\" is used to ask if there was even a small bit of help provided where the expectation of the asker is there will be a negative answer.","\"Much help\" is usually used in the negative \"not much help\", if someone was \"much help\", \"he was much help\" it would usually be phrased \"he was very helpful\"."]]]

name: light sleeper
meanings: [{"name":"someone who wakes up easily","examples":["All right, now, keep it down because I'm a very light sleeper.","Jane: You want to come in?\nKate: Yeah. Come on. But just be careful. She's a very light sleeper.","We are light sleepers and are prone to night terrors, and several of us are very allergic to bed clothing."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Antonyms",["heavy sleeper","sound sleeper"]]]

name: will do / won't tomorrow do?
meanings:
[{"name":"used as an informal way of saying that one will be able to do something one is asked to do to","examples":["Bob: Can you ask them to come in tomorrow afternoon?
Jane: Will do.
","Jane: Keep me posted.
Kate: Will do.","Bob: Come over this weekend. I want to hear all about it.
Tom: Will do."],"media":[]},{"name":"provide what is needed; satisfy a need; sufficient; acceptable; adequate","examples":["I don't need any more cake, thank you. One piece will do (for me).","I'd prefer to use glue, but tape will do.","I know I promised to help with cleaning, Kate. But, won't tomorrow do?","Can we reschedule? Won't tomorrow do? (= Would tomorrow be an acceptable alternative?)","I can't finish this report today. Won't tomorrow do? (= Is it okay if I finish it tomorrow?)"],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage Context for question form",["The phrase \"won't tomorrow do?\" is a shortened, informal version of \"Will tomorrow do?\" which means \"Is tomorrow an acceptable time?\" or \"Would tomorrow be suitable?\" "]]]

name: one/two/etc down, one/two/etc to go
meanings: [{"name":"an expression that is used to mean that you have done or dealt with the first, second, etc. of a series of things and have yet to do or deal with the rest","examples":["Bob: How are your finals going?\nJane: Two down, three to go.","Well, one down and only a dozen to go.","One down, three to go."],"media":[]}]

name: play detective
meanings: [{"name":"act like a detective for fun, investigate, or try to solve a mystery or problem","examples":["What are you doing after school? Wanna come over and play detective?","She loves to play detective and figure out who took the cookies.","The kids decided to play detective and search for clues in the backyard.","Jane: We've to get busy looking for the thief. Now that we've finished playing housemaid.\nKate: We can continue playing detective."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage context",["It is commonly used when someone is trying to figure out what happened to something or who did something, without being a professional investigator."]]]

name: get sidetracked
meanings: [{"name":"become distracted from your original task, goal, or topic and start focusing on something else instead.","examples":["I was cleaning the kitchen, but I got sidetracked by a phone call. (= became distracted and stopped focusing on cleaning.)","We were discussing the budget, but the meeting got sidetracked by unrelated issues. (= The discussion drifted away from the main topic.)","I opened my laptop to work, then got sidetracked by social media. (= I got distracted from the work I intended to do.)"],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase comes from railroads.","A sidetrack (or siding) is a secondary railway track branching off from the main track. Trains can be moved onto a sidetrack to allow other trains to pass or for storage.","Because a train on a sidetrack is no longer traveling on its main route, the term developed a figurative meaning."]],["Related expressions",["Get distracted","Lose focus","Go off on a tangent"]]]

name: go off on a tangent / get off on a tangent
meanings: [{"name":"suddenly start talking or thinking about a completely new topic. When someone telling a story goes off on a tangent, it means the story doesn't stick to a topic.","examples":["I kind of got off on a tangent.","She went off on a tangent about what happened to her last summer.","Every time we discuss work, he goes off on a tangent about sports. (= He leaves the main topic and starts talking about sports.)","The professor went off on a tangent about ancient history during a chemistry lecture.","Sorry, I went off on a tangent. What was I saying? (= Sorry, I got distracted and strayed from the main point.)\n"],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase comes from geometry.","A tangent is a line that touches a curve or circle at exactly one point and then moves away from it without crossing it.","The \"curve\" represents the main conversation or train of thought. To \"go off on a tangent\" means to touch the main topic briefly and then shoot off in a straight, new direction that no longer follows the original curve. ","The word tangent comes from the Latin tangens, meaning \"touching.\" It was introduced into mathematics by the Danish mathematician Thomas Fincke","By the 19th century, it had become a common idiom in English to describe erratic behavior or speech that deviates from the expected course. "]]]

name: well on one's way
meanings: [{"name":"making excellent progress toward a specific goal, destination, or outcome. ","examples":["Bob: Hey, guys. Did you get Mike to write the check?\nTom: Dude, we're well on our way.","With his latest promotion, he is well on his way to becoming CEO.","After the surgery, the patient is well on his way to a full recovery.","An hour later, Bob is well on his way to the Ranch."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage Context",["Progress, Not Completion: It indicates the subject is past the beginning stages but has not yet finished. They are firmly on the path to success.","Certainty: The word \"well\" adds a tone of confidence; it suggests the progress is substantial enough that the final result is expected.","Flexibility: It can refer to physical travel (\"He is well on his way to London\") or metaphorical achievements (\"He is well on his way to becoming a doctor\")."]]]

name: baby someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"give someone a lot of care, attention, or help, as if they were a young child","examples":["The boys were now ten and twelve and didn't want their mother to baby them.","Jane: I'm not gonna relax until I see Bob.\nTom: Don't baby him, Jane. He's not the same boy as when he left.","Mother, I'm a big girl now. I do what I please. So don't baby me.","These teachers are babying students by grading too easily."],"media":[]},{"name":"treat something with a lot of care and attention","examples":["I wasn't babying my knee at all.","You do not need to baby a cast iron pan; if something is stuck to it, use a metal scratch pad to clean it.","The vintage car was in impressive condition and had clearly been babied."],"media":[]}]

name: there's more to it than that
meanings: [{"name":"The situation, explanation, or problem is more complex than it appears, or there are additional important details that haven't been mentioned","examples":["I've a sneaky suspicion there's more to it than that. But never mind.","Bob: I just needed a place to rest, that's all.\nJane: I think there's more to it than that.","Well, that may be true, but, there's more to it than that. (= It was one reason, but not the whole story.)","Jane: You just have to push buttons.\nKate: There's more to it than that.","I always assumed it was a business deal gone bad, but maybe there's more to it.","You can't just say it was bad luck. There's more to it than that; poor planning was the real cause."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage context",[" It suggests that the initial explanation is incomplete or superficial.","It signals that hidden details, underlying motives, or complicating circumstances exist beyond the obvious surface level."]]]

name: as good a [time/place/opportunity/reason] as any
meanings: [{"name":"It's often used when there is no clearly better choice available","examples":["I suppose this is as good a place as any to stay.","They do as good a job as anyone in town.","Mmm, too bad you're not as good a realtor as you are a baker.","Well, I guess now's as good a time as any to order dinner.","You're not as good a private eye as I thought.","I think Jane has as good a chance as anyone.","The park is crowded, but this bench is as good a place as any to sit and eat our lunch.","I wanted to call you anyway, so your birthday is as good a reason as any to catch up.","Since we are already in the city, this is as good an opportunity as any to visit the museum."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782985740/phrases/tfubxogkqrdnvi4lyhuv.mp4","publicId":"phrases/tfubxogkqrdnvi4lyhuv","type":"video"},{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782985753/phrases/kijzowonrufr0eohdreb.mp4","publicId":"phrases/kijzowonrufr0eohdreb","type":"video"}]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage context",["This phrase used to suggest that the current moment, location, or reason is just as suitable or acceptable as any other, implying there is no need to wait for a \"perfect\" or \"better\" option. "]],["Structure",["The phrase follows the pattern: as + adjective + a/an + noun + as + any.","Correct: \"as good a time as any\"","Incorrect: \"as good time as any\" (missing article) or \"as good a timing as any\" (wrong noun). "]]]

name: on one's mind
meanings:
[{"name":"occupying a person's thoughts; something they are thinking about a lot, worrying about, or concerned with","examples":["You seem distracted. Is something on your mind? (= Are you thinking about something or worried about something?)","I have a lot on my mind lately. (= I have many things to think about or worry about.)","The upcoming exam has been on my mind all week. (= I've been thinking about the exam a lot.)","Bob: What's on your mind, Tom?
Tom: Does something really have to be on my mind?","Jane: What gives?
Kate: Uh, nothing. Sorry. I just got a lot on my mind.","Bob: Can I talk to you, Tom?
Tom: What's on your mind, Bob?","Everything okay? I just thought there was something else on your mind. You seemed a little upset about the trip.","Something on your mind, Jane?","Jane: He's not sleeping well, and he says it's jet lag, but this long?
Kate: No, there's something on his mind."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Distinction: \"In one's mind\" vs. \"On one's mind\"",["On one's mind\t- Occupying one's thoughts, often repeatedly or as a concern. (e.g., The exam is on my mind. = I'm thinking about it a lot.)","In one's mind - Existing in one's thoughts, imagination, memory, or opinion. (e.g., In my mind, the exam will be easier than everyone expects. = That's my belief or mental impression.)"]],["Origin",["The phrase comes from the metaphor of the mind as a place where thoughts can rest or sit. If something is \"on your mind,\" it is figuratively sitting there, occupying your attention."]]]

name: the last thing on one's mind
meanings: [{"name":"Something that a person is not thinking about at all, or is very unlikely to consider because other things are much more important or urgent.","examples":["Marriage is the last thing on his mind right now. (= He is not considering marriage at the moment.)","Bob: Are you thinking about buying a new car?\nTom: With all these medical bills, that's the last thing on my mind.\"","The exam is the last thing on my mind. (= I'm not thinking about it; something else is occupying my attention.)","When the storm hit, vacation plans were the last thing on their minds. (= They were focused on the storm, not vacations.)","With the exam tomorrow, going to the movies is the last thing on my mind.\" (I am not thinking about movies at all)."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Similar expressions",["Not even thinking about it","Not a priority"]]]

name: trot along
meanings: [{"name":"move at a steady, brisk pace that is faster than a walk but slower than a run; step along in a lively fashion; ","examples":["The horses trotted along in time with the music.","We trotted along the beach to stay warm in the breeze.","Well, trot along with Tina."],"media":[]}]

name: zip down
meanings: [{"name":"travel very quickly to a location; move very fast","examples":["She zipped down the stairs. (= She went down the stairs quickly.)","Well, I was thinking we should, zip down to the police station and file an official report.","Forget the whole thing. We can zip down to coffee shop and wallow in a hot chocolate.","I need to zip down to the grocery store before it closes.","The skier zipped down the slope with incredible speed."],"media":[]}]

name: owe it to oneself
meanings: [{"name":"deserve (to do something enjoyable); deserve and need to do something that will be good for you","examples":["Take a few days off work - you owe it to yourself.","You owe it to yourself to have some fun.","She owe it to herself to pursue her dreams and change careers.","You owe it to yourself to walk away from a toxic environment."],"media":[]}]

name: owe it all to someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"express complete gratitude or give total credit to someone or something for someone's success, achievement, good fortune, or positive outcome","examples":["I won the championship, but I owe it all to my coach's relentless training.","She owed it all to our nail polish.","My dad survived the accident. I owe it all to the paramedics who arrived so quickly.","I'm a better person today; I owe it all to my father's wisdom.","I owe it all to my parents. (= My parents are the reason for my success.)","He owes it all to years of hard work. (= His success comes from years of effort.)","Jane: How did you become such a good musician?\nKate: Honestly, I owe it all to my first music teacher."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Similar expressions",["\"I owe my success to...\"","\"It's all thanks to...\"","\"I give all the credit to...\""]]]

name: it's all thanks to someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"used to attribute a positive outcome, success, or situation entirely to a specific person, thing, or cause.","examples":["The video call was crystal clear. It's all thanks to the new high-speed fiber network.","Jane: Well, they're finally gonna break ground on Tuesday and it's all thanks to you.\nKate: Glad I could help.","All thanks to your help.","I'm feeling much better now. It's all thanks to a good night's sleep.","We finished the project on time; it's all thanks to the team's hard work.","The garden is blooming beautifully this year. It's all thanks to the extra rain we had in April."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782902824/phrases/rkjxsut7xuyzv1tklvrc.mp4","publicId":"phrases/rkjxsut7xuyzv1tklvrc","type":"video"}]}]

name: think something out / think out something / think it out
meanings: [{"name":"think through something; prepare a plan or scheme","examples":["This is an interesting problem. I'll have to take some time and think it out.","We spent all morning thinking out our plan.","Maybe i should think it out."],"media":[]}]

name: Glad I could help
meanings:
[{"name":"I'm happy that I was able to help you","examples":["Bob: Thank you for explaining that problem.
Tom: Glad I could help.","Jane: Thanks for giving me a ride.
Kate: Glad I could help.","Bob: Thanks for being here.
Kate: Oh, I'm glad i could be."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Similar expressions",["\"Happy to help.\"","\"You're welcome.\"","It was my pleasure.\"","\"My pleasure.\""]],["\"Glad I could help\" vs \"I'm glad I could be of service\"",["\"Glad I could help\": Neutral to casual. Suitable for friends, colleagues, and most everyday interactions.","\"I'm glad I could be of service\": High formality.  It uses the noun \"service\" instead of the verb \"help,\" creating a tone of professional duty, deference, or official capacity. "]]]

name: nothing in it (for someone)
meanings: [{"name":"nothing to be gained (by someone)","examples":["Why should they help? There's nothing in it for them.","He's buddies with a dealer I'm tracking. There's no bounty on him, nothing in it for me. Nothing but the joy of giving."],"media":[]}]

name: be in it for
meanings: [{"name":"be involved in something because of a particular motive, benefit, or goal","examples":["Many politicians claim to care about the people, but they are really just in it for the power.","He's just in it for himself.","He's not in it for the money. He's in it for the ego.","Bob: What's in it for me?\nTom: I'll buy you a cool drink.","I'm in it for the lifestyle ","She's not in it for the free meals. She's in it for keeps.","I'm letting you stay here for free, there has to be something in it for me."],"media":[]}]

name: fair's fair / fair is fair
meanings: [{"name":"something that you say when you want someone to behave reasonably or treat you the same as other people; used to say that something was done or should be done because it is fair","examples":["Fair's fair: I washed the dishes yesterday, so it's your turn to do them today.","Come on, it's my turn. Fair's fair!","All right Jane. I brought your doll back. Now let my puppy out, Ok? Fair's fair.","I paid for dinner last time, so fair's fair—you're buying tonight.","You helped me move my sofa, so fair's fair that I help you paint your house.","Come on, fair's fair!  I watched the kids all morning; it's your turn now."],"media":[]}]

name: in the short run / in the short term
meanings: [{"name":"for a short period of time; immediate or near future","examples":["In the short run, you can get lucky sometimes.","It won't make any difference in the short run.","These changes may improve profits in the short run, but they are going to cost us money in the long run.","We got to make some money in the short term."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Short Run vs. Long Run",["In the short run → soon, temporarily, over a short period.","In the long run → eventually, over an extended period."]]]

name: the short end of the stick
meanings: [{"name":"unfair or unfavorable treatment; If someone gets the short end of the stick, they receive worse treatment, fewer benefits, or a worse deal than other people.","examples":["She got the short end of the stick in the deal.","Everyone else got a bonus, but I didn't. I got the short end of the stick.","While the executives kept their jobs, many junior employees got the short end of the stick and were laid off."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The idiom likely comes from the old practice of drawing sticks or straws to make a random choice. The person who drew the shortest stick would lose, be chosen for an unpleasant task, or receive the less desirable outcome."]],["Similar expressions",["Draw the short straw → be selected for an unpleasant duty by chance.","Get a raw deal → be treated unfairly.","Get the worse end of the bargain → receive less benefit than the other party.","Be at a disadvantage → be in a weaker position."]]]

name: draw the short straw / get the short straw
meanings: [{"name":"have to do the least enjoyable of a range of duties, often because you have been chosen to do it","examples":["Mike drew the short straw and had to clean the bathroom.","Looks like someone got the short straw.","I drew the short straw and had to work on Christmas Day.","Someone had to clean the garage, and I drew the short straw."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782554700/phrases/kpnp7xcgdu9h8grgiyni.mp4","publicId":"phrases/kpnp7xcgdu9h8grgiyni","type":"video"},{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782554716/phrases/dj9hr7n4p0rxryavlrii.mp4","publicId":"phrases/dj9hr7n4p0rxryavlrii","type":"video"}]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase comes from an old method of making a random choice:","Several straws (or sticks) of different lengths were held together.","Each person drew one.","The person who drew the shortest straw was the \"loser\" and had to perform the unpleasant duty."]]]

name: What's got you/him/her
meanings: [{"name":"what is causing( or making) a particular feeling, behavior, or situation. Here, \"got\" means something like \"caused\", \"made\", or \"put you in that state.\"","examples":["You've been quiet all day. What's got you down? (= Why are you feeling sad?)","What's got you laughing so hard? (= What is making you laugh?)","Bob, I don't understand what's got you so busy."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage context",["The phrase \"what's got you\" is an informal expression that generally asks about someone's current state of mind, emotional condition, or the reason for their behavior or hesitation.","The grammatically correct form would be \"What has gotten you?\"  But is common in casual speech."]],["Common patterns",["\"What's got you smiling?\" → What is making you smile?","\"What's got you so excited?\" → What is making you excited?","\"What's got you worried?\" → What is causing you to feel worried?","\"What's got you thinking?\" → What are you thinking about?"]]]

name: What do you care?
meanings:
[{"name":"Why does it matter to you?; It's none of your business; is a rhetorical question used to express indifference, annoyance, or to tell someone that a matter is none of their business. When someone says "What do you care?", they think another person's concern is unnecessary, irrelevant, or surprising.","examples":["Bob: Why are you talking to him?
Tom: What do you care? We're just friends. ","Jane: How much did that car cost?
Kate: What do you care? It's my money.","Jane: I think your team name looks stupid.
Kate: What do you care? You don't want to be in our group any way."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Usage context",["The phrase is generally considered rude and aggressive.  It is rarely used in polite conversation."]],["Similar expressions",["Why do you care? (more direct and common)","Why does it matter to you?","What's it to you? (more confrontational)"]]]

name: I'm through / I'm through with
meanings: [{"name":"I am finished.; I am done; I'm finished with an activity","examples":["I'm through with my homework. (= I've finished my homework.)","Are you through using the phone? (= Have you finished using it?)"],"media":[]},{"name":"I'm ending a relationship or association with someone or something","examples":["I quit! I'm through with this job. (= I will not work here anymore.)","We argued all night. We're through. (= Our relationship is over.)","He's eighteen, he can do whatever the hell he wants. He's on his own, I'm through."],"media":[]},{"name":"fed up or refusing to continue; used to declare that you are finished with something, often with a tone of finality, relief, or anger. ","examples":["I'm through with your lies. (= I will no longer accept or listen to your lies.)","After all the delays, I'm through waiting. (= I refuse to wait any longer.)","Kid: I'm through. This stuff was awful. I want to go watch TV.\nMom: It's impolite to leave the table in the middle of a meal.","I'm through arguing about this.","I'm through talking about this.","I'm through running your errands.","Jane: Can you help me with this word?\nKate. I'm not telling you. I'm through helping you with words, you hear me? You'll have to figure it out by yourself."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["\"I'm through\" vs \"I'm done\"",["n modern English, \"I'm done\" is more common.","I'm through. → Slightly older-fashioned or more emphatic.","I'm done. → Very common and natural."]]]

name: lying in wait
meanings: [{"name":"hiding and ready to attack; hiding secretly and waiting patiently for a specific person or opportunity, usually with the intent to ambush, attack, or surprise.","examples":["The gunmen were lying in wait when Mr Smith came out of the hotel.","I knew that he was there, just lying in wait.","The tiger was lying in wait in the tall grass for its prey.","Police officers were lying in wait behind the warehouse to catch the smugglers."],"media":[]},{"name":"Fig. a problem, danger, or opportunity that exists unseen until it manifests or is discovered.","examples":["Financial troubles may be lying in wait for those who overspend.","The opposition party is quietly lying in wait for the President to make a mistake."],"media":[]}]

name: hop to it
meanings: [{"name":"act or move quickly; Get started right now!","examples":["The car was ready to leave and he was told to hop to it.","Go for it, buddy. Hop to it.","Go make me a sandwich. Come on, hop to it.","“Hurry up! Hop to it!” urged Bill. “We've got to get this done!”","Bill: I have to get these things stacked up before I go home. \nBob: Then hop to it! You won't get it done standing around here talking.","Mom: Bob, will you take this to the grabage bag in the garage please? Bob: The garage?, are you mad?\nMom: I'll be if you don't hop to it."],"media":[]}]

name: come after someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"chase someone or something; try to find or capture (someone you want to hurt or punish)","examples":["They're worried that the government might be coming after them.","You're safe now. Nobody's coming after you here.","Well, you can relax. Jane won't be coming after you.","I am not coming after your money."],"media":[]}]

name: around back
meanings: [{"name":"at the back of a building, house, store, or other place, often referring to an entrance, area, or location behind the front side.","examples":["The delivery entrance is around back. (= The entrance is located at the rear of the building.)","You can park around back. (= You can park in the area behind the building.)","The servants' entrance is around back.","I told him to pull the car around back so nobody would see us.","All right, I'm gonna go around back, see if I can climb in a window.","Jane: Bob! Kate's not in her room. I'll go look around the yard.\nBob: I'll check around back.","If the front door is locked, come around back and use the side entrance."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["\"around back\" vs \"out back\"",["\"The garden is around back.\" (behind the house)","\"The garden is out back.\" (same meaning, more informal) - Out back (very common in American English)."]]]

name: get cleaned up
meanings: [{"name":"become clean, neat, or presentable; make oneself clean and tidy, usually by washing, grooming, changing clothes, or improving one's appearance","examples":["I need to get cleaned up before the guests arrive. (= I need to wash up and make myself presentable.)","After working in the garden, she got cleaned up and went out for dinner. (= She washed and changed into clean clothes.)","The city got cleaned up before the festival. (= The city was made cleaner and tidier.)","You have mud on your shirt; go inside and get cleaned up before dinner.","I need 20 minutes to get cleaned up after the yoga."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Similar expressions",["freshen up"]],["\"clean Up\" vs \"get cleaned up\"",["I cleaned up the kitchen. (I did the work). It focuses on the action performed by the subject.","I got cleaned up. (I am now clean, regardless of how much effort it took or if I used a service). It focuses on the outcome or the process of becoming clean."]]]

name: that gives me something
meanings: [{"name":"that provides a useful starting point or piece of information; That provides me with something; That causes me to feel something; I have the specific feeling, item, or idea now.","examples":["Seeing you smile gives me hope.(Causes the feeling of hope).","This loud noise gives me a headache. (Causes physical pain).","Your honesty gives me confidence. (Instills a specific trait).","Okay, Bob and Tom are coming over for dinner tonight. That gives me nine hours to teach you to be courteous, gracious, and well-mannered"],"media":[]}]

name: stroll down
meanings: [{"name":"walk somewhere in a slow, relaxed, and leisurely manner, typically implying movement along a specific path (like a street, road, or hallway) or toward a destination.","examples":["Let's stroll down the road to the shop.\" (Focus: The road as a path to the shop).","We decided to stroll down Main Street to look at the holiday lights.","Let's stroll down the sidewalk."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["\"stroll along\" vs \"stroll down\"",["In \"stroll along\",  the preposition \"along\" focuses on the parallel movement beside a long feature (beach, river) or the duration of the walk.","In \"stroll down\", the preposition \"down\" emphasizes the direction of travel or the linear nature of the path (e.g., a street) rather than just the act of walking beside something."]]]

name: take a joke
meanings: [{"name":"laugh at a joke that is about oneself; laugh when someone says something funny about you and not be offended; accept ridicule good-naturedly","examples":["Better not tease Kate. She can't take a joke.","I wasn't being serious. Can't you take a joke?","God. Learn to take a joke."],"media":[]}]

name: grow to do something
meanings: [{"name":"gradually start to do something; gradually begin to do certain things, using verbs such as feel, know, like, need, respect, sense, suspect, think, want, wonder, etc.","examples":["I grew to hate Bob over a period of years.","As I grew to know Jane, I began to like her.","I'll eventually really grow to like it.","Jane: I don't want a doll. This is yours take it.\nKate: Oh, you will grow to like her, Jane.","I've grown to like her over the months.","I didn't like the city at first, but I've grown to love it. (The love developed slowly).","Over the years, he grew to understand his father's decisions.","She grew to rely on her assistant for everything."],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["\"Grow to\" vs. \"Start to\"",["\"Start to\" implies a specific beginning point, whereas \"grow to\" implies a process.","He started to like her (a specific moment).","He grew to like her (a slow development over time). "]],["\"Grow to\" vs. \"Grow into\"",[" \"Grow into\" usually takes a noun (e.g., \"grow into a role\")","\"grow to\" takes a verb (e.g., \"grow to accept the role\")."]]]

name: Wouldn't you like to know?
meanings:
[{"name":"is an idiomatic response meaning: You want to know the answer, but I'm not going to tell you.","examples":["Bob: What were you doing there?
Tom: Wouldn't you like to know.","Jane: How much did you pay for that car?
Kate: Wouldn't you like to know?","Jane: Who told you that?
Bob: Wouldn't you like to know? (= Bob doesn't want to reveal the source.)","Jane: Who'd (= Who did) you vote for?
Kate: Wouldn't you like to know! (Meaning: I'm not telling you). ","Bob: Hey. Where you going?
Tom: Wouldn't you like to know? Bob: I would. I would like to know!"],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Similar expressions",["I'm not telling.","That's a secret.","Nice try."]],["Usage context",["The phrase \"wouldn't you like to know\" is a rhetorical question used to refuse to answer a question while acknowledging the questioner's curiosity.","In most modern contexts, it is a sarcastic or firm way of saying, \"I know the answer, you want to know, but I am not going to tell you.\""]]]

name: you don't want to know
meanings:
[{"name":"used to say that someone would be shocked or upset to learn the answer to a question","examples":["Bob: What is she doing?
Tom: Believe me, you don't want to know.","Jane: What you up to?
Kate: Trust me, you don't want to know.","Bob: It's my wedding day. where are you going?
Jane:  Bob, you don't want to know. But it's absolutely, absolutely important. I promise.","Jane: How backed up are we?
Kate: Oh, you don't want to know.","Jane: Bob been any help?
Kate: You don't want to know."],"media":[]}]

name: Good gravy!
meanings: [{"name":"is an informal exclamation used to express surprise, amazement, disbelief, frustration, or annoyance.","examples":["Bob: I just won two free tickets to the concert!\nTom: Good gravy! That's awesome! (Here, \"Good gravy!\" simply means \"Wow!\")","Good gravy, what a mess! (Frustration or disbelief.)","Good gravy. What's going on?","Good gravy, whose side are you on? (Frustration )"],"media":[]}]
extraDetails: [["Origin",["The phrase is a euphemistic exclamation—a mild substitute for stronger religious expressions such as \"Good God!\" or \"Good Lord!\"","In English, people have long invented harmless words to avoid using sacred names in exclamations. Examples include: good heavens/grief/gracious","\"Good gravy!\" appears to have emerged in American English in the 20th century as a humorous, family-friendly expression.","The word gravy was chosen mainly because it sounds amusing and fits the pattern of other \"good + word\" exclamations, not because it has any connection to the food itself."]],["Similar expressions",["Good grief!","Wow!","That's surprising!"]]]

name: aim for something / aim at something
meanings: [{"name":"work towards (a goal); plan, hope, or intend to achieve something","examples":["The boys were aiming for a tree and just shot a little high.","If I'd been aiming for Bob, he'd be dead.","Aim for the head, not the legs.","Bob: You punched my face.\nTom: It was an accident! I was aiming for your arm.","We all aim for happiness but sometimes it's easier said than done.","Our company is aiming for an increase in turnover this year of 50%.","Kate: Jane, I'm starting to get tired of all the negativity aimed at Bob.\nJane: You need to let it go. I mean it."],"media":[]}]

name: allow for someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"plan on having enough of something (such as food, space, etc.) for someone.","examples":["Mary is bringing Bill on the picnic, so be sure to allow for him when buying the food.","Allow for an extra person when setting the table tonight. "],"media":[]},{"name":"plan on the possibility of something; think about or plan for (something that will or might happen in the future); consider something when one makes a calculation; consider additional, unforeseen factors","examples":["When purchasing property, the company should allow for possible future growth/expansion.","The total distance, allowing for detours, is about 10 miles.","If you allow for inflation, he's actually earning less money now than he was 10 years ago.","Allow for a few rainy days on your vacation.","You need to allow for traffic jams when traveling in rush hour.","When planning one must allow for delays due to unforeseen circumstances."],"media":[]},{"name":"make something possible","examples":["The design of the system allows for easy upgrades.","Bob says rectangular tables will allow for more people to attend."],"media":[]}]

name: apply for something / apply to someone or something / apply to someone or something for something
meanings: [{"name":"ask for something from someone or an organization; offer one's services for (a job, a vacancy…)","examples":["I want to apply for a credit card.","Don't apply for that job if you are not qualified.","I applied to seven colleges for admission."],"media":[]}]

name: ask for it / ask for something bad or dire
meanings: [{"name":"behave in a way that invites punishment or retribution; act badly, such that one will bring on bad consequences","examples":["If you keep misbehaving, you'll be asking for punishment.","You're really asking for it!"],"media":[]}]

name: beat down someone or something
meanings: [{"name":" defeat or demoralize someone","examples":["The constant bombing finally beat them down.","The attackers beat down the defenders."],"media":[]},{"name":"persuade someone to accept a lower amount of money for something; persuade a person or organization to accept a lower amount of money for something that they are selling","examples":["He wanted $75 for the bike, but I managed to beat him down to $50.","They tried to beat us down on the price, but we remained firm.","When you go to a supermarket you can't usually beat down the price of items."],"media":[]}]

name: soccer mom
meanings: [{"name":"a mother who spends a lot of time taking her children to after-school activities such as sports, swimming, or dance, etc. It is often used to refer to a type of middle-class mother.","examples":["You don't know these soccer moms like I do.","You know, I am not some shallow soccer mom. I have done things that you can't believe."],"media":[]}]

name: me, myself, and I
meanings: [{"name":"myself alone, without the help or companionship of others.; Just me; only myself.","examples":["Who paid for my education? Me, myself, and I!","I traveled through Europe alone, just me, myself, and I.","I moved all the furniture by me, myself, and I. (= I did it completely on my own.)","It was just me, myself, and I at home all weekend. (= I was alone.)","I started the business with me, myself, and I—no partners, no investors. extraDetails: [["Usage Context",["It most commonly describes doing something alone (e.g., \"I went on vacation with just me, myself, and I\").","It can indicate independence, suggesting one needs no one else (e.g., \"When it comes to my career, it's just me, myself, and I\").","In a negative context, it may describe someone who is self-centered or egotistical."]],["Why three words?",["In standard grammar, me, myself, and I all refer to the same person.","Using all three together is mainly for emphasis, rhythm, and style rather than grammatical necessity.","This idiom combines the three first-person singular pronouns—me (objective), myself (reflexive/intensive), and I (subjective)—to create a rhetorical triplet. "]]]

name: place to lay one's head
meanings: [{"name":"home or living place","examples":["He doesn't have a place to lay his head.","I have found a new place to lay my head."],"media":[]}]

name: spring cleaning / spring-cleaning / spring-clean

name: gather up someone or something
meanings: [{"name":"collect things that are scattered; collect, bring together, or pick up things (or sometimes people) into one place","examples":["Let's gather our things up and go.","Please gather up your things.","Okay, boys and girls, gather up your supplies and put them away.","I have to go gather up Bob's clothes.","I'll gather up some of your stuff.","Please gather up your toys before dinner.","She gathered up the papers from the floor."],"media":[{"url":"https://res.cloudinary.com/sriniavoz/video/upload/v1782552331/phrases/dnhqda0ulw7vkyvznivy.mp4","publicId":"phrases/dnhqda0ulw7vkyvznivy","type":"video"}]},{"name":"bring people together; assembling a group of people or animals from different locations","examples":["The teacher gathered up the students for an announcement.","We gathered up the team before the meeting.","The teacher told the students to gather up on the playground for the fire drill.","Everyone!
